{"assumptions":["α irrational (for the rational case the expansion terminates)","regular (simple) continued fraction with integer partial quotients a_k ≥ 1 for k ≥ 1","||t|| denotes the distance from t to the nearest integer"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492004+00:00","domain":"Diophantine approximation, circle rotations, continued fractions","id":"claim_7271e0510379bbe55262f0b504298ebded2c36c4dd6bb321ac077750203941b8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let α be irrational with regular continued fraction [a_0; a_1, a_2, ...], convergents p_n/q_n (p_{-1} = 1, q_{-1} = 0, p_0 = a_0, q_0 = 1, p_{n+1} = a_{n+1}p_n + p_{n-1}, q_{n+1} = a_{n+1}q_n + q_{n-1}) and complete quotients α_{n+1} = [a_{n+1}; a_{n+2}, ...], so a_{n+1} < α_{n+1} < a_{n+1} + 1. Write ||t|| = dist(t, Z) and δ_n = |q_n α − p_n| (so δ_{-1} = 1).

(1) Exact size and alternating sign. For all n ≥ 0, q_n α − p_n = (−1)^n / (q_n α_{n+1} + q_{n-1}). Hence 1/(q_n + q_{n+1}) < δ_n < 1/q_{n+1}, the errors alternate in sign, δ_n is strictly decreasing, and δ_n = ||q_n α|| for every n ≥ 1 (because q_{n+1} ≥ 2 gives δ_n < 1/2); for n = 0 this holds when a_1 ≥ 2.

(2) The distances obey the same recursion as the denominators: δ_{n-1} = a_{n+1} δ_n + δ_{n+1} for all n ≥ 0. Equivalently δ_n = 1/(α_1 α_2 ··· α_{n+1}).

(3) Closest returns (Lagrange's theorem on best approximations of the second kind). For every n ≥ 0 and every integer q with 1 ≤ q < q_{n+1}: ||q α|| ≥ δ_n, with equality if and only if q = q_n. In dynamical words: for the rotation t ↦ t + α (mod 1), among all times 1 ≤ q < q_{n+1} the orbit of any point comes closest to its starting point exactly at time q_n; the record-breaking (closest-return) times of the orbit are precisely the denominators q_0 (when a_1 ≥ 2), q_1, q_2, ..., and successive closest returns land on alternate sides of the starting point, at distances δ_n.

(4) Growth. q_{n+1} ≥ q_n + q_{n-1}, hence q_n ≥ F_{n+1} (Fibonacci) and q_n ≥ 2^{(n−1)/2} for n ≥ 1; the golden ratio (all a_k = 1) is the slowest case.

Where it fails. For rational α the expansion terminates, the last δ is 0 and the recursion (2) stops. Statement (3) is about ||qα|| = min_p |qα − p| (best approximations of the SECOND kind). For the FIRST-kind problem of minimising |α − p/q| over q ≤ Q, intermediate fractions (p_{n-1} + k p_n)/(q_{n-1} + k q_n) with k > a_{n+1}/2 can also be best approximations, so the two notions must not be conflated. When a_1 = 1 one has q_0 = q_1 = 1, the n = 0 case of (3) is vacuous, and ||α|| equals δ_1, not δ_0.","status":"unverified"}

from \(S_0=0\), and let \(\Xi\) be an independent lifetime with tail \(G\).
Define
\[
  D^*:=\max_{0\le k\le \Xi}|S_k|.
\]
Let
\[
  \tau_n:=\inf\{m\ge1: |S_m|=n\},
  \qquad n\ge1,
\]
with the convention \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\). Then
\[
  \Pbb(D^*\ge n)=\E[G(\tau_n)].
\]
If
\[
  D^\to:=\max_{0\le k\le\Xi}S_k,
  \qquad
  \tau_n^+:=\inf\{m\ge1:S_m=n\},
\]
then
\[
  \Pbb(D^\to\ge n)=\E[G(\tau_n^+)].
\]
Analogously, if
\[
  D^\leftarrow:=\max_{0\le k\le\Xi}(-S_k),
  \qquad
  \tau_n^-:=\inf\{m\ge1:S_m=-n\},
\]
then
\[
  \Pbb(D^\leftarrow\ge n)=\E[G(\tau_n^-)].
\]
In the last two identities, we again use the convention \(G(\infty)=0\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X is a compact topological space","T: X → X is a map (continuity needed only for the orbit-closure supplement and T(M) = M)","A ⊂ X is nonempty, closed, and T(A) ⊆ A","Zorn's lemma (axiom of choice) is available"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:57:26.111086+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, minimal sets","id":"claim_72825b37190726c07a48638d2ab2de6ae848c0f1fc5cf24098ec659b459ef7be","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a compact topological space and T: X → X a map. Then every nonempty closed set A ⊂ X with T(A) ⊆ A contains a minimal set: a nonempty closed set M ⊆ A with T(M) ⊆ M that has no proper nonempty closed T-invariant subset. In particular (A = X) every compact dynamical system has at least one minimal set. If moreover X is Hausdorff and T is continuous, then M = cl{Tⁿx : n ≥ 0} for every x ∈ M, T(M) = M, and (X metrizable) M carries a T-invariant Borel probability measure by the Krylov–Bogolyubov theorem, so every compact metrizable system has an invariant probability measure supported on a minimal set. The same statement and proof hold for a commuting family (or any semigroup) of maps X → X, with 'invariant' meaning invariant under every map of the family, and for flows. Sharp edges. (1) Compactness cannot be dropped: for the translation T(x) = x + 1 on ℝ, any nonempty closed invariant set A contains, for some a ∈ A, the closed invariant set {a + n : n ≥ 0}, which has the proper closed invariant subset {a + n : n ≥ 1}; so ℝ has NO minimal set, although it has plenty of nonempty closed invariant sets. (2) Existence uses only compactness and Zorn's lemma (the intersection of a chain of nonempty closed sets in a compact space is nonempty by the finite intersection property); continuity of T is needed only for the orbit-closure description and for T(M) = M. (3) Minimal sets need not be unique: the identity map has every single point as a minimal set; a system with a fixed point and a dense orbit (e.g. the doubling map) has minimal sets that are not the whole space. (4) 'Minimal' is with respect to inclusion among closed invariant sets; a nonempty invariant set that is not closed (a single dense orbit) is not a minimal set.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["nonempty compact X subset R^d; d,p>=1; n>=0 integer; eps,s>0; B,R>=0","continuous symmetric PSD kernel, rank <=p, k(x,x)<=R^2, zero-mean GP","independent N(0,s) observation noise; new noisy predictive observation","an admissible r>0 with Omega(r)<=eta/(2sqrt(p)), and a fixed h-net G subset X, are specified or bounded from a known modulus and covering bound","normalized bidirectional residual ReLU attention plus residual ReLU tokenwise MLPs; arbitrary real weights; raw coordinates and role flags"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:45:13.561071+00:00","domain":"Gaussian-process prediction; transformer approximation","id":"claim_7287d4292b2f0eb19800316b0df51e29ade681fed86b320517d42dc0df5e0416","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"CURRENT AUDIT STATUS: independently checked proof, T336-w727-C005 v2; urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28 PASS in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv. Exact proof SHA256 22df67c6b2aaec99499aac6bf3440e8d5d6305204deedcc98fe9b4a621583b40. No novelty or Lean certification is claimed. The following original submission text retains historical pre-audit status notices.

Every continuous real symmetric PSD kernel of rank <=p and diagonal <=R^2 on a nonempty compact X subset R^d admits an explicit raw-input normalized-ReLU-attention transformer for uniform noisy predictive forward KL <=eps, with positive noise s, labels bounded by B, and contexts <=n. The complete width/depth/MLP/head bound is given in C005 Section 1 in terms of the canonical kernel modulus Omega(r), a finite h-net cardinality J, and the solver constants. A fixed finite Gram factorization supplies all encoder feature values; no feature computation is hidden outside the count. Status: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C005 v2. Complete theorem, constants and scope:
# Target 1 for continuous finite-rank kernels on compact raw domains

Claim T336-w727-C005 v2. Status: proof (unaudited), dependent on C002 v1 and the deterministic perturbation/encoder constructions in C004 v1. The entire result is not Lean-checked. No independent review or novelty certification is claimed.

The hardest step is removing the supplied-feature oracle without adding a hidden feature-computation cost. A finite Gram factorization fixes the encoder weights; a kernel modulus controls its error. The size explicitly includes the resulting encoder.

## 1. Statement and all parameters

Let X be a nonempty compact subset of R^d, d>=1. Let k:X times X -> R be a continuous real symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel of rank at most p, p>=1, with k(x,x)<=R^2 for R>=0. The prior is the zero-mean GP with kernel k. Observation noise is independent N(0,s), s>0. Labels are bounded by B>=0, contexts have length <=n with n>=0 an integer, and eps>0. The prediction concerns a new noisy observation.

Define the canonical kernel modulus in the ambient L1 metric by

    Omega(r)=sup_{x,y in X, ||x-y||_1<=r}
                sqrt(k(x,x)+k(y,y)-2k(x,y)).

The expression is nonnegative by positive semidefiniteness. Omega(r) tends to zero as r decreases to zero, as proved below.

Retain the following explicit constants from C004's deterministic perturbation bound:

    S=R+1, C_A=n(2R+1),
    C_m=nB[(R+S)/s+S C_A R/s^2],
    C_v=R+S+S^2 C_A/s>0,
    eta=min(1,sqrt(s eps)/(2(1+C_m)),s sqrt(eps)/(2C_v),s/(4C_v)),
    eps0=min(eps/4,1/16), e=eta/sqrt(p)>0.

Choose any **fixed admissible** r>0 with Omega(r)<=e/2. An explicit upper modulus for k can be used to choose r; continuity guarantees existence, not an algorithm for computing a modulus of an arbitrary black-box kernel. Put

    A_cone=(2R+e)/r>0, h=e/(2A_cone)>0.

Choose a finite h-net G contained in X, of cardinality J>=1. The size bound is explicit in J (or in a known upper bound for the covering number). For X=[0,1]^d one may take the regular grid with

    m=max(1,ceil(d A_cone/e)), J=(m+1)^d.

For the attention solver define

    kappa=1+max(1,n)S^2/s, M=nS^2B/s,
    delta0=min(1/2,s/(2S^2),sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/S^2),
    T=ceil(sqrt(kappa) log(2/delta0)/2).

There is a transformer, using normalized residual ReLU attention and tokenwise residual ReLU MLPs, with

    D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ,
    H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1,
    L_total=T+5+ceil(log_2 J),
    at most five attention heads per layer,
    at most L_total(15D^2+2DH)+2D dense scalar parameters,

whose positive-variance Gaussian output has forward KL<=eps from the exact noisy GP predictive, uniformly over all admissible raw-input contexts and queries. Its input contains only raw coordinates, labels, fixed context/query flags, and constants. The encoder is counted. These are arbitrary-real-weight size bounds; no finite-bit, kernel-evaluation, offline factorization-time, SGD, or ERM-generalization bound is asserted.

## 2. Canonical finite-dimensional features and the kernel modulus

Form the vector space of finite formal combinations of symbols delta_x with bilinear form

    <sum_i a_i delta_{x_i},sum_j b_j delta_{y_j}>
       =sum_{i,j}a_i b_j k(x_i,y_j).

Positive semidefiniteness makes this a nonnegative quadratic form. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality follows by applying nonnegativity to u+t v for all real t; in particular a zero-norm vector is orthogonal to every vector. Quotient by the zero-norm subspace. For any finite list of symbols, the dimension of their quotient span is the rank of their Gram matrix. Every finite list of quotient vectors is contained in the span of finitely many symbols. Thus the dimension of the resulting inner-product space is the supremum of these Gram ranks, which is the kernel rank and is at most p. It is finite dimensional, so no completion issue remains.

Choose an orthonormal basis and pad with zeros in R^p. The coordinates z(x) of delta_x then satisfy

    k(x,y)=z(x)^T z(y), ||z(x)||<=R,
    ||z(x)-z(y)||^2=k(x,x)+k(y,y)-2k(x,y).

Thus z is continuous and ||z(x)-z(y)||<=Omega(r) whenever ||x-y||_1<=r. To justify Omega(r)->0 directly, suppose the contrary. There are sequences r_j->0 and x_j,y_j in X at distance <=r_j with feature distance bounded away from zero. Compactness supplies a subsequence x_j->x; then y_j->x as well. Continuity of k makes the squared feature distance tend to k(x,x)+k(x,x)-2k(x,x)=0, a contradiction. The supremum is finite because the kernel is continuous on the compact product. In particular every fixed positive e admits the required r.

The factorization at the finite net does not require evaluating any feature map on runtime inputs. Form the fixed J-by-J Gram matrix K_G=(k(a,b))_{a,b in G}. It is PSD of rank <=p, so a finite spectral factorization gives vectors v_a in R^p with v_a^T v_b=k(a,b). There is an isometry between the spans of z(a) and v_a: the map sum c_a z(a) -> sum c_a v_a is well defined and norm preserving because both squared norms equal c^T K_G c. Extend orthonormal bases of the two spans to R^p. The isometry extends to an orthogonal map on R^p. Applying it to all z(x) gives a representation, still called z, with z(a)=v_a for every a in G and with the same norm and modulus bounds.

Consequently **all feature values used as weights below can be obtained from the finite prior Gram matrix on G**. Computing this fixed factorization is preprocessing of the fixed prior, not an input-dependent inverse hidden in the predictive head. Its real entries are included in the encoder's parameter count.

## 3. Cone envelope for a general continuous feature map

Define, using the finite Gram feature values,

    ztilde_j(x)=min_{a in G}[v_{a,j}+A_cone ||x-a||_1].

This formula is valid even though z_j need not be Lipschitz. We claim |ztilde_j(x)-z_j(x)|<=e for every j,x.

For a with ||x-a||_1<=r, the modulus gives v_{a,j}>=z_j(x)-Omega(r)>=z_j(x)-e/2. Adding a nonnegative cone term preserves this lower bound. For a with ||x-a||_1>r, the coordinate bound |z_j|<=R gives

    v_{a,j}+A_cone ||x-a||_1
      >z_j(x)-2R+A_cone r=z_j(x)+e.

So every candidate is >=z_j(x)-e/2, and the finite minimum is too.

For the upper bound choose a net point with ||x-a||_1<=h. Since h=e r/(2(2R+e))<=r/2, the modulus bound applies. Therefore

    ztilde_j(x)<=z_j(x)+Omega(r)+A_cone h
                  <=z_j(x)+e/2+e/2=z_j(x)+e.

It follows that sup_x ||ztilde(x)-z(x)||<=sqrt(p)e=eta and ||ztilde(x)||<=R+eta<=S. All denominators above are positive, including R=0. For a cube grid, coordinate rounding gives L1 distance <=d/(2m)<=e/(2A_cone)=h, which verifies the displayed grid size.

## 4. Exact network realization and original-posterior KL

Use C004 Section 4's explicit register construction, with the J centers now the net points a and with the slope K in the cone layer replaced by A_cone. Layer 1 computes all Jd absolute differences with 2Jd ReLUs. Layer 2 forms the pJ affine cone values using these nonnegative absolute registers and the constant register. A balanced residual-min tournament takes ceil(log_2 J) layers, including zero layers when J=1. The last gating layer, using the binary context/query flags and |ztilde_j|<=S, writes the context/query feature registers exactly. For padding choose a fixed anchor point in X as its raw coordinates, rather than assuming the ambient origin belongs to X. Its flags are zero, so the computed features are gated to zero.

This uses E=3+ceil(log_2 J) encoder layers and precisely the width and hidden-width bounds in Section 1. This invokes the exact algebraic encoder construction, **not the Lipschitz-error assertion** of C004 Section 3. Section 3 above supplies the replacement uniform approximation guarantee.

C004 Section 2's perturbation proof uses only ||ztilde-z||<=eta<=1, not feature Lipschitzness. It therefore gives original-versus-encoded predictive errors

    |mu-mutilde|<=sqrt(s eps)/2,
    |v-vtilde|<=min(s/4,s sqrt(eps)/2).

Apply C002 v1 to the encoded features with bound S and accuracy eps0. The one-head query broadcast, T five-head Chebyshev layers, and four-head readout produce muhat,vhat with vhat>=s and errors

    |mutilde-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps)/2,
    |vtilde-vhat|<=min(s/4,s sqrt(eps)/2).

The original predictive variance is also >=s. Adding scalar errors gives |mu-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps) and |v-vhat|<=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)). The Gaussian calculation in C002 Section 5 then yields forward KL<=eps from the **original kernel** predictive distribution to the transformer output. No triangle inequality for KL is used.

Combining the E encoder layers with the T+2 solver layers gives the depth. Count three D-by-D matrices for each of at most five heads, two MLP matrices of dimensions H-by-D and D-by-H per layer (even counting zeros), and a two-coordinate linear readout. This proves the displayed parameter bound.

## 5. Exact scope

C005 covers every continuous bounded finite-rank kernel on a nonempty compact Euclidean domain, with an explicit bound in terms of a kernel modulus and a finite covering number. It includes continuous kernels whose features are not Lipschitz. C004 gives the simpler closed grid formula when a coordinatewise Lipschitz feature bound is available. C002 is smaller when features are supplied directly.

C003 proves that the bounded-kernel statement without continuity can fail for continuous raw-input Gaussian-output architectures. Thus these results distinguish the feature-input interpretation from the regularity needed for a raw-input theorem. They do not claim that a raw-input size bound can ignore the fixed kernel's modulus or its feature-computation complexity. All three constructive claims remain independently unaudited.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:25:35.795629+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_72ab84954d47f7ba9454aa464a4a285daf3fa8ca77bb4816fcfbb64e852b8950","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm.llt_stein of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let ${\bf Y}_i$, $1 \le i \le m$ be independent $\mathbb{Z}^d$-valued vectors with

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:18:13.232634+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_72c467e008a478c48361d67caa0325c7229ae4c2ed22001b38458e4412b3be1b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:double-in-banach of arXiv:2506.17168, '{\bf Scaling limits for sample autocovariance operators of Hilbert space-valued linear pro'] Let $(\mathbb Y,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space, and let $\{W^{(r)}\}_{r \in \mathbb Y}$ be a family of Gaussian random measures on $(\mathbb R, \lambda)$ with covariances (equation eq:covWW of the paper). Consider a kernel $f: \mathbb Y^2 \times \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R$. We say that there exists an $L^2(\mathbb Y^2)$-valued double Wiener-It\^o integral of the kernel $f$, denoted $\mathcal{I}_2(f)$, if there exists a sequence $\{f_{(n)}: n \geq 1\}$ of $L^2(\mathbb Y^2)$-valued special kernels, defined on $\mathbb Y^2 \times \mathbb R^2$, such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item $\lim_{n \to \infty} \|f^{(r,s)} - f_{(n)}^{(r,s)}\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)} = 0$ $\mu^{\otimes 2}$-a.s.,
    
    \item the sequence $\{\mathcal{I}_2(f_{(n)}): n \geq 1\}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $L^1(\Omega:L^2(\mathbb Y^{2}))$.
    
\end{enumerate}
In that case, we define the double Wiener-It\^o integral by 
\[
\mathcal{I}_2(f) \doteq \lim_{n \to \infty} \mathcal{I}_2(f_{(n)}),
\]
where the limit is again understood in $L^1(\Omega:L^2(\mathbb Y^{2}))$. For an $\mathbb R^d-$valued kernel $f = (f_1,\dots,f_d)$ such that $\mathcal{I}_2(f_i)$ exists for all $i = 1,\dots,d$, we fix the notation $\mathcal{I}_2(f) \doteq (\mathcal{I}_2(f_1),\dots,\mathcal{I}_2(f_d))$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:01:48.633710+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_72f4b0d36bb96430ec80c8176f034705350ac15459ceb9958434cbf1c32581a0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lmm:m1m2 of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] With the above notations, we have
    \[
    m_2 = \frac{d-1}{d}am_1
    \]
and $1 \le a \le ( 2 \log (1/p))^{1/2}$.
Furthermore, assuming $a\le \sqrt d/2$, we have
\[ \zeta^2 \asymp pa^{2} \lesssim h(p)\,,
\]
where we recall that $\zeta$ is defined by ~((eq:zeta-def of the paper)).

\begin{proof}
In this proof, we fix $d$ and suppress it from the notation.  We abbreviate $\mathbb{P}=\nu$, and write $\mathbb{E}$ for expectation with respect to $\nu$.  We also abbreviate $c\equiv c_{d,1}$ and $f(t)\equiv f_d(t)$. Define
    \[ g(t)
    = c \bigg(1-\frac{t^2}{d}\bigg)^{(d-1)/2}\,,
    \]
and note that
    \begin{align*}
    \frac{d}{dt} g(t) &= -\frac{d-1}{d}  t f(t)\,,\\
    \frac{d}{dt} [tg(t)]
        &= -(t^2-1) f(t)\,.
    \end{align*}
It follows that
    \begin{align*}
    &m_1
    = \mathbb{E}[T;T\ge a]
    = \int_a^{d^{1/2} } t f(t)\,dt
    = \frac{d}{d-1} g(a)
    = \frac{cd}{d-1} \bigg(1-\frac{a^2}{d}
        \bigg)^{(d-1)/2}\,,\\
    &\mathbb E[T^2; T \ge a]-p
    =\int_a^{d^{1/2}} (t^2-1) f(t)\,dt
    =ag(a)
    = \frac{d-1}{d}am_1\,.
    \end{align*}
Rearranging the last expression gives
    \[
    m_2
    = \mathbb E[T^2 K(T)]
    = \mathbb E[T^2;T\ge a]-p
    = \frac{d-1}{d}am_1\,,
    \]
which proves the first claim. Next, recalling that $p=\mathbb{P}(T\ge a)$, to bound $a\ge1$ it suffices to prove that $\mathbb{P}(T\ge 1)> p$. In fact it is easy to argue that $\mathbb{P}(T\ge 1)$ is lower bounded by an absolute constant: $T$ is equidistributed as
    \[
    \frac{d^{1/2} Z}{(Z^2 + S)^{1/2}}
    \]
where $Z$ is a standard gaussian random variable, and $S$ is a chi-square random variable with $d-1$ degrees of freedom, independent of $Z$. If $Z \ge 2^{1/2}$ and $S \le 2(d-1)$ then the above ratio is $\ge1$, so we conclude
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(T\ge1)
    \ge \mathbb{P}(Z \ge 2^{1/2}) \mathbb{P}(S \le 2(d-1))
    \ge \frac{\mathbb{P}(Z \ge 2^{1/2})}{2}
    \ge 0.03\,.
    \]
This proves $a\ge1$, as claimed. On the other hand the upper bound on $a$ is equivalent to the bound 
\[p = \mathbb{P}(T\ge a) \le \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(-\frac{a^2}{2}\bigg)\,,\] which follows from the fact that $T$ is $1$-subgaussian (Lemma~(lem:beta.mgf of the paper)). Next, recalling the definition ~((eq:zeta-def of the paper)) of $\zeta$, it is clear that $\zeta\gtrsim p^{1/2}a$. For the upper bound, we recall that the integration by parts above gives
    \[m_1 = \frac{d}{d-1} f_d(a) 
    \bigg(1-\frac{a^2}{d}\bigg)
    \leq 2 f_d(a)\,.
    \]
It is shown later in

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:30:50.717152+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_731709fb58b17b0d6e02febf8b90d96eb1a7312fa44e1c01c675da337ce3c276","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Openproblem Uniform concomitant asymptotics and growing top-$k$ sets of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] \label[openproblem]{op:growq}
For fixed $\rho\in(0,1)$, Gaussian plurality stability measures the probability
that two correlated Gaussian score vectors select the same extremal coordinate.
The corresponding literature gives the classical asymptotic
[khot2007optimal,deklerk2004approximate]
\[
p_q(\rho)\sim
\frac{\Gamma(1/(1+\rho))^2}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}
(q-1)^{-(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)}
\bigl(4\pi\log(q-1)\bigr)^{-\rho/(1+\rho)}.
\]
When the correlation varies with $q$, existing uniform Gaussian-tail control
and Borell's bound imply [khot2007optimal]
\[
\limsup_{q\to\infty}q\,p_q(\rho_q)\le e^{2\lambda}
\qquad\text{when}\qquad \rho_q\log q\to\lambda\in[0,\infty).
\]
A matching lower bound, ideally with a uniform error estimate, remains open in
this triangular regime, where $q\to\infty$ and
$\rho_q\log q\to\lambda$. The case $\lambda=0$ already follows from the
upper bound and $p_q(\rho)\ge1/q$ for $\rho\ge0$. More generally, determine
overlap when $q$, $k$, and $\rho^{-1}$ grow jointly. The goal is to establish
a sharp triangular-regime and top-$k$ extension of the Gaussian stability
kernel.
Deterministic ordinal capacity and the corresponding Gaussian-cloud
conjecture are recorded in
(thm:ordinal,conj:ordinal-gaussian of the paper). (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:25:39.116307+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_733471e1b267fe76f9b33cbbbebb4e2ca1489cbfef0b2ecb9bc930e13e6da4f9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def: plus minus interface of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Let $$\mathtt{Dob}^+:=\partial\Lambda_N\cap \{z=(z^{(1)},z^{(2)})\in\mathbb Z^d, z^{(2)}\geq 0\},\quad \mathtt{Dob}^-:=\partial\Lambda_N\cap \{z=(z^{(1)},z^{(2)})\in\mathbb Z^d, z^{(2)}<0\}$$
    denote the upper and bottom half parts of the boundary of the box $\Lambda_N.$ Then the Dobrushin boundary condition (denoted $\pm$) is the boundary condition that being plus on $\mathtt{Dob}^+$ and minus on $\mathtt{Dob}^-.$ Now given any configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_N}$ satisfying Dobrushin boundary condition, we define the upmost plus--minus boundary interface $\gamma=\gamma(\sigma)$ as follows.

Let
$
\mathtt{Plus}(\sigma)=\{z\in\Lambda_N:\sigma_z=1\}
$
denote the set of plus spins. By definition, we have
$
\mathtt{Dob}^+\subset \mathtt{Plus}(\sigma).
$
Since $\mathtt{Dob}^+$ is connected in $\mathbb Z^2$, there exists a unique connected component of $\mathtt{Plus}(\sigma)$ containing $\mathtt{Dob}^+$, which we denote by $\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)$.

Define
\[
\Lambda^+(\sigma)
=
\big\{
z\in\Lambda_N:
\text{every path from }z
\text{ to }\partial\Lambda_{N+1}
\text{ intersects }
\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)
\big\},
\]
and let
$
\Lambda^-(\sigma)=\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda^+(\sigma).
$
Intuitively, $\Lambda^+(\sigma)$ is obtained by filling in all holes of $\mathtt{ConPlus}(\sigma)$.

We then define
\[
\gamma^+(\sigma)
=
\{x\in\Lambda^+(\sigma):
\exists y\in\Lambda^-(\sigma)
\text{ with }
x\sim_* y
\}
\setminus \mathtt{Dob}^+,
\]
and
$\gamma^-(\sigma)=\partial_{\mathrm{ext}}\Lambda^+(\sigma)\setminus \mathtt{Dob}^-.$
Here $x\sim_* y$ means that $x$ and $y$ are $*$-neighbors. By planar duality, $\gamma^+$ forms a connected set of plus spins, while $\gamma^-$ forms a $*$-connected set of minus spins. Hence
$
\gamma=(\gamma^+,\gamma^-)
$
defines a plus--minus interface. Moreover, $\gamma$ is the upmost interface, since every $*$-connected minus path from $\mathtt{Dob}^-$ to $\mathtt{Dob}^-$ must intersect $\gamma^+$.

Finally, let $\Sigma_\gamma$ denote the collection of configurations satisfying $\gamma(\sigma)=\gamma$.
It is easy to see that 
$\Sigma_\gamma=\{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_N}: \sigma_{\mid \mathtt{Dob}^+\cup\gamma^+}=1, \sigma_{\mid \mathtt{Dob}^-\cup\gamma^-}=-1\}.$
For convenience, write
$
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,\epsilon h}(\gamma)
=
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,\epsilon h}(\Sigma_\gamma),
$
and similarly
$
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,0}(\gamma)
=
\mu^\pm_{\Lambda_N,0}(\Sigma_\gamma),
$
where the superscript $\pm$ indicates Dobrushin boundary conditions.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.317781+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_733d5128b10f526ef8ef551d38a822d942fe8b13bd76d1e6063b6994468a5eec","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition {\cite[Definition 4.10 of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] {Gabai1983_FoliationsAndTheTopologyOf3Manifolds_PUB},[AgolZhang2022_GutsInSuturedDecompositionsAndTheThurstonNorm_ARXv1]}]
Let \((N,\gamma)\) be a taut sutured manifold and let \(S\) be the maximal set of pairwise disjoint non-parallel product annuli and product disks in \(N\).
We define the \emph{sutured guts} \(\mathrm{Guts}(N)\) of \((N,\gamma)\) as the sutured manifold obtained from \((N,\gamma)\) by decomposing along \(S\) and discarding \emph{windows}, namely, product sutured manifold components.

The sutured guts is well-defined up to isotopy class of inclusion map by classical JSJ decomposition theory \autocite{Johannson1979_HomotopyEquivalencesOf3ManifoldsWithBoundaries_PUB} \autocite{JacoShalen1979_SeifertFiberedSpacesIn3Manifolds}.","status":"unverified"}

    Let $D=f(x)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+g(y)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ be a derivation on the field $\mathbb{Q}(x,y)$.

    Then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a non-constant $F\in \mathbb{Q}(x,y)$ such that $D(F)=0$.
        \item One of the following is true:
    \begin{enumerate}

        \]
        \item There exists a quadratic extension $L/\mathbb{Q}$, irreducible polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{Q}[y]$ that split over $L$ into conjugate factors $f_i=f_{i1}f_{i2}$ and $g_j=g_{j1}g_{j2}$, and $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in L\setminus \mathbb{Q}$, $d_1,\ldots,d_m\in L\setminus \mathbb{Q}$ satisfying $c_i+\overline{c_i}=0,d_j+\overline{d_j}=0$ such that
        \[

        \hspace{1cm} 
        \frac{1}{g}=\sum_{i=1}^m \frac{d_i (g_{i1}'g_{i2}-g_{i2}'g_{i1})}{g_i}.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:33:06.561696+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73b882c425523866250a75884430f40e37c5bd3d993ed81a7966323040759410","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 31 (\cite{RT}) of arXiv:2608.26068, 'All once-extended 3D TQFTs are Reshetikhin--Turaev theories'] Let $M$ be a closed connected 3-manifold and $\Gamma$ a labelled embedded ribbon graph in $M$ with ribbon-colouring $K$ and vertex labels $\set{f_v}$. The invariant $\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) \in k$ is defined as follows: 

    Let $L$ be a framed link in $S^3$ (viewed as an embedded $S^1\times I$) with $\# L$ components, and $(\Gamma,K,\set{f_v})$ a labelled embedded ribbon graph in $S^3$ such that performing surgery on $L$ yields the pair $(M,|\Gamma|)$. Then, we have an embedding of $|\Gamma\cup L|$ in $S^3$; call this a \emph{surgery presentation} of the pair $(M,|\Gamma|)$. $\Gamma\cup L$ is now a labelled ribbon graph with some uncoloured loops. Additionally, let $X_L$ be the trace of the framed link $L$ (the 4-manifold with boundary $M$ given by attaching 2-handles to $D^4$ along the framed link $L$). Define $\sigma(X_L)$ to be the signature of $X_L$.

    The invariant on the labelled embedded ribbon graph $\Gamma$ is a scalar multiple of the operator invariant of $\Gamma\cup L$: $$\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) := p_-^{\sigma(X_L)}\sqrt{D}^{-\sigma(X_L)-\# L-1} F(\Gamma \cup L,K,\set{f_v}).$$

    In general, if $M$ is not connected, say $(M,\Gamma) = \bigsqcup (M_i,\Gamma_i)$ where each $M_i$ is connected, then we define $$\tau(M,\Gamma,K,\set{f_v}) := \prod\tau(M_i,\Gamma_i,K|_{\Gamma_i},\set{f_v})$$ to be the product of $\tau$ over all the components.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-07T05:37:56.959283+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73bc069b75844adba49e89625e6b0eb1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] For any $\\sigma\\geq 0$, and $0<a<b\\leq 1$, let us define the analytic function $\\begin{split}Z(\\cdot,\\sigma:a,b):z\\in D_{\\sigma}(a,b)\\mapsto Z(z,\\sigma:a,b):=\\frac{1}{\\sigma+f(0)+(1-z)f(0)(1/a-1/b)}\\in\\mathbb{C}\\end{split}$ on the open disc $D_{\\sigma}(a,b)$ of radius $R_{\\sigma}(a,b)$, where $\\begin{split}R_{\\sigma}(a,b)=1+\\cfrac{\\sigma+f(0)}{f(0)(1/a-1/b)}>1\\.\\end{split}$ Then for any $z\\in D_{\\sigma}(a,b)$ we have $\\begin{split}\\lim_{\\varepsilon\\to 0}Z^{\\varepsilon}(z,\\sigma:a,b)=Z(z,\\sigma:a,b)\\.\\end{split}$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.009931+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73bcb31239d41e9890cd7900fe624ca644493718e01d1a221369e09347e39dd3","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For every field $\kk$, the class $\RV$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item It is invariant under permutations of variables and nonnegative
rational linear substitutions, including coordinate restriction.
\item It is closed under products.
\item If $f\in\RV$, then every ordinary coordinate derivative
$\partial_x^\gamma f$ lies in $\RV$.
\item It is closed under coordinatewise lower and upper truncations in the
divided-power basis.
\item It is invariant under common divided-power translations:
\[
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha]}\in\RV
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^{[\alpha+\gamma]}\in\RV.
\]
\item If $f\in\RV$, then its factorial normalization $\Nrm(f)$ lies in
$\RV$.
\item If $F_1,F_2$ have realizable factorial normalizations, then
$\Nrm(F_1F_2)$ lies in $\RV$.
\item Full polarization preserves $\RV$.
\item Membership is invariant under arbitrary field extension; for
polynomials with rational coefficients, it depends only on
$\operatorname{char}(\kk)$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:46:36.093174+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73be9b6f86d9edc7e06c25ab690a01a5d9b777b0ea8a246cd2a959d9b8c1e573","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:tangent-ball-convergence-general of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Let $K\Subset O$. For $x\in K$ and small $h$, the sets $B_{x,h}$ lie in a
common compact subset of $\mathbb R^n$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}

  \longrightarrow0.

Consequently, locally uniformly in $x\in O$,
\begin{align}
  \int_{B_{x,h}}\xi_i\xi_jJ_x(\delta_h\xi)\,\,d\xi
  &\longrightarrow M_{ij}(x),
  &&1\leq i,j\leq k,
  \\

  &\longrightarrow\widehat V_x.

 \int_{B_{x,h}}\Psi(x,\xi)J_x(\delta_h\xi)^\theta\,\,d\xi
 \longrightarrow
 J_x(0)^\theta\int_{\widehat B_x}\Psi(x,\xi)\,\,d\xi .
\end{equation}
The convergence is locally uniform in $x$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:52:08.667563+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_73d0c639faad0d6c7c76fd8740caf43e4cd9f3f12e44e8145caac13ef1aab777","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 17 (Fiber-equivalent torus fibrations) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let
\[
        \pi_i:M\to S^1_i,\qquad i=0,1,
\]
be torus fibrations.  The target circles are not part of the fixed data and may
be different.  Choose a basepoint \(x\in M\) and, for each \(i=0,1\), an identification
\(\pi_1(S_i^1,\pi_i(x))\cong\ZZ\), and let
\[
        \alpha_{\pi_i,x}:\pi_1(M,x)\longrightarrow\ZZ,
\]
be the surjective homomorphism induced by \(\pi_i\).  Changing the
identification changes \(\alpha_{\pi_i,x}\) by a sign.  Equivalently, \(\pi_i\)
determines a cohomology class \([\pi_i]\in H^1(M;\ZZ)\), well-defined up to
sign.  We say that \(\pi_0\) and \(\pi_1\) are \emph{fiber-equivalent}
if
\[
        [\pi_0]=\pm[\pi_1]\in H^1(M;\ZZ).
\]
Equivalently, after choosing a common basepoint,
\[
        \ker\alpha_{\pi_0,x}=\ker\alpha_{\pi_1,x}\subset\pi_1(M,x).
\]
For a different basepoint, the two kernels are changed by the same conjugacy
convention.  Thus, in fiber-subgroup language, the definition says that the
images of the two fiber fundamental groups agree, up to this usual conjugacy
ambiguity.","status":"unverified"}

We define the following subspaces of $L^2(\Omega)$.
    \begin{align*}
    H^1_0(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^1_\Gamma(\Omega) & \coloneq  \{f\in H^1(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}^{\Gamma}(f) = 0\},\\
        H^{\operatorname{div}}_0(\Omega)& \coloneq   \{f\in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)~|~ {\operatorname{tr}}_N(f) = 0\},\\

         H^\Delta_0(\Omega)& \coloneq \{f\in H^1_0(\Omega)~|~ \nabla f \in H^{\operatorname{div}}(\Omega)\},\\

    The first two spaces are equipped with the usual $H^1$-norm, the third and fourth with the usual $H^{\operatorname{div}}$-norm,

Method: A Feller topology for limits of reversible Markov chains structural attempt Result: The suggested unweighted heat-kernel metric can be infinite in a basic admissible example. For Brownian motion on the two-torus, the squared row-distance integrated against exp(-t)dt equals sum_(k in Z^2) |1-exp(2pi*i*k.h)|^2/[1+8pi^2*|k|^2]. At h=(1/2,0), every odd k1 has numerator4. Each dyadic annulus contains order N^2 such terms of order N^-2, so the series diverges. A repair is to use w(t)=exp(-t)/(1+G(2t)), where G is the integrated diagonal heat trace: Fubini gives finite weighted row norm for almost every state. This produces an almost-everywhere finite Hilbert-space pseudometric after identifying indistinguishable rows. Obstruction: Brownian motion already has a good usual topology, so the divergence refutes only the illustrative formula, not the existence conjecture. {"assumptions":["(X,B,mu) is a probability space and T preserves mu (invertibility is not needed)","P and Q are countable measurable partitions","H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity","entropies are taken with a fixed logarithm base throughout"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090248+00:00","domain":"ergodic theory, entropy","id":"claim_73e397e27849e65c29b0ad85dd4fc2d78bd89a46e9ea1748bcc9855a192424af","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let T be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space (X, B, mu) and let P and Q be countable measurable partitions with H_mu(P) < infinity and H_mu(Q) < infinity. Write P_n for the join of T^{-i}P over 0 <= i <= n-1 and h_mu(T,P) = lim_n (1/n) H_mu(P_n) (the limit exists by subadditivity and equals the infimum over n). Then h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P) + H_mu(Q | P). Two standard consequences: if P refines Q then H_mu(Q | P) = 0 and hence h_mu(T, Q) <= h_mu(T, P), so the partition entropy is monotone under refinement; and |h_mu(T,P) - h_mu(T,Q)| <= H_mu(P | Q) + H_mu(Q | P), i.e. the map P -> h_mu(T,P) is 1-Lipschitz for the Rokhlin metric. WHERE IT FAILS: finiteness of H_mu(P) and H_mu(Q) is used - with infinite-entropy partitions both sides can be infinite and the inequality carries no information. The inequality is one-sided: nothing bounds h_mu(T,P) from below in terms of h_mu(T,Q) unless the conditional entropy in the other direction is also controlled. It is an inequality between the entropies of PROCESSES, not of the partitions: H_mu(Q) <= H_mu(P) + H_mu(Q|P) is the (easier) static statement and must not be quoted in its place.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:19:42.577408+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7405fcfc60ba2e2b510f49b725ba23ec3d1ae5ec2bd38cd0f3790d4437a8427b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 1 of arXiv:2609.03512, ''] Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$, and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ be a vector of positive integers. The \emph{blow-up} $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by replacing each vertex $v_i$ with an independent set
\[
V_i = \{v_i^1,\ldots,v_i^{m_i}\}
\]
of $m_i$ vertices, and joining $v_i^s$ to $v_j^t$ if and only if $v_iv_j\in E(G)$. We call $V_i$ the \emph{part of $G\bigodot m$ corresponding to $v_i$}, and say that $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplication of vertices} (Golumbic \cite{Graph-multiplication-Golumbic}, p.~53).

If $m_j=1$ for all $j\ne i$, we say $G\bigodot m$ is obtained from $G$ by \emph{multiplying the single vertex $v_i$}; if moreover $m_i=2$, this is called \emph{duplicating} $v_i$ (Henning and Southey \cite{Henning-Michael}). If $G$ has a vertex of degree $2$, \emph{degree-$2$ vertex duplication} denotes the operation of duplicating any such vertex.

For graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_k$, we write $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$ for the family of all graphs obtainable from some $G_\ell$ by multiplication of vertices. Since $G\bigodot(1,\ldots,1)=G$, each $G_\ell$ itself belongs to $\mathcal{M}(G_1,\ldots,G_k)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.808109+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_743cf06b65abbce3837731c48aedf308156ff722d986e3dbe43f324ccbc4041f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm FirstPresentation of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathcal{Q} $ be an acyclic quiver with $ N $ vertices such that the vertices $ 1, \ldots, n $ are mutable 
	and $ n+1, \ldots, N $ are frozen.  
	Let $ K $ be a field
	and let $ \boldsymbol{x} = (x_1, \ldots, x_N ) $ be an $ N $-tuple of elements that are algebraically independent over $ K $.
	The cluster algebra $ \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{Q}) \subset K(\boldsymbol{x}) =  K(x_1, \ldots, x_n, \ldots, x_N) $ (defined over $ K $) corresponding to $ \mathcal{Q} $ is isomorphic to
	
	\begin{equation}
		 
		K[x_{n+1}^{\pm 1}, \ldots, x_{N}^{\pm 1}][x_1, \ldots, x_n, x_1', \ldots, x_n']
		/ \langle x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \} \rangle 
	\end{equation}
	where $ (x_1', \ldots, x_n') $ is another tuple of algebraically independent elements over $ K $, 
	the products range over those vertices $ i $ of $ \mathcal{Q} $ for which there is an arrow $ i \rightarrow k $ (resp.~$ i \leftarrow k $),
	and
	$ b_{ik} \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $ is the number of arrows $ i \rightarrow k $ which is negative if there are arrows $ i \leftarrow k $. 
	\\
	Moreover, 
	$ (x_k x_k' - \prod_{i\rightarrow k} x_i^{b_{ik}} - \prod_{i \leftarrow k} x_i^{-b_{ik}} \mid k \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \}) $ 
	is a Gr\"obner basis for the ideal which it generates with respect to any term order
	giving preference to $ x_1', \ldots, x_n' $ over $ \boldsymbol{x} $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:01:01.827867+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_743d5d91ec5fa0d1bc263db5a121c45eb8eb88690abe3f623f6e6499dcabf8b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:CGO-PhS_int-by-parts of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] [zbMATH07801151]\sl 
Consider $F \in L^2(\Sigma)$ such that 
there exists $c > 0$ so that $e^{c|\mathrm{x}|} F \in L^2(\Sigma)$.
Let $u \in C([0,T]; L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ satisfy the conditions

\[
\left\{

		\begin{aligned}
		& (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u = F & & \textnormal{in} \enspace \Sigma, \\
		& u(0, \centerdot) = u(T, \centerdot) = 0 &  & \textnormal{in} \enspace \mathbb{R}^n.
		\end{aligned}

	\right.
\]

For every $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$,
consider a measurable function 
$v^\nu : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ such that

\[ \sup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} \big[ 2^{-|\alpha|/2} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} \big] + \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^2} 2^{|\alpha| \theta} \| e^{- \nu \cdot \mathrm{x}} (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) v^\nu \|_{L^2(\Pi_\alpha^\nu)} < \infty, \]
for some $\theta \in (0, 1/2)$. Then,

\[\int_\Sigma (i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta) u \overline{v^\nu} = \int_\Sigma u \overline{(i\partial_\mathrm{t} + \Delta)v^\nu} \, \]
for all $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{ 0 \}$ with $|\nu| < c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:35:05.847715+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_743d8ab82a44d95452e5859b4d8664f0515c640850c73fc24487dec1d16c4265","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:cheeger-M of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Let $A\subset S$ with $\pi(A)\le 1/2$ be a set achieving the Cheeger
constant~$h_P$, and assume $h_P \le 1 - \pi(A)$ (at equality the bound
below has zero numerator; see Remark~(rmk:cheeger-balanced of the paper)).
Then there exists $x^*\in A$ with $P(x^*,A)\ge 1-h_P$, and
\[
  M
  \;\ge\;
  r(x^*)
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{(1-h_P)\log\dfrac{1-h_P}{\pi(A)}
  +h_P\log\dfrac{h_P}{1-\pi(A)}}{\log\!\bigl(1/\pi(x^*)\bigr)}.
\]
The term involving $h_P$ is interpreted by continuity as $0$ when $h_P=0$.
In particular, for small $h_P$,
$M \gtrsim \log(1/\pi(A))/\log(1/\pi_{\min})$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.339073+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_745e5681f8b0886f342dc96352830c0936cd6c44a07fdad151e955aaaba841b8","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 16 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (Two-blocks estimate,
cf.\ Lemma 5.6 of \cite{BFS})
Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$ 
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.  Then, there exists 
a constant $C = C(u_0,\ell_0)$ such that, for $\ell \geq  \ell_0$,  and 
a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x)\\
& \hskip 20mm \times\Big\{
E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm  \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2}\ell^{p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times \Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell_0)}(x)]-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag\\
&\hskip 10mm \leq CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^p \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac1N \sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:30.017980+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7463beeea5e6e439db51790c99eaf33807214ea361def5c7eb7baa2ed41e5398","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 31 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Let $\{\mu_n, \mu\} \subset {\cal D}$ and let $\{A^n, A\}$ be the corresponding PCAFs.
Assume that $d_{\cal D}(\mu_n, \mu) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the following assertions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm (1)] For any compact set $K \subset E$, there exists a subsequence $\{n_k\}$ such that the PCAFs $A^{n_k}$ converge to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to $K$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$. That is,
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} \left| \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA^{n_k}_u - \int_0^s 1_K(X_u) \, dA_u \right| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E.
$$

\item[\rm (2)] Suppose there exists a compact nest $\{F_\ell\}$ satisfying the following tail estimate:
\begin{equation} 
\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \sup_{\nu \in {\cal S}_{c,00}^1} \left\{ \left( \sup_n \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu_n \right) \vee \int_{F_\ell^c} U_1 \nu \, d\mu \right\} = 0.
\end{equation}
Then, there exists a further subsequence $\{n'_k\}$ such that $A^{n'_k}$ converges to $A$ locally uniformly in $t$ on $[0,\infty)$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for quasi every $x \in E$:
$$
{\mathbb P}_x \left( \lim_{k \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le s \le t} |A^{n'_k}_s - A_s| = 0 \text{ for all } t > 0 \right) = 1, \quad \text{q.e. } x \in E,
$$
where ${\cal S}_{c,00}^1 := \{ \nu \in {\cal S}_0 : \mathrm{supp}[\nu] \text{ is compact}, \nu(E) \le 1 \text{ and } \|U_1\nu\|_\infty \le 1 \}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] the numbers $\overline{C}_b^\rho(n)$ of $\rho$-color $b$-ary

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:41:03.337123+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_746bed522e7c725f463dd256513d70b837b5e6533c85e85cd18bc2fc043d9e60","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Linear-tilt localization scheme of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\mu = \mu_0$ be a probability measure,  $(\mu_t)_{t \in \Z_{\ge 0}}$ be a localization process.

\begin{equation}
        \sum_{j=1}^N q_{N,j}(B_N+C_Nx)^2\to0.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:43:45.382679+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74acf4f1f508c15c520e36d5a05358fd1b8a83767ea6093789c543d1fd4ced5c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2609.04069, 'Positive and Negative Square Energies of $2$-Connected Graphs'] For $n\geq3$, we have,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.844443+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74aea2cd8db60f8ef6abeb2f0de339c455d193112a37b4b95a29233b010327f5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:joint of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $m\ge2$, $\beta>0$, $m\beta>1$, set $\delta=m\beta/2$ and $d=m-1$, and write $\xi=\xi^{\beta,\delta}$. For $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)\in\mathbb R^d$ define
\[
H_b(t):=\mathbb E\prod_{j=1}^d|\xi(tb_j)|^\beta,
\qquad
A(b):=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j,
\qquad
B(b):=\sum_{j=1}^d b_j^2.
\]
Then, uniformly for $b$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R^d$,
\begin{equation}
H_b(t)=1-\beta tA(b)\mathbb E S_1
+\frac{t^2}{2}\left[\beta^2A(b)^2\mathbb E S_1^2-\beta B(b)\mathbb E S_2\right]+o(t^2).
\end{equation}
For real $\delta$ the zero process is reflection symmetric, hence $\mathbb E S_1=0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236900+00:00","domain":"category theory","id":"claim_74afa4479d3dad60357c9de74c72bf7b39271c211d26362c05beb1fb4b52a5ba","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let J be a small category (the index or diagram shape) and D: J -> C a functor (a diagram of shape J) into a category C. A cone over D is an object X of C together with morphisms mu_j: X -> D(j), one for each object j of J, such that for every morphism alpha: j -> j' in J, D(alpha) o mu_j = mu_{j'} (composing with D(alpha) recovers the other leg of the cone). A limit of D is a cone (L, (pi_j)) that is universal among cones over D: for every other cone (X, (mu_j)) there is a unique morphism u: X -> L in C such that pi_j o u = mu_j for every j. Dually, a cocone under D is an object Y with morphisms nu_j: D(j) -> Y such that nu_{j'} o D(alpha) = nu_j for every alpha: j -> j' in J, and a colimit is a universal such cocone (Co, (iota_j)): for every cocone (Y,(nu_j)) there is a unique morphism v: Co -> Y with v o iota_j = nu_j for every j. Products, equalizers, and pullbacks are examples of limits; coproducts, coequalizers, and pushouts are examples of colimits.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.249203+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74bfb754ef697d03a45d3c3692cfc52ab863d127087047336529dceb24eb75a9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:advancing-escape-final of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Consider the VEB setting, and let $\Psi = (g,\tau_g,j,\overline{z},\mathcal{S},\textup{advancing}) \in \ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$ be a high-level state. 
Let $S$ be the (sole) set in $\mathcal{S}$ (Definition~(def:advancing-state of the paper)).
Suppose that $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$  is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning. Conditioned on the events $\Psi(\tau_g) = \Psi$ and $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(\tau_g) = \overline{a}$, with probability at least $1-\exp(-400j/\lambda^2)$, 
the following events occur. 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $(6j^{25},j^{27},2/(\xi j^3),2)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g + j^{22} \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\mathcal{N}_S^{E_g}(t+1) \le \lambda|S|/80$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:55.056193+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74dd1bada3ca3b546ba102ccdb0e550227e7ab7cfe659716f57c191e23d1f1b9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:int-ik-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Diamond$-p model, then
  $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ and $x \in W$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only prove the modal cases.
    We note that $\Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent by the proof of Proposition (prop:hybrid-persistency of the paper).

    ($\Box\Leftrightarrow$)
    Easily proven by the induction hypothesis.

    ($\Diamond\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then $\forall x'\, (x \leq x' \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y'\, (x' \sqsubset y' \mathrel{\text{\&}} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi))$.
    This and $x \leq x$ imply that there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, then $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    Now take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$,
    then by the $\Diamond$-p condition, $x' \geq x \sqsubset y$ implies that there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y' \geq y$.
    Here, $y \leq y' \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by persistency,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.432046+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_74ecfeb3596696dc875c4e1e12763ce9b3c90cb3eca1bd9b37058b930e3572e9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma Affine invariance of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:affine_invariance}
Let $X \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ be discrete, 
let $f_Y \in \Sym(X)$, 
let $A$ be a linear bijection on $\mathbb{R}^d$
and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^d$. 
Then $f_{AY - b} \in \Sym(AX + b)$. 

Moreover, for any fixed $c>0$, $H(AY-b) \ge cH(AX + b)$ iff $H(Y) \ge cH(X)$, 
and for $d=1$ and nonzero $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Var(aY-b) \ge c\Var(aX+b)$ iff $\Var(Y) \ge c\Var(X)$. 

\begin{proof}
For the first claim it is sufficient to check the symmetry equations, 
and indeed
\[ 
f_{AX+b + AY-b}(z)

= f_{X+Y}(A^{-1} z)
= f_{X+Y}(-A^{-1} z)

= f_{AX+b + AY-b}(-z). 
\]

Also, $H(AY-b) = H(Y)$ and $H(AX+b) = H(X)$. 
Finally, $\Var(aY-b)= a^2\Var(Y)$ and $\Var(aX+b) = a^2\Var(X)$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:31:57.880757+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_751309b82d7f82ca4bfb545cf6a1028a0c7b34cf49e805d99035691add0554ba","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $\mu$   be a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the \emph{decomposability bundle} is a Borel map $T^{AM}_\mu: \mathbb{R}^n \to \Gr(\mathbb{R}^n)$ such that the following
		statements hold:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Every Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is differentiable at $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with respect to the
			linear subspace $T_\mu^{AM}$, that is, there exists a linear function $df_x^{AM}: T^{AM}_\mu(x) \to \mathbb{R}$, such that
			\[ f(x+h) = f(x) + df_x^{AM}(h) + o(\lvert h\rvert)
			\quad \text{for } h \in T^{AM}_\mu(x). \]
			\item The previous statement is sharp:  there exists a Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$
			such that for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$ the derivative of $f$ at $x$ in the
			direction $v$ does not exist. More precisely, for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have
			\[
			\liminf_{t \to 0} \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t} < \limsup_{t \to 0}  \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}, \quad \mbox{for all $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$}
			\]
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:41:29.035941+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_751c73dbc4a9b3c6f851dc22d88b5cb0ba550e33a9bce5e0b889e2df6e8082ec","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] Let $N\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a domain. {"assumptions":["Omega is an open subset of R^n","a^{ij}, b^i, c are real measurable functions on Omega","lambda|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta| for a.e. x and all xi, eta, with 0 < lambda <= Lambda","b, c in L^infinity(Omega)"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:46.146605+00:00","domain":"elliptic partial differential equations","id":"claim_75419cd164d6c32ab1bfadcce110ec20099caa13bce89689fcdfa2e327dc1380","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Omega be an open subset of R^n. A second-order operator in divergence form is Lu = -sum_{i,j} D_i(a^{ij}(x) D_j u) + sum_i b^i(x) D_i u + c(x) u, written Lu = -div(A grad u) + b.grad u + c u, where A = (a^{ij}) is a real n x n matrix-valued measurable function on Omega (not necessarily symmetric, not necessarily continuous) and b = (b^i), c are real measurable functions. L is uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda if for a.e. x in Omega and all xi, eta in R^n: A(x)xi.xi >= lambda|xi|^2 and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta|; one normally also assumes b, c in L^infinity(Omega). Only the symmetric part of A enters the ellipticity condition. Sign convention: with the leading minus sign, L = -Laplacian when A = I, b = 0, c = 0, so a subsolution (Lu <= 0) generalizes a subharmonic function, and the favorable sign of the zeroth-order coefficient is c >= 0. The ratio Lambda/lambda is the ellipticity ratio; the constants in the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory depend only on n and Lambda/lambda. For u in H^1_loc the expression Lu is defined only weakly (in the sense of distributions); no differentiability of A is required.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:09:41.190841+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_755f38c99ac504c380213f824b488ba7e34c6a4417bc09bbc2db797ea15a7f76","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In differential geometry, the Ricci curvature tensor, named after Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro, measures how a curved space locally differs from flat space by tracking how nearby geodesics spread apart or converge. In Riemannian geometry, the Ricci curvature in a given tangent direction may be interpreted as an average of the sectional curvatures of planes containing that direction. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:32:56.084096+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7563ad0e35a3413e3e49d2d77ceb4be071dfe625cef4e526dba40e6e4803462b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2411.12522, 'Canonical insurance models: stochastic equations and comparison theorems'] Let  $(V^i)$ and  $(\bar V^i)$  be the state-wise prospective reserves of canonical insurance models $(\alpha, \Lambda, \Phi, B, b)$ and $(\bar \alpha, \bar \Lambda, \bar \Phi, B, b)$, where on each compact interval the differences {$\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ shall} have finite variation. 	\begin{align*}

	\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{ V^i(t) \geq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:32:58.301200+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_75709dd5f2dc73b63b81f372db4678ef3bbe3e2ee643593b134f378343ad3f51","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm: density R configuration of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] Let \( (v_1, \dots, v_k) \) be an inductive configuration with covariance matrix \( R \), and assume that
\[
\norm{v_k - v_{k-1}}_2 \neq \operatorname{diam}\left(\bigcap_{j < k-1} S_{v_j, r_j}\right).
\]

Then for any measurable set \( A \subseteq \mathbb{S}^{n-1} \) with \( \sigma(A) \geq \omega_R(n^{-\epsilon_R}) \), the probability that a uniformly random tuple \( (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta(n, R) \) lies entirely in \( A \) satisfies
\[
\mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta(n, R)}(x_1 \in A, \dots, x_k \in A) \geq \Omega_R(\sigma(A)^{C_R}),
\]
as \( n \to \infty \). The constant \( C_R \) is given by
\[
C_R = \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \frac{2}{1 - |c_i|} \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} \frac{1 + |c_j|}{1 - |c_j|},
\]
with
\[
c_1 = r_1, \quad c_i = (f_{c_{i-1}} \circ \cdots \circ f_{c_1})(r_i), \quad i = 2, \dots, k-1,
\]
and \( f_c(r) = \frac{r - c^2}{1 - c^2} \). The constant $\epsilon_R$ is given by
$$\epsilon_R=\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{1-|c_i|}{1+|c_i|}.$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:57:44.942619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_75f3feba910cc773f54b511a7f352aa50e21cd04aa787c111a17615bda234f11","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Perron 1 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] Let $A \in M_n$, $n \geq 2$, be irreducible with nonnegative entries. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item There exists a  number $\mu > 0$, called the Perron--Frobenius eigenvalue of $A$, such that $\mu$ is a simple eigenvalue of $A$ and any other eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ verifies $|\lambda| \leq \mu$. Thus $\rho(A)=\mu$.

\item The Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue of $A$ fulfils the row-sum inequalities
\begin{equation}
\min_{1\leq i \leq n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} \leq \mu \leq  \max_{1\leq i \leq n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}.
\end{equation}

\item The matrix $A$ is similar to $e^{2\pi i /h} A$ and the spectrum of $A$ is invariant under multiplication by $e^{2\pi i /h}$.

\item If $h>1$, there exists a permutation matrix $P$ such that
\begin{equation}
            P^{\intercal}AP =
            \begin{bmatrix}
        0&\!\!\!\smash{A_{{1,2}}}&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0 \\
        0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\smash{A_{{2,3}}}&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0 \\[-4pt]
        \vdots&\!\!\!\vdots&\!\!\!\vdots&\!\!\!\ddots&\!\!\vdots \\
        0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!\smash{A_{{h-1,h}}} \\
        \smash{A_{{h,1}}}&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!0&\!\!\!\cdots&\!\!0
\end{bmatrix},
\end{equation}
where the non-zero blocks are square matrices.

\item If $h=1$, then the limit $$\lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{A^m}{\mu^m}$$ exists. This limit is called the \emph{Perron projection} of $A$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.486800+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_761b2d8f3655734a94ab4ea519ee44debdd80eba52b88e90ff61f055e52f8b37","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Suppose the coefficient $G:=gg^\top/2$ is non-degenerate in $y$ uniformly with respect to $x$ and the drift $f$ satisfies the weak recurrence condition 
\bea\ad
\lim_{|y| \to \infty} \sup_{x\in \rr^{d_1}} \bqv{y,f(x,y)}=-\infty.
\eea 
Assume that $f,g\in C_b^{\vartheta, \dl}$ with $0< \dl \leq 1$ and $\vartheta \geq 0$. Then for every $Z\in C_p^{\vartheta, \dl}$ satisfying \eqref{cen-cond}, there exists a unique solution $u\in C_p^{\vartheta,2+\dl}$ to Poisson equation \eqref{Poi-eq} satisfying \eqref{cen-cond} given by 
\bea\ad 
u(x, y)= \int_0^\infty \EE Z(x, y_t^x)dt.
\eea
Moreover, there exists a constant $\wdh n>0$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] (Case $\vartheta=0$) for any $x\in \rr^{d_1}$ and $y\in \rr^{d_2}$,
\beq{u-der-y}
|u(x, y)|+|\nabla_y u(x, y)|+ |\nabla_y^2 u(x, y)| \leq C_0 (1+|y|^{\wdh n}),
\eeq
where $C_0> 0$ depends only on $d_1, d_2$ and $\|f\|_{C_b^{0,\dl}}$, $\|g\|_{C_b^{0,\dl}}$ and $[Z]_{C_p^{0,\dl}}$;
\item[(ii)] (Case $\vartheta>0$) for any $y \in \rr^{d_2}$,
\bea
\|u(\cdot,y)\|_{C_b^{\vartheta}} \leq C_0 C_\vartheta (1+|y|^{\wdh n}),
\eea
where $C_\vartheta>0$ depends on $d_1, d_2$ and $\|f\|_{C_b^{\vartheta,\dl}}$, $\|g\|_{C_b^{\vartheta,\dl}}$ and $[Z]_{C_p^{\vartheta,\dl}}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.895558+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7630bcd8578b012b53c6ad45fac8a6b934b685cfad5321eaf6b48e5767bb2dbd","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 2 (Positive local maxima use one cluster) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Consider the constrained maximization problem
\[
    \max_{b_1,\ldots,b_K,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_K}
    F(b_1,\ldots,b_K,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_K),
\]
where
\[
    F(b_1,\ldots,b_K,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_K)
    :=
    -\frac{\zeta}{K\sqrt6}
    \sum_{c=1}^K
    b_c\varphi(b_c)\rho_c^3,
\]
subject to
\[
    \sum_{c=1}^K\frac{b_c^2}{R^2}
    +
    \sum_{c=1}^K\rho_c^2
    =

\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-10T02:20:17.000000+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_763385ef9e7316333ac3a58b77085518aa2854967b6182c2dc3d9f10ebd9af37","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"In multivariable calculus, the implicit function theorem is a theorem that provides sufficient conditions under which a planar curve specified by an equation F(x, y) = 0 can also be specified as the graph of a function y = g(x), so that for each point (x, y) on part of the curve, one has y = g(x). An example is the unit circle, whose points satisfy x^2 + y^2 = 1, which can locally be solved by y = sqrt(1 - x^2), expressing the top semicircle as a graph. It is not always possible to solve the equation for y algebraically, and the implicit function theorem gives analytic conditions under which there exists a function g whose graph belongs to the given curve, and, in some formulations, also gives a way of constructing approximations to g.","status":"verified_replacement"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.247859+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_76391ba9f312cc4e9d91aedd80277f0f6372f1ad10d69428d886dff6c036560b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:applied-excess-conc of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j$ be a sufficiently large positive integer.  Fix an integer $\tau \ge 0$ and a real number $\nu\ge 0$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_j$ be independent binomial random variables, 
and for each $i\in [j]$
let $m_i = \mathbb{E}(A_i)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.219408+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7663636cd1e0dfa30578941f7c7e6f97c365af33ac796736a45470b15303a539","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:spectral-structure of arXiv:2607.05693, 'Free multiplicative convolution and Erlang moments in monitored quantum transport'] The limiting law $\mu_\tau$ has an atom at $1$ of mass
\[
  \mu_\tau(\{1\})=(1-\tau)_+.
\]
Consequently, the mass away from the atom at $1$ is $\min\{1,\tau\}$. Moreover,
the Stieltjes-transform equation has a real branch point at
\[
  x_*(\tau)=\tau \mathrm{e}^{1-\tau}.
\]
At $\tau=1$ this branch point reaches $1$, precisely where the atom at $1$
disappears.

\begin{remark}
Beenakker [Beenakker2501] computes the $\tau=1$ moments for the
\emph{orthogonal} version of the model, in which
$Q_N=\prod_{n=1}^N\bigl(I-u^{(n)}(u^{(n)})^\top\bigr)$ is a product of $N$
real rank-$(N-1)$ projectors, and obtains
\[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Tr(Q_NQ_N^\top)^p\bigr]
  =\frac{(p/\mathrm{e})^p}{p!}.
\]
This agrees exactly with the law identified here: setting $\tau=1$ in
(equation eq:moment-formula of the paper) and using $G_p(1)=p^{p-1}$ (a short induction,
or Cayley's formula for the number of labelled rooted trees on $p$
vertices) gives
\[
  m_p(1)=\mathrm{e}^{-p}\frac{p^{p-1}}{(p-1)!}
  =\mathrm{e}^{-p}\frac{p^p}{p!}
  =\frac{(p/\mathrm{e})^p}{p!}.
\]
Our rigorous results are stated for the complex (unitary) ensemble, whereas
Beenakker's computation is for the real (orthogonal) one; the two limiting
moment sequences coincide because the leading-order free limit does not
depend on the symmetry class, the difference appearing only in the $1/N$
corrections. Beenakker further notes, following a question of Bulatov, that
at $\tau=1$ the squared singular values are \emph{approximately} distributed
as $\mathrm{e}^{-\pi X^2}$ with $X$ standard normal, and asks for a direct
explanation. The measure $\mu_1$ identified here is the exact limiting law:
the approximate Gaussian form is its Stirling approximation, with the factor
$\pi$ originating from Stirling's constant in
$(p-1)!\sim\sqrt{2\pi p}\,(p/\mathrm{e})^{p-1}$.
\end{remark} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:56:49.285532+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7664c648bde9d0f4fa2006ba0b3ef2f6099ff7fe0ef540d61d4f68dcdbd042ca","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 11 (Majority rule) of arXiv:2606.22960, '2606.22960'] Let \((T_n,(B_v)_{v\in[n]})\) be the broadcast-coloured tree of size \(n\), where

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.828777+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_766d044176fd2e4c0c0de75ac184d02abc15cb5eef47db3efe6a8e3b8a38f695","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01} and 
that the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}. 
Then, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$, there exists a Borel probability measure $\wt \nu_{\wt b}$ on $\wt B$ such that, for any continuous 
function $\varphi$ on $\wt B$, we have 
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}  P_{\mu}^k \varphi(\wt b) 
=  \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}  \bb E \varphi(g_k \cdots g_1 \wt b)

\end{align*}
Moreover, this convergence holds uniformly over $\wt b \in \wt B$, and we have the following harmonicity property: for any $\wt b \in \wt B$, 
\begin{align*}
\wt \nu_{\wt b} = \int_G \wt \nu_{g \wt b} \mu(dg). 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.161069+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_76804a3a87c48929c68daf05e6e3d2decc6088f5077b4716f90e77a58e30b1b8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 9 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1 > 0$ and $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, we have $S_\star(\lambda,\mu) \subseteq S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_1)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:36:23.147496+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7704284e0fcaa577127086a3f257c2befa721bec4c43be82be076962c6aa3bdd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:bipartite of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1]$. Let $G^{(n)}$ be a sequence of bipartite graphs on $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for the same $\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$. Then, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, the binary noisy voter model on $G^{(n)}$ with noise $\theta$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}}(\varepsilon) = \frac{1+o(1)}{\min\{4-2\theta,4\theta\}}\log n\,,

\]
thus $\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}$ is the asymptotically fastest initial condition on $G^{(n)}$. In particular, for Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}_n$ (the case $G^{(n)}=\mathbb{Z}_n$) at any inverse temperature $\beta>0$, the alternating initial condition $\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}$ is the asymptotically fastest initial condition. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:58:24.517485+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7705c43eb63198ec74f754b5e6e5d52f598ef4d5d482adc600311aca8bca9f5c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem t:joint.sum.max.star of arXiv:2601.12677, 'Stable and Fréchet limit theorem for subgraph functionals in the hyperbolic random geometr'] $(i)$ If $\frac{1}{2} (k-1)<\alpha< k-1$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
\begin{align}
&\left( \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n\cdot\,]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) - [N_n\cdot\,]  \mathbb{E} [\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_1)] \bigg), \ \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}\bigvee_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot \,]} \mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i)\right)  \Rightarrow (S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot),\, Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot)),   
\end{align}
in the space $D\big([0,1], {\mathbb R} \times [0,\infty)\big)$ of right-continuous functions from $[0,1]$ to ${\mathbb R}\times [0,\infty)$ with left limits. The weak limit in (equation e:weak.conv.join.sum.max.star of the paper) is defined by the hybrid characteristic–distribution function
\begin{equation}  
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{ivS_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t)} {\mathbf 1} \{ Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t) \le z \} \big] = t\int_0^z e^{ivy} g(v,y)^t e^{-ty^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}} \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif y),  \  \ v\in {\mathbb R},\,  z\ge 0,  
\end{equation}
where
$$
g(v,y) := \exp \Big\{ \int_0^\infty \big( (e^{ivx}-1){\mathbf 1} \{ x<y \} -ivx \big) \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif x)\Big\}, 
$$
and $\mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a Radon measure on $(0,\infty]$ satisfying $\mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}\big((y,\infty]\big)=y^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}$ for $y>0$. \\
Marginally, $S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a zero-mean $2\alpha/(k-1)$-stable L\'evy process whose characteristic function is given by (equation e:chf.first.comp.zero.mean.stable of the paper) below. Furthermore, $Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is an extremal $2\alpha/(k-1)$-Fr\'echet process; that is, for $0\equiv t_0<t_1<\cdots <t_m<\infty$ and $z_i\ge0$, $i=1,\dots,m$, 
$$
\mathbb{P}\big( Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t_i)\le z_i, \, i=1,\dots,m \big)=\exp \Big\{ -\sum_{j=1}^m (t_j-t_{j-1}) (z_j \wedge \cdots \wedge z_m)^{-2\alpha/(k-1)} \Big\}. 
$$
$(ii)$ If $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<\frac{1}{2} (k-1)$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
$$
\left( \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}  \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot\, ]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i), \ \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \bigvee_{i=1}^{[N_n \cdot \,]} \mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) \right)  \Rightarrow (\widetilde{S}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot), Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(\cdot)), \ \ \text{in } D\big( [0,1], [0,\infty)^2\big), 
$$
where the weak limit is defined by 
\begin{equation}  
\mathbb{E} \big[ e^{iv\widetilde{S}_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t)} {\mathbf 1} \{ Y_{2\alpha/(k-1)}(t) \le z \} \big] = t\int_0^z e^{ivy} \, \widetilde{g}(v,y)^t e^{-ty^{-2\alpha/(k-1)}} \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif y),  \ \ \ v\in {\mathbb R},\,  z\ge 0,  
\end{equation}
with 
$$
\widetilde{g}(v,y) := \exp \Big\{ \int_0^y (e^{ivx}-1) \mathsf{m}_{2\alpha/(k-1)} (\dif x)\Big\}. 
$$
Marginally, $\widetilde S_{2\alpha/(k-1)}$ is a $2\alpha/(k-1)$-stable subordinator (i.e., a stable L\'evy process with increasing paths) with its characteristic function given by (equation e:chf.first.comp.zero.stable.subordinator of the paper) below. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:45:27.977670+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7716321ff6de0969ba7144f6fe87b838b1edf749750c9f7f75a0a1fe3273e5ba","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:periodic-marked-winding-bridge-limit of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume \(d>2\) and let \(N_L/V_L\to\rho>\rho_{\mathrm c}\). 
Then the finite-volume periodic marked Feynman cycle process

mass $\rho-\rho_{\mathrm c}$ with length-dependent mark measure \(\eta_x\) given by
(equation eq:periodic-limiting-eta of the paper).  More precisely, before conditioning on the
total macroscopic mass, the limiting tilted Poisson intensity is
$ du\,e^{-s x}dx/x\,\eta_x(dm)$,

Let
$ \bigl(X_{L,i},U_{L,i},R_{L,i},Y_{L,i},\zeta_{L,i}\bigr)_{i\ge1}$

  \bigl(X_i,U_i,R_i,Y_i,\zeta_i\bigr)_{1\le i\le m}.

The limiting ranked lengths satisfy
$ (X_i)_{i\ge1}
  \sim
  (\rho-\rho_c)\,{\rm PD}(0,1)$.
Conditionally on \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\), the marks are independent and, for each
\(i\),
\[
  R_i\sim\mathsf H_{\mathbb T^d},
  \qquad
  Y_i\sim N(0,2\beta X_iI_d),
  \qquad
  \zeta_i\sim \sqrt{2\beta X_i}\,B^{\mathrm{br}}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:01:39.503084+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_77506cfe405be253e6695e7c8cc650b308b02010717284f043886beb76d4a19b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:graph_event_E_reg of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $K^{\mathcal{E}}$ be a large constant. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item  For $k\in \{1, 2\}$ and any distinct $s_1, \dots, s_k\in [n]$ we have
    \[\sum_{1\leq i\leq n} |A_{s_1i}-p|\cdots |A_{s_ki}-p|\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}p^k n, \quad \text{ which implies}\quad

    \item  For $k\in \{1, 2\}$, any interval $I\subseteq [n]$ and any distinct $s_1, \dots, s_k\in [n]$ we have
    \[\Big|\!\sum_{i\in I} (A_{s_1i}-p)\cdots (A_{s_ki}-p)\Big|\!\leq\! K^{\mathcal{E}}\sqrt{p^k n\log n}, \text{ which implies } \Big|\!\sum_{i\in I} \!\!\lambda_{s_1i}\cdots \lambda_{s_ki}\Big|\!\leq \!O(K^{\mathcal{E}}z_p^k \sqrt{p^k n\log n}).\]

    \item  We have $\|A-pJ\|_{op}\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}\sqrt{np}$. If the $n\times n$ matrix $\Lambda$ is defined by $\Lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{ij}$, this also implies $\|\Lambda\|_{op}\leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}}z_p\sqrt{np})$.

{"assumptions":["psi_X is the cumulant generating function of X","E|X| < infinity, so that E X is defined (used only in comparing the one-sided and two-sided transforms)"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T16:00:40+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7751577616946b1cba36dc864f8319107779abefa80121218d0cfaece15cbfec","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let psi_X be the cumulant generating function of a random variable X. The Cramer transform, in the one-sided convention used for upper-tail (Chernoff) bounds, is psi_X^*(t) = sup_{lambda >= 0} (lambda * t - psi_X(lambda)). For t >= E X it equals the Fenchel-Legendre dual (convex conjugate) sup over all real lambda of (lambda * t - psi_X(lambda)), which is Cramer's rate function; for t < E X the one-sided transform is 0, while the conjugate is in general positive (for a standard normal X the conjugate is t^2/2 for every t).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:27:25.791643+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_7754caf2c164aae1fa5a545cc57e36008f3e9a844f3df67d5cc1aa5e1a256641","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem.mathcalY of arXiv:2605.11785, 'Regularization of a mean-field SDE by an additive common noise: the conditional expectatio'] For any $\mu_0\in \mathcal P_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, there exists a unique Borel measurable map $\mathcal Y^{\mu_0}: [0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d\times  {\mathcal C}\to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for any $(t,x,\bm{x})\in [0,T]\times \mathbb{R}^d\times {\mathcal C}$,
