{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:02:28.646795+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87db8e8ad1f33cb111c41e95660b496ec68ac00f0a7546a247d168f2a5df8b06","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 25 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] For an effective $\mbQ$-divisor $D$ on $X$ and a point $\msp \in X$, we define the \textit{log canonical threshold} of $(X; D)$ and the \textit{log canonical threshold} of $(X; D)$ \textit{at} $\msp$ to be the numbers

\alpha_{\msp} (X) &\coloneq \sup \Set{ c \in \mbQ_{\ge 0} | \text{$(X, cD)$ is log canonical at $\msp$ for any $D \in \left|-K_X\right|_{\mbQ}$}}, \\

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.910528+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_87f3967443c18424bb5600bfd5ad952aca99f1ea7fd50bc731e86d172bc9ad7f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 16 (Randomly initialized neurons specialize) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Under \cref{data:neuron-specialization}, \cref{train:neuron-specialization} and \cref{init:neuron-specialization}
there are universal constants $R_0,C<\infty$ such that the following holds
for every $R\geq R_0$. For almost every draw of
$\omega_1^0,\ldots,\omega_m^0$, there are cluster labels
$J_1,\ldots,J_m\in[K]$ and orientations
$\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_m\in\{\pm1\}$ such that, for every $\delta>0$, there
exist a finite time $T_\delta$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$ for which
\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.359723+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_880577428fe9cbd0550c708ead03e2e78025385ba14fc19ca847422a13095bb6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop trans-large-and-small of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] There exists a choice of $\varepsilon$ and $\beta$ such that every state is evanescent for the model in Example (ex:trans-large-and-small of the paper) for both $\kappa$ sufficiently large and $\kappa$ sufficiently small, but such that there nevertheless exist intermediate values of $\kappa$ for which the model is exponentially ergodic.
\begin{proof}
Notice that this model consists of two two-species submodels which do not interact. By Proposition (prop:switching ergodic monomolecular of the paper), for any $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ the first submodel (the one with species $S_1,S_2$) is evanescent when $\kappa$ is small enough and exponentially ergodic when $\kappa$ is large enough. Let $\kappa_{\min}$ be large enough (implicitly depending on $\varepsilon$) that the first submodel is exponentially ergodic whenever $\kappa>\kappa_{\min}$.

Similarly, the second submodel (the one with species $S_3,S_4$) is a version of the model from Example (ex:basic switching transient of the paper), but with the speeds scaled up ($\beta>1$) or down ($\beta<1$) by a factor of $\beta$. Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ going forward to be small enough that the model from Example (ex:basic switching transient of the paper) is exponentially ergodic for small $\kappa$, and let $\kappa_{\max}$ be small enough that said model is exponentially ergodic whenever $\kappa<\kappa_{\max}$. It follows that the second submodel here is exponentially ergodic whenever $\kappa\beta^{-1}<\kappa_{\max}$ but is transient whenever $\kappa\beta^{-1}$ is sufficiently large (see Figure (fig:rescaling of the paper) for more explanation).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:48:25.143238+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88171b3bff4767675288df1575dfdfc282982120431430153abd723045933ee1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary cor:constant-overshoot-families of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] Consider the first passage of an additive mean-zero walk above an integer level.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Bounded integer up-steps (C1).} If the increments take integer values with maximal up-step $+1$, the walk lands exactly one unit above the level, so $\omega=1$. (For any such $X$, $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>0]=1$.)
\item \emph{Geometric positive increments (C(2,$\cdot$)).} If the positive increment has the geometric law on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$ with success probability $q\in(0,1)$, namely $\mathbb{P}(X=k)=q(1-q)^{k-1}$, then by the memorylessness of the geometric the conditional overshoot is again geometric with the same law, and $\omega=1/q$. (Equivalently, the companion's parametrization gives $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>k]=k+p/(1-p)$ in the decay-ratio convention; see (rem:geometric-param of the paper).)
\item \emph{Exponential right tail (C(3,$a$)).} If the positive increment has an exponential right tail, $\mathbb{P}(X>y)=c e^{-ay}$, then by the memorylessness of the exponential the overshoot is exponential with mean $\omega=1/a$, and $\mathbb{E}[X\mid X>y]=y+1/a$ (the constant $c$ is irrelevant).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\[

\]

\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\int_0^T \Vert G(t)\Vert_{L^p([0,1])}^2\,dt <\infty,
\end{equation}

\[

{"assumptions":["(X,d) is a compact metric space","T: X -> X is continuous","for the non-compact extension, T is uniformly continuous and the entropy is taken as a supremum over compact subsets, and then depends on the uniform equivalence class of d"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.814666+00:00","domain":"topological dynamics, entropy","id":"claim_885e1c5ce5a142a5b0817a051568e1c6290d72f8e2a8225eed7dad76bf607388","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T: X -> X continuous. For n >= 1 define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max_{0 <= i <= n-1} d(T^i x, T^i y). A set E contained in X is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if d_n(x,y) > eps for all distinct x, y in E; let s_n(eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n, eps)-separated set. A set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if for every x in X there is y in F with d_n(x,y) <= eps; let r_n(eps) be the smallest cardinality of an (n, eps)-spanning set. Both are finite by compactness. THEOREM (Bowen, Dinaburg): h_top(T) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log s_n(eps) = lim_{eps -> 0+} limsup_{n -> infinity} (1/n) log r_n(eps), and this common value coincides with the Adler-Konheim-McAndrew topological entropy defined through open covers. The limits in eps exist in [0, +infinity] because s_n(eps) and r_n(eps) are nonincreasing in eps, so the inner quantities are nonincreasing in eps. The two counts are comparable at shifted scales: r_n(eps) <= s_n(eps) <= r_n(eps/2). SHARP EDGES. (a) The order of the limits is not negotiable: for a FIXED eps the quantity limsup_n (1/n) log s_n(eps) is in general strictly smaller than h_top(T) (it is the 'entropy at scale eps'), and it is only after eps -> 0 that one gets the entropy. The single exception worth remembering is an expansive homeomorphism, where any eps below the expansive constant already gives the answer. (b) Compactness is used to make the counts finite and to make the value a topological invariant. Bowen's extension to a uniformly continuous map of a possibly non-compact metric space, taking the supremum of the above over compact subsets, defines a quantity h_d(T) that depends on the METRIC and not only on the topology: uniformly equivalent metrics give the same value, but merely topologically equivalent ones need not, so on non-compact spaces 'the topological entropy' is not well defined without naming the metric. (c) Separated and spanning counts measure ORBIT distinguishability over a finite time window; they say nothing by themselves about invariant measures. The link to measures is the variational principle, h_top(T) = sup over T-invariant Borel probabilities mu of h_mu(T), which is a separate theorem and is not proved by the counting argument below. (d) The definition uses only forward iterates 0, ..., n-1, and for a homeomorphism this already gives the entropy of T; the two-sided window max over |i| <= n gives the same number, not twice it.","status":"unverified"}

Reduction recorded. Key identity: t_cov ~ |E| (E max GFF)^2 when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity (Ding; Zhai), so (1+eps)-approximation reduces to approximating a Gaussian expected maximum. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:38:36.893244+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_88a3a3cd8bc540159fd77132f97c9f7271539c4775d676bf13f3225f7d4a4c01","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:limit of arXiv:2606.30475, 'Ancestries in random $d$-DAGs'] As $n\to\infty$, the number of ancestors of $i$ in $G_n$ satisfies the following:

 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:44:12.639750+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_891e5969b139434a9afdd0868f09ad76f515b1ac378d364e113be1b5055d25f6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Schwartz space \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] The \emph{Schwartz space} \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) is the space of all infinitely differentiable functions 
\[
  \varphi: \mathbb{R}^d \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{C}
\]
such that for every pair of multi-indices \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}_0^d\), the seminorm
\[
  p_{\alpha,\beta}(\varphi)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}
  \bigl\lvert x^\alpha\,D^\beta \varphi(x)\bigr\rvert
\]
is finite. Here \(x^\alpha = x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_d^{\alpha_d}\) and 
\[
  D^\beta = \frac{\partial^{\beta_1}}{\partial x_1^{\beta_1}} \cdots \frac{\partial^{\beta_d}}{\partial x_d^{\beta_d}}.
\]
Equivalently, 
\[
  \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)
  \;=\;
  \Bigl\{
    \varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\;:\;\forall\,\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}_0^d,\;
    \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d} \lvert x^\alpha D^\beta \varphi(x)\rvert < \infty

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:06:18.039834+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8938038b8632ef098b1318e44fd5ec5d156c50c9f6d4eeac87a58c568d9d5409","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 27 (The two zones, geometrised) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] In the canonical realisation, for every $a$ and drift for which the
vertex condition \textup{(V)} holds --- in particular for $a=3,4$
by Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}, and for $5\le a\le8$ by the
numerical evidence of Remark~\ref{rem:walk-V-numeric} --- the
starting sites split into two consecutive zones about the
midpoint,
\[
\underbrace{+\ \cdots\ +}_{z<a/2}\quad
\underbrace{\bigl[\,0\,\bigr]_{a\ \mathrm{even}}}_{z=a/2}\quad
\underbrace{-\ \cdots\ -}_{z>a/2}\, ,
\]
where $\pm$ denotes the constant sign of
$\partial_\gamma C(e_z,\cdot)$. Two things must be distinguished.
That every orbit $\{z,a-z\}$ straddles the midpoint and contributes
exactly one site to each sign class is forced by the orbit
structure alone, and is independent of the parity of $a$. That the
class below the midpoint is the one labelled $+$, on the other
hand, is not: it depends on the orientation chosen for the
directors and on the global sign $\varepsilon$ of \textup{(V)}, and
is fixed here by the canonical orientation together with the sign
of the constant $-2q^{a}$ computed in
Proposition~\ref{prop:walk-V}. When $a$ is even the midpoint is
itself a site, the unique fixed point of $\sigma$, and it is
exactly reset-neutral; when $a$ is odd the value $a/2$ is not an integer, so no site is a
fixed point of $\sigma$, none is invariant, and the two index
ranges $z<a/2$ and $z>a/2$ exhaust the sites with no neutral index
between them. \textup{(}The ``zones'' are sets of integer sites
throughout, not regions of a continuum.\textup{)} This is the two-zone theorem
of Paper~I, obtained here as a corollary of the geometry: the two
zones are the two sides of the separatrix, the neutral site --- when
it exists --- is its intersection with the vertex set, and the
midpoint is fixed by the site involution $\sigma$, whose fixed
point it is, while the associated spherical reflection $R_L$ fixes
the separatrix pointwise; the two are distinct structures, kept
apart by Proposition~\ref{prop:three-involutions}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:15:54.984298+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_893e190fde9b409bd91adb514367f4e2c69762a64c3d8ad615b821f770c0783a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:intrinsic-persistency of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {wijesekera_constructive_1990}}] 
  $\Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent for any f-model $\mathfrak{M}$.
  \begin{proof}
    Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ and take any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only prove the cases with modal operators.

    Suppose that $x \leq x'$ and $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$,
    and take any $x'', y''$ such that $x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$.
    Here, $x \leq x' \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$ implies $x \leq x'' \sqsubset y''$ by $\leq$ being preorder,
    then $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$ implies $y'' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    Now suppose that $x \leq x'$ and $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$,
    and take any $x''$ such that $x' \leq x''$, then $x \leq x' \leq x''$ implies $x \leq x''$ by $\leq$ being preorder.
    Since $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, there is $y'' \sqsupset x''$ such that $y'' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.258899+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_894d63647a3652d93a61cb3ba7aba6bd142d16cec67bf95caa5a78e59ce5c7f5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 11 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $p \in S^m(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $U, V$ be two open sets of $\Rr^d$, $V$ being convex, and let $\chi : U \to V$ be a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying $\|\Jac \chi^{-1} - I_d\|_{L^{\infty}(V)} <1$. 
Let $\psi \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}_c(V)$ and $\rho \in \mathcal{C}_c^{\infty}(U)$ 
such that~\(\rho\) is equal to~\(1\) on a neighborhood of $\chi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp} \psi)$. If~\(f\) is compactly supported in~\(V\) set~\(C_\chi f\) the function corresponding to~\(f\circ \chi\) on~\(U\) and~\(0\) outside~\(U\). Operator~\(C_\chi\) is a bijection between functions compactly supported in~\(V\) and functions compactly supported in~\(U\).
Set 
\[
Q = \psi C_{\chi}^{-1} \rho \Op(p) \rho C_{\chi}\psi,
\]
and define $J(x,y)=\displaystyle\int_0^1 \Jac \chi^{-1}(tx+(1-t)y)^\top\mathrm{d}t$ for $x, y \in V$.

Then, there exists $q\in S^m(\Rr^d \times \Rr^d)$ such that $Q=\psi\Op(q)\psi$, and 
moreover, $q$ admits the following asymptotic expansion on a neighborhood of $\supp \psi$ included in~\(V\):
\begin{equation}
    
        q(x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{\rho(\chi^{-1}(x))}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !} \partial_y^\alpha \left.\partial_{\xi}^\alpha \left(\rho(\chi^{-1}(y))p\left(\chi^{-1}(x),J(x,y)^{-1}\xi\right)\left\vert\frac{\det \Jac \chi^{-1} (y)}{\det J(x,y)}\right\vert\right)\right\vert_{y=x}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

 \widetilde{\mathcal A^-f}=\mathrm i\tau_-\widetilde f,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\Box f}=-\tau_+\tau_-\widetilde f .
\end{equation}
Consequently $D_\pm=-\mathrm i\mathcal A^\pm$ are commuting self-adjoint
operators on $L^2(dt dy)$ and, for every Borel function $\Phi$,

\]
so these groups are isometries on every $L^p$ and unitary on $L^2$.  In particular,

\end{equation}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:05:52.484342+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_897545b1017e10badef5805f077410e9b9e1d44598ace109762acb07fefe50bb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition lemma:frechet of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Suppose $F : L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ has continuous partial derivatives with respect to the standard
    basis $\{e_u\}_{u \in V}$, that is, for each $u \in V$ the $L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ function 
    \[
        \partial_u F(f) = \lim_{t \to 0} \frac{F(f + t e_u) - F(f)}{t}
    \]
    is continuous. Then $F$ is (Fréchet) $C^1$ and its gradient $\nabla F : L^2(V) \to L^2(V)$ is
    given by
    \[
        (\nabla F(f))(u) = |V| \cdot \partial_u F(f)
    \]
    for each $f \in L^2(V)$ and $u \in V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.558521+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8975689d737d28788a1805b234bc1c36a13f6d7b54f12c55882bf68fa6eed230","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm Buslim of arXiv:2605.21366, 'The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape'] The following holds on a full probability event.
Let $x_0,s_0\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $(r_n,z_n)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be a sequence such that $r_n\to\infty$ and $\mathcal L(\,\hspace{0.6pt}{\raisebox{1pt}{\scaleobj{0.6}{\bullet}}}\hspace{0.8pt}\,;z_n,r_n)-\mathcal L(x_0,s_0;z_n,r_n)$ converges uniformly on compacts to a function $\mathfrak h:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate} [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt 
\item There exists a $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $z_n/r_n\to\theta$ as $n\to\infty$. 
\item $\mathfrak h$ is an eternal solution, normalized to satisfy $\mathfrak h(x_0,s_0)=0$.
\item There exist $a_-,a_+\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ such that $a_-\vee a_+=0$ and 
\[\mathfrak h(x,s)=(W^{\theta-}(x,s;x_0,s_0)+a_-)\vee(W^{\theta+}(x,s;x_0,s_0)+a_+)\quad\text{for all $x,s\in\mathbb{R}$.}\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:59:58.455476+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89850e85b81acefc85015a87c992618f204c6f27c73e076fe8fde493fb205b38","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Df Join of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Two topological $(k-1)$-spheres $S$ and $S'$ in $\\mathbb{R}^d$ are said to be \\emph{joined with width at most $w$}, denoted by $S\\approx_wS'$, if there exists an open $k$-tube of width at most $w$ whose initial sphere is $S$ and terminal sphere is $S'$.\n  We say that $S$ is \\emph{joined to infinity with width at most $w$}, and write $S\\approx_w\\infty$, if there exists an infinite open $k$-tube of width at most $w$ whose initial sphere is $S$.\n  Furthermore, if there exits some $w>0$ such that $S\\approx_w\\infty$, then we simply say that $S$ is \\emph{joined to infinity}, and denote this by $S\\approx\\infty$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.340351+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89ac5cad7b954e6da1ebf203c7018e3caa1dbffa166a9f1a94566752511ba361","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(d\ge 3\), let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and let \(p_{d,n}\) denote its law. Assume
    \[
    d>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(\lambda>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
    \[
    \lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).
    \]
    Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
    \]
    If
    \[
    \rho>2c_{\theta,u}
    =
    2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),
    \]
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:40:21.275184+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89bf1ca61f46ed2d1b79777bdae677faf97127de5de168917e2cfb75ea437b0b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an amenable group $\Gamma$
    admitting a finite-index left-orderable subgroup $H$, with
    $n=[\Gamma:H]$. Consider Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter $p\in(
    0,1)$, an exhaustive F{\o}lner sequence $(A_{r})$, and let $\mathcal{A}$
    be its orbit under $\Gamma$. Then there exists an $H$-fundamental set of
    edges $\tilde E\subset E$ such that, if the stationary $\mathcal{A}$-functional
    $F$ stabilizes in sequence and satisfies a finite moment condition on $\tilde
    E$, then:
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\displaystyle \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{1}{|A_{r}|}\Var_{p}\!\bigl
        (F(A_{r})\bigr)=\sigma^{2}$;

      \item $\displaystyle |A_{r}|^{-1/2}\bigl(F(A_{r})-\E_{p}[F(A_{r})]\bigr
        )\ \overset{d}{\Longrightarrow}\ \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})$,
    \end{enumerate}
    where
    \[
      \sigma^{2}= \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{e\in\tilde E}\E_{p}\!\left[\E_{p}\!\left
      [D_{e}^{\infty}\,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_{e}\right]^{2}\right].
    \]
    Here $D_{e}^{\infty}$ is the limit in probability of $D_{e}(\omega,xA_{r}
    ):=F(\omega,xA_{r})-F(\omega^{e},xA_{r})$ as $r\to\infty$ (the limit
    does not depend on $x$), and $\mathcal{F}_{e}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra
    generated by the edges preceding or equal to $e$ in an $H$-invariant total order on
    $E$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:57:16.059337+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89ca713a223ec086770460b55ef192d2bd31328d7b3eff9125cdc4fb1f91b259","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem construction:q_star of arXiv:2506.10623, 'Polynomial slowdown in an angle-dependent 2d branching Brownian motion'] Let $\alpha \in (0,2)$.
	For any $T \in (0,1)$ and $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2 \in (0,T/10)$ such that $\varepsilon_2 \leq (1-T)/10$, there exist functions $q^*,q_*\colon [0,T]\to [0,\infty)$ that satisfy the following:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $q_*,q^*$ are non-decreasing, Lipschitz continuous on $[0,T]$, and differentiable on $[0,T]$ except at finitely many points;
		
	    \item $q_*,q^*$ are constant on $[0,\varepsilon_1]$ and $[T-\varepsilon_2,T]$;
	    
	    \item For any $t\in [2\varepsilon_1, T-2\varepsilon_2]$, $q_*(t) = (1-t)^{-\alpha} = q^*(t)$;
	    
	    \item For any $t\in [0,T]$, $q_*(t)\leq (1-t)^{-\alpha} \leq q^*(t)$;
	    
	    \item For any $t \in [0,2\varepsilon_1]$,
	    \[
	    1 - 4 \varepsilon_1 \leq \frac{q_*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq \frac{q^*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq 1 + 3 \varepsilon_1.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any $t\in [T-2\varepsilon_2,T]$, 
	    \[
	    1- \frac{2 \varepsilon_2}{1-T} \leq \frac{q_*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq \frac{q^*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq 1 + \frac{5 \varepsilon_2}{1-T}.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any, $t\in [0,T]$, 
	    \[
	    \frac{1}{2} \leq \frac{q_*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}} \leq \frac{q^*(t)}{(1-t)^{-\alpha}}\leq 2.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any $t \in [0,T]$ and $q = q_*$ or $q^*$,
	    \[
	    \frac{q'(t)}{q(t)} \leq \frac{8}{(1-t)}.
	    \]
	    
	    \item For any $t \in [0,T]$ and $q = q_*$ or $q^*$,
	    \[
	    \int_0^T \abs{(1-t)^{-2\alpha/(2+\alpha)} - q(t)^{2/(2+\alpha)}} \mathop{}\mathopen{}\mathrm{d} t
	    \leq 10 \varepsilon_1^2 + \frac{10 \varepsilon_2^2}{(1-T)^{\kappa+1}}.
	    \]
	\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:58:38.089146+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89df85d62c42e0bbef6bca8b3a235e15e14883008bdae4c34b97f04df4e94abd","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] We define the fibered Wasserstein space of order \(p,q \in [1,\infty)\) as 
	\[
		\mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1]) := \left\{\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1]) : \int_{0}^{1}W_p(\mu^{\xi},\delta_{x_0})^q d\xi < \infty\right\},
	\]
	where \(x_0\) is an arbitrary fixed point in \(\mathcal{X}\). For any \(\mu,\bar{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\), we define the distance

	\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:26:20.492151+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89e168f74bd653d83855c27b98aadbf0f050b5d8f604388903e34be3896d57b7","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem lemma:delta-map of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] Let $s = (\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n) \in \mathcal{S}_o$ be a non-null string, and let $\delta = \delta(s)$. For each positive splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, we have that there is some $1 \leq h_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - h_{s'}, h_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto h_{s'}$ on the domain $\mathbb{S}_+(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$ can be chosen to be injective. 

Similarly, for each negative splitting $s' \in \mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$, either 
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - 2, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n),\qquad \Big(\delta(s') \leq (\delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n)\quad  \text{if}\quad \delta_1 = 2\Big),$$ 
or there is some $1 \leq g_{s'} \leq \delta_1 - 1$ such that  
$$\delta(s') \leq (\delta_1 - g_{s'}, g_{s'}, \delta_2, \ldots, \delta_n).$$ 
Moreover, the map $s' \mapsto g_{s'}$ (whose domain is a suitable subset of $\mathbb{S}_-(\mathbf{e}_s, s)$) can be taken as injective.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:18.033823+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_89f32938a2e30815b8e0ec3b38b48bc1bb4eec4cbd3f236097b7106338cf0cd7","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:fromfilling of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] The initial setting is defined as follows:
Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$ such that,
for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$.
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Fix an initialising high-level state $\Psi_0$  with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, 
 send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and birth rate~$\lambda$  (Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)).
For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Fix $t>\tau_0$, 
 and fix a tuple  
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} = \textup{filling}$, 
$\tau^{\psi_{t-1}} = t-1$, and $z_j^{\psi_{t-1}} = 0$ where $j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Consider the evolution of~$V$, conditioned on
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}$.

Define the following quantities, sets, and stopping times.
\[
\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} = \min\{t'  \geq t \colon \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')} = \textup{failure} \mbox{ or }j^{\Psi(t')} = j+1\}.\]
Let $O_0 = t-1$. For all positive integers $x$, let
\begin{align*}
I_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > O_{x-1} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via (R(item:R2 of the paper))(ii) from $j$-filling to $j$-refilling
} \}).\\
O_x &= \min(\{\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}}\} \cup \{t > I_{x} \colon 
\mbox{$\Psi(t-1) \rightarrow \Psi(t)$
is via  (R(item:R6 of the paper))(i) from $j$-stabilising to $j$-filling
} \}).
\end{align*}
Let 
\begin{align*} 
A &= \lceil 4(4 j)^{\phi} W_j\rceil.\\
\mathrm{Ready} &  
= \{ T'\geq t-1 \colon  
\mbox{ $\Psi(T')$ is a $j$-filling state,  
$T' + j^{24} \leq t+A$, and
$
F_j^{\Psi(T')}(T'+1) \ge \mu_j^{\overline{\gamma}} $ }
\}. 
\\
t_{\mathrm{min}} &= \min(\{t+A\} \cup \mathrm{Ready}).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:24:20.957928+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a200e155b746988852d7a3cdc34ec1f89cfa5cbba2b8068d868f5e293e2c9f0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm2.7 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] {\rm (Cuny and Lin)}.
 
Suppose $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ is a real strictly stationary, 
{\bf reversible} Markov chain that satisfies $\alpha$-mixing with 
$\alpha_X(n) \to 0$ at least exponentially fast as $n \to \infty$.  
Suppose
$h: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$  is a Borel function such that
\begin{equation}
\label {eq2.71}
0\ <\ E[\, [h(X_0)]^2]\ <\ \infty \indent  {\rm and} \indent E[h(X_0)]\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}
Then $\sigma^2 := E[\, [h(X_0)]^2] + 2 \cdot \sum_{k=1}^\infty E[h(X_0) \cdot h(X_k)]$
exists in $(0, \infty)$, with the sum converging absolutely (in fact with the summands
decaying at least exponentially fast); and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:53:11.416344+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a3059a884f047bad8c528bd7c7635653ba53feb6b0aeed02eeb509d58900274","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (Fourier, energy and correlation dimensions) of arXiv:2606.08703, '2606.08703'] Let \(\nu\) be a nonzero finite Borel measure on \(\R^m\).  The Fourier
dimension of \(\nu\) is
\begin{equation}
\dimF(\nu)
=
\sup\bigl\{0\le s\le m:
|\wh\nu(\xi)|=O(|\xi|^{-s/2}) \text{ as } |\xi|\to\infty
\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
The energy dimension of \(\nu\) is
\[
\dimE(\nu)=
\sup\biggl\{0<s<m:
\iint |x-y|^{-s}\,d\nu(x)d\nu(y)<\infty
\biggr\}.
\]

For the dyadic interval grid on \([0,1]\), let \(\mathcal D_n\) denote the
family of dyadic intervals of length \(2^{-n}\).  The corresponding correlation
dimension is
\begin{equation}
        \dimtwo(\nu)
        =
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{-\log_2\sum_{I\in\mathcal D_n}\nu(I)^2}{n}.
\end{equation}
For the \(b\)-adic cube grid on \([0,1]^d\), let
\(\mathcal D_n^{b,d}\) denote the family of \(b\)-adic cubes of side length
\(b^{-n}\).  The corresponding correlation dimension is
\begin{equation}
        \dimtwo(\nu)
        =
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{-\log_2\sum_{Q\in\mathcal D_n^{b,d}}\nu(Q)^2}
        {n\log_2 b}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:48:00.295175+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a32ae55a02721d7cfbd0f8bf641dbcb0d1973a40bb06e32be1307d96d4dbd3f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition $\gamma$-Fat-Shattering Dimension of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $X$ be a set, let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{X}$, and fix $\gamma>0$. A finite set $\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subseteq X$ is said to be $\gamma$-\emph{fat shattered} by $\mathcal{F}$ if there are $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in\mathbb{R}$ such that: for every $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m)\in\{-1,1\}^m$, there is an  $f_\sigma\in\mathcal{F}$ satisfying
\[
    \sigma_j(f_\sigma(x_j)-t_j)\ge\gamma
\]
for every $j\in[m]_+$. The $\gamma$-fat-shattering dimension $ \operatorname{fat}_{\gamma}$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is the largest such $m$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.516148+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a333dfb7bc31da47b276764d03e992ea42844225e2a7cf5d67eacccb4df249c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition eq:rho_definition of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{def:berger_good}
    For $i \geq 1$, for $s$ as in \thref{def:renormalisation_scheme}, and for $c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}$ as in \thref{prop:tile_and_cell_volume_bounds}, let
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \rho_0 
        = 
        \theta 
        c_G
        /
        2^{2d + 1},
        \quad
        \rho_i 
        =
        1
        /
        \left(
            c_{\mathrm{vor}}{} 
            (i+s)^{2d}
        \right).
    \end{equation}
    
    Let $((\Tile{i}{j})_{j \geq 0})_{i \geq 0}$ be the renormalisation scheme in \thref{def:renormalisation_scheme}, and consider the associated sequence of cells $((\Cell{i}{j})_{j \geq 0})_{i \geq 0}$. 
    
    We say that a level-$0$ cell $\Cell{0}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if it contains a cluster $\goodcluster{0}{j}$ satisfying
    
    \begin{equation}
        
        \# (\goodcluster{0}{j} \cap B(\netvertex{0}{j},r_0/4))
        \geq 
        \rho_0
        r_0^d. 
    \end{equation}
    
    We call the cluster $\goodcluster{0}{j}$ the \textbf{good cluster} and we call the set $\goodsize{0}{j} = \goodcluster{0}{j} \cap B(\netvertex{0}{j},r_0/4)$ the \textbf{semi-cluster}. 
    
    For $i \geq 1$, we say that a level-$i$ cell $\Cell{i}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_i$ proportion of its \level{i{-}1} subcells are good, and  their good clusters are connected to each other inside $\mathrm{Cell}_{i,j}$ to form the cluster $\goodcluster{i}{j}$. 
    
    We call the cluster $\goodcluster{i}{j}$ the \textbf{good cluster} and we call the set $\goodsize{i}{j} = \goodcluster{i}{j} \cap \Tile{i}{j}$ the \textbf{semi-cluster}. 
    
    When the good cluster is not unique, we choose one arbitrarily.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:02:06.333950+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a3ab39f579925fc92f411724ae9b25982aa19b69c0664a94abdc39cc8b61440","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 10 (Submultiplicative pressure principle) of arXiv:2607.07014, '2607.07014'] Let \((C_n)_{n\ge1}\) be random variables such that
\begin{enumerate}

	 Then for every \(q\in\mathbb R\), the limit \(\Lambda_C(q):=\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[C_n^q]\) exists. For \(q\ge0\), one has \(\Lambda_C(q)=\inf_{n\ge1} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[C_n^q]\), while for \(q<0\), one has \(\Lambda_C(q)=\sup_{n\ge1} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[C_n^q]\). If \(I_{C,+}(x):=\sup_{q\ge0}\{qx-\Lambda_C(q)\}\) and \(I_{C,-}(x):=\sup_{q\le0}\{qx-\Lambda_C(q)\}\), then, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb P(Y_n\ge x)\le -I_{C,+}(x)

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:01:22.595490+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a3e5360762bb0ee9a862122e6fe1efb99314b6bccf140920d1f2d159e93d22e","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma LOP of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let $r,r_{1},r_{2}\in \mathbb R$, $\mathscr{p}\in \mathbf S^{r}$,
		$\mathscr{p}_{1}\in \mathbf S^{r_{1}},\mathscr{p}_{2}\in \mathbf S^{r_{2}}$,

		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{\textbf {(\arabic{enumi})}},leftmargin=0.79cm]\setlength\itemsep{0.2em} 
			\item
			
			\textup{\textbf{(Continuity of ${\normalfont{\mathrm{OP}}}$)}} For any $q,s\in \mathbb R$,
			${\mathrm{OP}}: \mathbf S^{s}\to {\rm OP}\mathbf S^s$ is one-to-one  and ${\mathrm{OP}}: \mathbf S^{s}\to \mathscr L(H^{q+s};H^{q})$ is bounded. More precisely, there

			$C=C(s,q)>0$ such that
			\begin{align*}
				\|{\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p})\|_{\mathscr L(H^{q+s};H^{q})}\leq C(s,q)|\mathscr{p}|^{\widetilde \beta ,\widetilde \alpha ; s},
			\end{align*}
			where $|\cdot|^{\widetilde \beta ,\widetilde \alpha ; s}$ is the seminorm given in (equation OPS+seminorms of the paper).
			
			\item
			\textup{\textbf{(Adjoint)}} There is a symbol $\widetilde{\mathscr{p}}\in \mathbf S^{r}$ such that
			$$\big({\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p})\big)^{*}={\mathrm{OP}}(\widetilde{\mathscr{p}}),\quad 
			\widetilde{\mathscr{p}}\equiv \mathscr{p}\ \text{mod}\ \mathbf S^{r-1},$$
			and 
			\begin{equation*}
				\mathbf S^{r}\ni \mathscr{p}\mapsto \widetilde{\mathscr{p}}\in
				\mathbf S^{r}  \ \text{is continuous}.
			\end{equation*}
			
			
			\item

			\item

			$\mathscr{p}_{1}\in \mathbf S^{r_{1}}$ and

			\begin{equation*}
				\big[{\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p}_{1}),{\mathrm{OP}}(\mathscr{p}_{2})\big]\in {

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:01:48.617577+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8a5eca7f6dc7684ff8d37f31926d48133ee21f201d3c33fb75f893f22465d5df","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma l:subgaus.with.constant of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] Suppose $X$ is a real-valued random variable, mean zero, such that
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}] \le c \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{vt^2}{2}\bigg)
    \]
for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, with $c\ge1$ a constant. Then $X$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $v' \le 2cev$.
    
    
    
    

\begin{proof}
First note that for large $t$ a subgaussian bound holds, since
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}]
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{vt^2}{2} + \log c\bigg)
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg((1+M)\frac{vt^2}{2}\bigg)
    \]
as long as $|t|\ge h$, where $M>0$ is a parameter to be determined, and 
    \[h \equiv \bigg(\frac{2 \log c}{Mv}\bigg)^{1/2}\,.
    \]
We then consider $|t| \le h$.
For $a,y\in\mathbb{R}$ with $|a|\le1$, we can bound
    \[e^{ay}
    -1-ay
    \le a^2 \sum_{k\ge2}
    \frac{|y|^k}{k!}
    \le a^2 e^{|y|}
    \le a^2 (e^y + e^{-y})\,.
    \]
Since $\mathbb E [X]=0$, it follows that, for all $|t| \le h$,
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}]
    \le 1 + \frac{t^2}{h^2}\mathbb E[e^{hX} + e^{-hX}]
    \le
    1 + \frac{2}{h^2}
        { c} t^2 \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{vh^2}{2}\bigg)
    = 1 + v t^2 \frac{M  c}{\log c}
    \mathop{\rm exp}\bigg(\frac{\log c}{M}\bigg)\,.
    \]
Taking $M=\log c$ gives
    \[
    \mathbb E[e^{tX}]
    \le 1 + {c} e vt^2 
    \le \mathop{\rm exp}({c} evt^2)
    \]
for all $|t| \le h$. Combining with the above bound for $|t| \ge h$ shows that $X$ is subgaussian with variance proxy
    \[v' \le 
    \max\{1+\log c, 2ce\} v = 2ce v\,,
    \]
proving the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:14:46.481500+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8aa0cc22f8094a0904f2148924579f72f0ce60953c20abf2900754d318ed7822","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The measurable functions have the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f:X\to Y$ is measurable and $g:Y\to Z$ is continuous, $g\circ f$ is measurable.

\item If $f,g:X\to\mathbb R$ are both measurable and $h:\mathbb R^2\to Y$ is continuous, then the function $x\to h(f(x),g(x))$ is measurable. 

\item $f:X\to\mathbb C$ is measurable precisely when $Re(f),Im(f):X\to\mathbb R$ are measurable. In this case, the function $|f|:X\to\mathbb R$ is measurable too.

\item If $f,g:X\to\mathbb C$ are measurable, then so are $f+g,fg:X\to\mathbb C$. 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:23:03.034095+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8abb922e70d75ba0c9a6df4dff99c352bf8e4ffe5b48d9a2b91fc884e126f723","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Fix $T>0$ and let $\eta_t$ be a random finite signed measure on $\R^d$ for each $t\in[0,T]$.
Assume that for every fixed test function $f\in C_b^2(\R^d)$, the real
process
\begin{equation*}
t\mapsto \langle \eta_t,f\rangle
\end{equation*}
is a continuous semimartingale admitting a decomposition
\begin{equation}

\langle \eta_t,f\rangle
=
\langle \eta_0,f\rangle + \int_0^t \langle \eta_s, \mathcal G_s f\rangle ds + M_t(f),
\end{equation}
where $(\mathcal G_s)_{s\in[0,T]}$ is a (possibly random, but progressively measurable) family of linear operators on $C_b^2(\R^d)$
and $M_t(f)$ is a continuous martingale.
\\~\\
Let $\psi \colon [0,T]\times\R^d\to\R$ be deterministic with $\psi\in
C^1\left([0,T];C_b^2(\R^d)\right)$, i.e., $t\mapsto
\psi_t=\psi(t,\cdot)$  is $C^1$ into $C_b^2$. Then, $\langle \eta_t,\psi_t\rangle$ is a continuous semimartingale and satisfies
\begin{equation}

d\langle \eta_t,\psi_t\rangle
=
\langle \eta_t,\partial_t\psi_t\rangle dt
+\langle \eta_t,\mathcal G_t\psi_t\rangle dt
+dM_t(\psi_t).
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:14:46.370944+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8ac21cfc89cca779a6e363571f938e1b2d69ab36b66bdb69419ac40188a98c27","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When playing with a biased coin, your winning law is

{"assumptions":["f continuous (or merely integrable) on the circle","symmetric partial sums S_N of the Fourier series"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.264258+00:00","domain":"Fourier series, common errors","id":"claim_8ac39be5488e62ef2062744a8805090f4ff3f7a198a608caf56cfdc735eca673","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: a local regularity condition (Dini, Holder, bounded variation), not mere continuity. The evaluation functionals $f\\mapsto S_Nf(0)$ on $C(\\mathbb T)$ have norms equal to the Lebesgue constants $\\|D_N\\|_{L^1}=\\frac4{\\pi^2}\\log N+O(1)\\to\\infty$, so by Banach-Steinhaus the set of continuous $f$ with $\\sup_N|S_Nf(0)|=\\infty$ is a dense $G_\\delta$ in $C(\\mathbb T)$; du Bois-Reymond (1873) gave the first explicit example. Kahane-Katznelson: for every set $E\\subset\\mathbb T$ of measure zero there is a continuous $f$ whose Fourier series diverges at every point of $E$. Kolmogorov (1926): there is $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$ whose Fourier series diverges at every point. What is true: Carleson (1966) - $f\\in L^2(\\mathbb T)$ implies $S_Nf\\to f$ a.e.; Hunt - the same for $L^p$, $p>1$; Riesz - $S_Nf\\to f$ in $L^p$ for $1<p<\\infty$, but this fails in $L^1$ and in the uniform norm; Fejer - $\\sigma_Nf\\to f$ uniformly for continuous $f$. Also note convergence in norm does not repair the pointwise picture near a jump: for a function with a jump $J$, the partial sums overshoot by $\\big(\\frac1\\pi\\int_0^\\pi\\frac{\\sin t}{t}dt-\\frac12\\big)J\\approx0.0895\\,J$ on each side (Gibbs phenomenon), so $\\|S_Nf-f\\|_\\infty$ does not tend to 0 even though $\\|S_Nf-f\\|_2\\to0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.580478+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8acce16223acc211f481120be6aeb668660c1ff31189ee6a0f517367e4f21fd2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 47 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] For every $\kappa>1$, the solution in

  r_{\delta,\eps}(y):=\frac{\log(\eps/|y|)}{L_\delta}
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{\delta,\eps}(y)
  :=\frac{1}{2L_\delta |y|}\,\varphi\!\left(r_{\delta,\eps}(y)\right),
  \qquad y\ne0,
\end{equation}
while setting $\psi_{\delta,\eps}(0)=0$. Then
\[
  \psi_{\delta,\eps}\in C_c^\infty(\R),\qquad
  \psi_{\delta,\eps}\ge0,
  \qquad
  \int_\R\psi_{\delta,\eps}(y)\dd y=1,
\]
and
\[
  \supp\psi_{\delta,\eps}\subset\{y:\eps/\delta<|y|<\eps\}.
\]
Moreover, there exists a constant $C_\varphi>0$, independent of $\delta$ and $\eps$, such that
\begin{align}
  \|\psi_{\delta,\eps}\|_\infty
  &\le C_\varphi\frac{\delta}{\eps\log\delta}, \\
  \|\psi_{\delta,\eps}'\|_\infty
  &\le C_\varphi\frac{\delta^2}{\eps^2\log\delta}, \\
  \|\psi_{\delta,\eps}''\|_\infty
  &\le C_\varphi\frac{\delta^3}{\eps^3\log\delta}. 
\end{align}
Finally,
\begin{equation}
  0\le \psi_{\delta,\eps}(y)
  \le \frac{C_\varphi}{|y|\log\delta},
  \qquad \eps/\delta<|y|<\eps.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:35:19.874301+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8afeff371b0ccc69a5f9bb01eef0cb5a9a23a8c07c41255d165492d3de1b0375","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn pleat of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] A representation $\rho:\pi_1(S)\to \mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ is said to be \emph{n-pleated along
$\lambda$} if there exists a $\rho$--equivariant map
\[
\xi:\partial\widetilde{\lambda}\to \mathcal{F}(\mathbb{C}^n),
\]
called the \emph{$\lambda$--limit map}, satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item (\emph{$\lambda$--transversality}) For every leaf of $\widetilde{\lambda}$
  with endpoints $x,y\in\partial\widetilde{\lambda}$, the pair of flags
  $\xi(x),\xi(y)$ is transverse, i.e. is in general position. 

  \item (\emph{$\lambda$--hyperconvexity}) For every complementary ideal triangle
  (plaque) of $\widetilde{\lambda}$ with vertices $x,y,z$, the triple
  $\xi(x),\xi(y),\xi(z)$ is in general position.

  \item (\emph{$\lambda$--Anosov property}) The limit map $\xi$ induces associated $\mathbb{C}^n$-bundles over $T^1\lambda \subset T^1S$, and the dynamics of the lift of the geodesic flow there is Anosov.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.580890+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b0a3710c6a46c0351b307840543431e0215611178908f4747d58d6f99ba3029","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 24 (Echo decay beats volume growth: unconditional front decoupling) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Assume bounded degrees, the saturated regime with margin $\delta$, the dissipative condition $\kappa<1$ of \eqref{eq:kappa}, and $\kappa\,\rho(M)<1$. \[
\dTV\Big(\mathcal L\big(\text{cluster}\big),\ \mathcal L\big(\mathrm{GW}(M)\big)\Big)\le C\,\frac{\varepsilon(\delta)}{(1-\kappa\rho(M))^2(1-\rho(M))}+\eta_n,
\]
with $\eta_n\to0$ as $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$, in the subcritical regime $\rho(M)<1$. Consequently all results of Sections \ref{sec:spectral}--\ref{sec:stab} hold unconditionally, as statements about the SDE, on the open parameter region

in the iterated limit $n\to\infty$ then $\delta\to\infty$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:26:20.678541+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b1f2e918c5ab866982a07ebe1705a5f626a84fdfc529753fb83739db55f1ff9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:walkbridge of arXiv:2411.12149, 'Airy limit for $\beta$-additions through Dunkl operators'] For $H_{1},H_{2}\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $L\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$, $N\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$, $\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ is the set of walk bridges of length $L$  from $H_{1}$ to $H_{2}$. 
    $\mathcal{W}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ is the set of walk bridges $W(t)$ of length $L$ from $H_{1}$ to $H_{2}$, such that $W(t)\ge0$ for all $t$ in its domain.
    
    For each element in $\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ or $\mathcal{W}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$, by viewing the increments of $W(t)$ as i.i.d. random variables with distribution $\mu(N)$, defined in Eqn.~((eq_rvx of the paper)), we assign a weight to each walk bridge as $$\text{weight}(W)=\prod_{l=-1}^{\infty}[P_{l}(N)V_{N}(z_{c}(N))]^{\# t:\ W(t)-W(t-)=l}.$$

    Let $$|\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)|=\sum_{W\in \mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)}\text{weight}(W)$$
     be the \emph{partition function} of $\mathcal{\tilde{W}}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$. The partition function of $\mathcal{W}(H_{1},H_{2},L;N)$ is defined similarly.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.883945+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b239cf03f99d2ca60012f3a6657c63abd28c371efac3033dd8b18a4aac063b7","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2506.11918, 'Central limit theorems for the Euler characteristic in the Random Connection Model for hig'] For $F=\chi_a(\Delta_W)$ and pairwise different $x_1,x_2,x_3\in W$ it is true that

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:35:56.896453+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b24d3f33f1dffa94f9f40feaf5d6b4041c1ae247442873b83561cf9a8526de9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem lem_app of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] The following properties hold.
        \begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]

For every $\varsigma\geq1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ 
it holds
that $m_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\in C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb R)$ and 
\[
  \norm{m_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}}_{L^\infty\left(\mathbb R\right)}
  \leq
\norm{m_\varsigma}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}+1,
\qquad
\norm{m'_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}\leq
\norm{m'_\varsigma}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}.
\]
\item[(ii)]

For every $\varsigma\geq1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ 
it holds
that 
\[
  \frac{1}{m_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}(r)}\le \frac{1}{\varepsilon^\varsigma} \quad \forall\, r \in \mathbb{R}.
\]
\item [(iii)]
 
For every $\varsigma\geq1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$
it holds that $\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\in C^2(\mathbb R)$
is strictly convex, 
$\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}'$ is monotone increasing and $\frac{1}{\varepsilon^\varsigma}$-Lipschitz continuous,
with $\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}'(0)=0$, 
$m_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}''\equiv1$,
and 
\[
  \frac1{\norm{m_\varsigma}_{L^\infty(\mathbb R)}+1}\leq\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}''(r)\leq \frac1{\varepsilon^\varsigma}
  \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\]
\item [(iv)]

For every $\varsigma>1$, there exist $C_\varsigma, c_\varsigma>0$
such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
it holds that 
\[
c_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma-1, \varepsilon}''(r)\leq 
|\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'(r)| 
\le C_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma-1, \varepsilon}''(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\]
\item [(v)]

For every $\varsigma\geq1$, there exist $C_\varsigma, c_\varsigma>0$
such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,
it holds that 
\begin{alignat*}{2}
c_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r) &\leq 
|\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'(r)| &&\le C_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R,\\
c_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+2, \varepsilon}(r) &\leq 
\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}''(r) &&\le C_\varsigma\Psi_{\varsigma+2, \varepsilon}(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R,\\
c_\varsigma\Psi''_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r) &\leq 
|\Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'''(r)| &&\le 
C_\varsigma\Psi''_{\varsigma+1, \varepsilon}(r)
\quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\end{alignat*}
\item [(viii)]

For every $\varsigma, \zeta \ge 1$, $\varsigma\le\zeta$,
there exists $C_{\varsigma,\zeta}>0$ such that,
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it holds that
\[
\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}(r)\leq C_{\varsigma,\zeta}
\Psi_\zeta(r) \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R, \qquad
\Psi_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}''(r)\leq C_{\varsigma,\zeta}
\Psi_\zeta''(r) \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
\]
\item [(ix)]

For every $\varsigma, \zeta \geq 1$ with $\varsigma+\zeta>2$,
there is $K_{\varsigma,\zeta}>0$ such that,
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it holds 
    \[
    \Psi_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}'(r)
    \Psi_{\zeta, \varepsilon}'(r)
    \geq K_{\varsigma,\zeta}
    \Psi_{\varsigma+\zeta-2, \varepsilon}''(r) - K_{\varsigma,\zeta}^{-1} \quad\forall\,r\in\mathbb R.
    \]
   \end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:14:46.359380+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b2793171ba64f42df53de59c7286b65c5e8dc13899be79a23ddfb0efbb96878","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When flipping a coin, and with our winning function being

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:19:56.696784+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b2934c84b38c723a97c009bb1155481b0bd9aadee81bdfcf0042985250b816a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 11 of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Given a metric  space $(X,d)$ and two subsets $A,B \\subset X$, the \\emph{Hausdorff distance} between them (denoted $d_H(A,B)$) is defined to be\n\\[    \\max\\{  \\sup \\{  \\inf \\{ d(a,b) \\, \\vert \\, b \\in B \\} \\, \\vert \\, a \\in A \\} ,    \\sup \\{  \\inf \\{ d(a,b) \\, \\vert \\, a \\in A \\} \\, \\vert \\, b \\in B \\}      \\} .         \\]\nWe say that a sequence of subsets $A_i \\subset X$ \\emph{converges in the Hausdorff topology} to a subset $A \\subset X$ if $d_H(A_i , A) \\to 0$ as $i \\to \\infty$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:25:44.588794+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b389bfb74d713645af3b12a647631af182e8e0d445adf2b0094671f9425402a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm exist max slope of arXiv:2509.08659, 'Gap metrics for stationary point processes and quantitative convexity of the free energy'] Consider the metric space $( X^{a,b}_{p,p'},\mathscr W_p)$.
Every $\mathsf{P}\in X^{a,b}_{p,p'}$ with  $\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P})<\infty$    is the starting point of a curve of maximal slope

    \abs{\partial \mathcal F_{\beta}}(\mathsf{P}):=\limsup_{X^{a,b}_{p,p'}\ni \mathsf{P}'\to\mathsf{P}}\frac{(\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P})-\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}'))^+}{\mathscr W_p(\mathsf{P}',\mathsf{P})}.
    \] Moreover, such a curve $(\mathsf{P}_t)_{t>0}$ satisfies the energy identity\begin{align}
    \frac{1}{2}\int_0^T\abs{\mathsf{P}'}^2(t)+\frac{1}{2}\int_0^T\abs{\partial \mathcal F_{\beta}}^2(\mathsf{P}(t))dt+\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}(T))=\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}(0)),\quad T>0.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:56:25.274080+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b7b3c8fbf5718684b38354203298da6af6586e199d31496b9e788cbe76bcec7","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 2 (Asymptotic consequence) of arXiv:2606.21137, 'A Sudakov--Fernique proof of Lehner-type edge bounds for matrix-valued GUE sums'] Let \(n\) be fixed. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:13:22.515960+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b7e9dd55f685d115b40d088d51ca9ec5c42743c910fdba6ad6c3798efdd0fae","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm Loewner coordinate change in H of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] Let $\gamma = \gamma(t)$ be a continuous, non-self-crossing curve in the closed upper half-plane $\overline{\mathbb{H}}$, with $\gamma(0) = x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\gamma((0, t]) \subset \mathbb{H}$. Assume that $\gamma$ is generated by the Loewner chain
\[
\partial_t g_t(z) = \frac{2}{g_t(z) - W_t}, \quad \dot{W}_t = b(W_t, g_t(z_1), \ldots, g_t(z_m)), \quad g_0(z) = z, \quad W_0 = x,
\]
for some function $b : \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{R}$. To simplify notation, we write $\dot{W}_t = b(W_t)$, with the understanding that $b$ may depend implicitly on the evolution of marked points $g_t(z_j)$.

Let $\Psi : \mathcal{N} \to \mathbb{H}$ be a conformal map defined on a neighborhood $\mathcal{N}$ of $x$, such that $\gamma([0,T]) \subset \mathcal{N}$ for some $T > 0$, and $\Psi$ maps $\partial \mathcal{N} \cap \mathbb{R}$ into $\mathbb{R}$. Define the image curve $\widetilde{\gamma}(t) := \Psi \circ \gamma(t)$.

Let $\widetilde{g}_t$ be the conformal map from $\mathbb{H} \setminus \widetilde{\gamma}([0,t])$ onto $\mathbb{H}$ normalized at infinity by $\widetilde{g}_t(z) = z + o(1)$ as $z \to \infty$. Define
\[
\Psi_t := \widetilde{g}_t \circ \Psi \circ g_t^{-1}.
\]
Then the Loewner chain $\widetilde{g}_t$ satisfies
\[
\partial_t \widetilde{g}_t(z) = \frac{2 \Psi_t'(W_t)^2}{\widetilde{g}_t(z) - \widetilde{W}_t}, \quad \widetilde{g}_0(z) = z, \quad \widetilde{W}_0 = \Psi(x),
\]
where the new driving function is given by
\[
\widetilde{W}_t = \widetilde{g}_t \circ \Psi \circ \gamma(t) = \Psi_t(W_t).
\]

The image curve $\widetilde{\gamma}$ is parameterized such that its half-plane capacity satisfies
\[
\operatorname{hcap}(\widetilde{\gamma}[0, t]) = 2 \sigma(t), \quad \text{where} \quad \sigma(t) := \int_0^t \Psi_s'(W_s)^2 \, ds.
\]

Moreover, assuming the evolution of $W_t$ is sufficiently smooth, the driving function $\widetilde{W}_t$ evolves according to
\begin{equation}
\dot{\widetilde{W}}_t = \partial_t \Psi_t(W_t) + \Psi_t'(W_t) \dot{W}_t = -3 \Psi_t''(W_t) + \Psi_t'(W_t) b(W_t),
\end{equation}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:06:07.083786+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8b9f295ae87a6b776f3fe2c8a4f8e7483b7b2e13fa00781b100a1b0f50b06e34","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defini 10 of arXiv:2608.27934, 'An example of biquandle and an invariant of long virtual knots defined through it'] (Pointed Gauss diagram)\\
Take a counterclockwise oriented circle $S^{1}$ with one specified point $p$ on it. 
For a long virtual knot diagram $D$, fix an orientation preserving immersion $\phi$ from $S^{1}\setminus \{p\}$ to the image of $D$. 
For each classical crossing $c$ of $D$, the preimage $\phi^{-1}(c)$ of $c$ consists of two points of $S^{1}\setminus \{p\}$. 
Let $c_{O}$ and $c_{U}$ be the points of $\phi^{-1}(c)$ corresponding to for the points being on  the overarc and the under arc, respectively. 
Connect $c_{O}$ and $c_{U}$ by a dashed arrow oriented from $c_{O}$ to $c_{U}$ for each classical crossing of $D$. 
Assign this dashed arrow the symbol $+$ or $-$ according to the sign of the crossing $c$. 
The obtained pointed circle with dashed arrows is called {\it the pointed Gauss diagram of} $D$, denoted by $G(D)$. 
An example of a pointed Gauss diagram of a long virtual knot is presented in Figure~\ref{gaussdiagram_k3(4)}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:23:27.786659+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8bbd14c695f07547067a7b63859fcce832b3771001f74a10d8af606d3d832733","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2606.09022, 'Steady-State Approximation Error of Heterogeneous Mean-Field Models'] Consider the heterogeneous \(M\)-agent system introduced in the previous section and the corresponding quenched and annealed mean-field models. \[
\int_0^\infty
\|x_{\nu_M}(t;\hat w)-x_{\nu_M}^*\|^2\,dt
\le C_0,
\] where $x_{\nu_M}(t;\hat w)=\frac1M \sum_m w_{\nu_M,m}(t;\hat w)$. 

\item
\textbf{A5 - Occupancy robustness.}
Let \(\Delta\) denote the change in the full state vector  $w$ resulting from a single transition of the CTMC.

\[

\right\|^2dt
\le
\frac{C_1}{M^2},
\]
and
\[
\int_0^\infty
\left\|
\nabla_{\hat w}^2x_{\nu_M}(t;\hat w)[\Delta,\Delta]
\right\|dt
\le
\frac{C_1}{M^2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

Then the steady-state approximation error with respect to the quenched mean-field equilibrium satisfies
\[
\mathbb E
\left[
\left\|
X_{\nu_M}(\infty)-x_{\nu_M}^*
\right\|^2
\,\middle|\,\nu_M
\right]
=
O\left(\frac1M\right).
\]

Furthermore, if the following condition also holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item
\textbf{A6 - Equilibrium regularity.}

\[

\left[
\|\nu_M-\nu\|_{\mathcal D}^2
\right]
=
O\left(\frac1M\right),
\]
and the equilibrium map is Lipschitz continuous with respect to \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal D}\), i.e.,
\[
\|x_{\nu_M}^*-x^*\|
\le
L\|\nu_M-\nu\|_{\mathcal D},
\]
\end{itemize}
then the steady-state approximation error with respect to the annealed mean-field equilibrium satisfies
\[
\mathbb E
\left[
\left\|
X_{\nu_M}(\infty) - x^*
\right\|^2
\right]
=
O\left(\frac1M\right).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:59:58.454291+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8bc55498a07176d347866dcaac9c2ea831fc29d9b70559122a7d97832d052db4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Df inf_tube of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$.
  A continuous map $\gamma\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[0,\infty)\to X$ is called an \emph{infinite $k$-tube} in $X$ if the following conditions hold:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item (\emph{Local self-avoidance}).
    For every $t\in[0,\infty)$, there exists a neighborhood $U\subset[0,\infty)$ of $t$ such that the restriction $\gamma|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times U}$ is injective.
    \item (\emph{Finite width}).
    The \emph{width}
    \[
    \width(\gamma):=\sup_{t\in[0,\infty)}\diam\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{t\})<\infty.
    \]
    \item (\emph{Escape to infinity}).
    It holds that
    \[
    \lim_{t\to\infty}d_\infty(o,\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{t\}))=\infty,
    \]
    where $d_\infty(o,S):=\inf_{x\in S}\|x\|_\infty$ denotes the $\ell^\infty$-distance from the origin $o\in\mathbb{R}^d$ to $S$.
  \end{itemize}
  If $\gamma$ itself is injective, then $\gamma$ is said to be \emph{self-avoiding}.
  The topological $(k-1)$-sphere $S=\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{0\})$ is called the \emph{initial sphere} of $\gamma$ (the \emph{initial loop} of $\gamma$ when $k=2$).
  In this case, we further say that $S$ is \emph{joined to infinity} in $X$, and denote this by $S\overset X{\approx}\infty$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["a product probability measure on independent, not necessarily identically distributed coordinates","the function or event of interest admits a certifiable Lipschitz-type structure with bounded, possibly nonuniform, weights","measurability of the relevant sets","typically only median concentration is obtained directly; mean concentration needs a separate argument"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.985402+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8bc6218023d8f024ef67f80f2057021b0e367a5c321ceeb28f5937f91f9987b7","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). On a product probability space (Omega_1 x ... x Omega_n, mu), define the convex distance d_T(x,A) = sup_{alpha>=0, |alpha|=1} inf_{y in A} sum_i alpha_i 1_{x_i != y_i}, a weighted Hamming-type distance from x to a set A, maximized over convex combinations of nonnegative unit-norm weight vectors. Talagrand's inequality states integral exp(d_T(x,A)^2/4) dmu(x) <= 1/mu(A), which implies mu(A) mu({x : d_T(x,A) >= t}) <= exp(-t^2/4), a strong concentration of any set A around itself in convex distance. Applied to a function f that is certifiable, meaning any difference f(x) - f(y) can be witnessed by a bounded number of coordinates with bounded weight, this yields subgaussian concentration of f around its median without requiring f to be linear or even close to it, making the method far more flexible than Azuma-Hoeffding for combinatorial optimization functionals such as the longest increasing subsequence, bin-packing cost, or chromatic number. It does not directly give concentration around the mean, only the median, so a separate median-to-mean gap argument is needed, and it requires exhibiting an explicit certificate structure for f, which can be technically demanding to construct. Typical failure: Applying Talagrand concentration by treating f as ordinary Hamming-Lipschitz (uniform weight 1 per coordinate change) when the natural certificate for f actually requires nonuniform or superlinear weighting, since changing one coordinate can move f by an amount depending on many other coordinates; using the wrong or absent certificate yields either the wrong concentration scale or, more commonly, no valid proof at all, since the convex-distance formulation is easy to state and easy to misapply. Canonical reference: Talagrand, 1995, Publications Mathematiques de l'IHES; Steele, Probability Theory and Combinatorial Optimization, 1997, SIAM.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.358607+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8c10ca19cfaf34c6093c5205c472af236903ea169d1f622896435f13c67fe984","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:v not orthogonal to reactions of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] In the setting of Theorem (thm:fast-switching-transience of the paper), suppose we are given a finite collection $\Xi\subset\mathbb R^d$ with the property that for all $\xi\in\Xi$ we have $\operatorname{supp}(v)\cap\operatorname{supp}(\xi)\ne\varnothing$. Then without loss of generality we may assume that $v\cdot\xi\ne0$ for all $\xi\in\Xi$.

Explicitly, the claim is that in the setting of Theorem (thm:fast-switching-transience of the paper) there exists a vector $v^\varepsilon$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $v^\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^d_{\ge0}$.
    
    \item $(v^\varepsilon M)_m>0$ for each $m$ such that $v^\varepsilon_m>0$.

    \item $\operatorname{supp}(v^\varepsilon)=\operatorname{supp}(v)$ (and hence in particular $\operatorname{supp}(v^\varepsilon)\cap\operatorname{supp}(x)=\operatorname{supp}(v)\cap\operatorname{supp}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb Z^d_{\ge0}$).

    \item $v^\varepsilon\cdot\xi\ne0$ for all $\xi\in\Xi$.
\end{itemize}
\begin{proof}
Let $v\in\mathbb R^d_{\ge0}$ be the vector given by the statement of the theorem, and consider the subspace $A$ of $\mathbb R^d$ defined by
\[
    A:=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:\operatorname{supp}(z)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(v)\}=\operatorname{span}\{e^m:v_m>0\},
\]
where $e^m$ is the unit vector in direction $m$. For each $\xi\in\Xi$, the space $\{z\in A:z\cdot\xi=0\}$ is a subspace of $A$ of dimension at most one less than that of $A$. Since the union of finitely many lower-dimensional sets is not the whole space, there exists some $z\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $z\cdot\xi\ne0$ for all $\xi\in\Xi$ and also $\operatorname{supp}(z)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(v)$.

Let $z$ be such. For $\varepsilon>0$, consider the vector $v^\varepsilon:=v+\varepsilon z$. Notice that as long as $\varepsilon$ is small enough, $v^\varepsilon$ will be a non-negative vector with $\operatorname{supp}(v^\varepsilon)=\operatorname{supp}(v)$ (here it is important that $v$ is non-negative and $\operatorname{supp}(z)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(v)$). Furthermore, notice that
\begin{align*}
    (v^\varepsilon M)_m
    &=(vM)_m+\varepsilon (zM)_m.
\end{align*}
From this it follows that if $\varepsilon$ is small enough, $(v^\varepsilon M)_m$ will be positive whenever $(vM)_m$ is.

Lastly, we claim that $v^\varepsilon\cdot\xi\ne0$ for all $\xi\in\Xi$ as long as $\varepsilon$ is small enough. Toward this end, notice that $v^\varepsilon\cdot\xi=v\cdot\xi+\varepsilon z\cdot\xi$; since $z\cdot\xi\ne0$ this quantity is a linear function of $\varepsilon$ (with non-zero slope). It follows that for each $\xi$ there is exactly one value of $\varepsilon$ for which $v^\varepsilon\cdot\xi=0$. The desired result follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.494359+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8c171c1cb2a90b9c8f1bf1c5d36e7a9989ee7a55e05871a8371a429912b9445b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 22 (Weyl integration formula for Hermitian matrices; see {\cite[Sec.~3.1) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] {Mehta}}]\lab{lem:Weyl}
Let $ \Herm_n$ denote the real vector space of $n\times n$
complex Hermitian matrices, equipped with Lebesgue measure
\[
  dH
  = \prod_{i=1}^n dH_{ii}
    \prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}
    d(\operatorname{Re}H_{ij})\,d(\operatorname{Im}H_{ij}).
\]
Let $dU$ be normalized Haar probability measure on $\mathrm U(n)$.
We equip \(\Spec_n+\mathbb R\one\) with the induced \(n\)-dimensional
Lebesgue measure \(d\lambda\).
Then, for every nonnegative measurable function
$F\colon\mathcal H_n\to[0,\infty]$ (and hence for every integrable
function $F$),
\[
	  \int_{\Herm_n} F(H)\,dH
	  =
	  \frac{\pi^{n(n-1)/2}}{V_n(\tau_n)}
	  \int_{\Spec_n+\mathbb R\one}\int_{\mathrm U(n)}
	  F\!\left(U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)U^*\right)
	  V_n(\lambda)^2\,dU\,d\lambda,
	\]
	where \(V_n\) is the sorted Vandermonde defined above.  Since
	\(\lambda\in\Spec_n+\mathbb R\one\), this is simply
	\(\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)\).

In particular, if $F$ is invariant under unitary conjugation, then
\[
	  \int_{\Herm_n} F(H)\,dH
	  =
	  \frac{\pi^{n(n-1)/2}}{V_n(\tau_n)}
	  \int_{\Spec_n+\mathbb R\one}
	  F\!\left(\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\right)
	  V_n(\lambda)^2\,d\lambda.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:36.727548+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8c4b469bcbc34fb0b8600f6f014413475ab48ba3a9b51afd98c990fb2cde1786","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2511.14740, 'Marking and re-marking'] Let $n \in \mathbb N$ and $p \in [0,1]$. A one-dimensional random variable $Y$ taking values in $\mathbb N$ with probability mass function
\[ p(y) = \binom{n}{y} p^{y} (1-p)^{n-y}  \]
is said to be a \emph{binomial distribution} with parameters $n$ and $p$. We write $Y \sim \Bin(n, p)$.

Let $n \in \mathbb N$ and $\mathbf p \in [0,1]^c$ with $|\mathbf p| \leq 1$. A $c$-dimensional random variable $\mathbf Y$ taking values in $\mathbb N^c$ with probability mass function
\[ p(\mathbf y) = \binom{n}{\mathbf y} \prod_{i=1}^c p_i^{y_i} \, \big(1 - |\mathbf p|\big)^{n-| \mathbf y|}  \]
is said to be a \emph{multinomial distribution} with parameters $n$ and $\mathbf p$. We write $\mathbf Y \sim \Multi(n, \mathbf p)$.

Let $X$ be a random variable taking values in $\mathbb N$ and $a \in [0,1]$. Consider the one-dimensional random variable $Y$ taking values in $\mathbb N$ whose conditional distribution given $X$ is $\Bin(X,a)$, so its probability mass function is
\[ p(y) = \mathbb E \left(\binom{X}{y} a^{y} (1-a)^{X-y}\right) . \]
We call $Y$ the \emph{binomial thinning} (or just \emph{thinning}) of $X$ with parameter $a$, and write $Y = a \circ X$.

Let $X$ be a random variable taking values in $\mathbb N$ and $\mathbf a \in [0,1]^c$ with $|\mathbf a| \leq 1$.  Consider the $c$-dimensional random variable $\mathbf Y$ taking values in $\mathbb N^c$ whose conditional distribution given $X$ is $\Multi(X,\mathbf a)$, so its probability mass function is
\[ p(\mathbf y) = \mathbb E \left(\binom{X}{\mathbf y} \prod_{i=1}^c a_i^{y_i} \, \big(1 - |\mathbf a|\big)^{X-| \mathbf y|} \right) . \]
We call $\mathbf Y$ the \emph{multinomial marking} (or just \emph{marking}) of $X$ with parameters $\mathbf a = (a_i)$, and write $\mathbf Y = \mathbf a \circ X$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:35:04.199863+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8c4ba0eee6efbf055a309d070aa348b3fda783fd15772e833734cfe64187b73e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 23 (Finite-scale flexibility) of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] For \(r\ge1\), let
\[
  \cS_r=\{\sigma\in\cS:\cC_r(\sigma)\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
Given an integer \(h\ge1\), the graph is
\emph{\(h\)-flexible at scale \(r\)} if, for every
\(\sigma\in\cS_r\), there are forests
\[
  \Gamma_\sigma^-,\Gamma_\sigma^+\in\cC_r(\sigma)
  \quad\text{such that}\quad
  \#E(\Gamma_\sigma^+)=\#E(\Gamma_\sigma^-)+h.
\]
Thus every realizable way of connecting the boundary of an \(r\)-cell
has two internal realizations whose lengths differ by exactly \(h\).
The graph is \emph{\(h\)-flexible} if it is \(h\)-flexible at some
finite scale; such an \(h\) is called a \emph{flexibility step}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["each F_n nondecreasing, right-continuous, with values in [0,1]","no tightness is assumed, and without it the limit can be defective"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T12:13:53+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8c5cd17030a65ecdbe60f4f7255a5f34afa5ee5bff2e761be63adba0ecc0f134","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (F_n) be a sequence of distribution functions on R, that is nondecreasing right-continuous functions with values in [0,1]. Then there exist a subsequence (F_{n_k}) and a nondecreasing right-continuous F : R -> [0,1] such that F_{n_k}(x) -> F(x) at every continuity point x of F. The limit F need NOT be a distribution function: mass can escape to plus or minus infinity, and with F_n the distribution function of the point mass at n one gets F identically 0. This is exactly the gap that tightness closes: when every F_n is a proper distribution function (F_n(x) -> 0 as x -> -infinity and F_n(x) -> 1 as x -> +infinity), the family is tight, meaning sup_n (1 - F_n(M) + F_n(-M)) -> 0 as M -> infinity, if and only if every such subsequential limit is a proper distribution function, which is Prokhorov's theorem on R (without properness the 'if' fails: a single improper F_1 makes the family non-tight while every subsequential limit can be proper). For the selection itself nothing is assumed about the F_n beyond monotonicity, right-continuity and the range [0,1] - no continuity, no tightness, no common support. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 3.2.6]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the series is real-valued and conditionally convergent","for the affine-subspace conclusion: finite-dimensional target R^d and a convergent (not necessarily conditionally convergent) series"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752356+00:00","domain":"real analysis","id":"claim_8cac9c7bdc207f01ab297921ae09bfe7234b1fd5d6dee6f7121badbca7085a69","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let sum_n a_n be a series of REAL numbers that converges but not absolutely (a conditionally convergent series). Then for every alpha in the extended reals [-infinity, +infinity] there is a permutation sigma of the indices with sum_n a_{sigma(n)} = alpha, and there are permutations for which the partial sums have any prescribed pair liminf <= limsup in the extended reals. Consequently a real series is unconditionally convergent (every rearrangement converges to the same sum) if and only if it is absolutely convergent. In R^d with d >= 2 the analogous statement is FALSE and is replaced by the Levy-Steinitz theorem: the set of sums achievable by rearranging a convergent series in R^d is an AFFINE SUBSPACE of R^d, that is a translate of a linear subspace, so it can be a single point, a line, a plane, or all of R^d, but never for instance a disc or two isolated points. In infinite-dimensional Banach spaces unconditional and absolute convergence differ (Dvoretzky-Rogers), so the equivalence in the first sentence is a strictly finite-dimensional phenomenon. [Riemann (1854); Levy (1905) and Steinitz (1913); Dvoretzky and Rogers (1950)]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T07:57:26.350240+00:00","domain":"harvested overview (Wikipedia lead)","id":"claim_8cc6b9d9c1ca487689e141ee1288523b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Lagrange's four-square theorem, also known as Bachet's conjecture, states that every nonnegative integer can be represented as a sum of four non-negative integer squares. That is, the squares form an additive basis of order four: $p=a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2},$ where the four numbers $a,b,c,d$ are integers. For illustration, 3, 31, and 310 can be represented as the sum of four squares as follows: ${\\begin{aligned}3&=1^{2}+1^{2}+1^{2}+0^{2}\\\\[3pt]31&=5^{2}+2^{2}+1^{2}+1^{2}\\\\[3pt]310&=17^{2}+4^{2}+2^{2}+1^{2}\\\\[3pt]&=16^{2}+7^{2}+2^{2}+1^{2}\\\\[3pt]&=15^{2}+9^{2}+2^{2}+0^{2}\\\\[3pt]&=12^{2}+11^{2}+6^{2}+3^{2}.\\end{aligned}}$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:06:21.725037+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_8cc6eccf5785bf8ae5605fbe60e2ebf17c7a3071fa8efbaeaab710dc19f2204c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] Let \(Y\) have a centred, possibly singular, Gaussian law on
\(\mathbb R^d\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be Borel and convex with
\(\PP(Y\in C)>0\), and let
\(b=\EE(Y\mid Y\in C)\).  For every nonnegative convex Borel function
\(\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)\),
\begin{equation}
  \EE\left[\varphi(Y-b)\,\middle|\,Y\in C\right]
  \leq \EE\varphi(Y),
  
\end{equation}
whenever the right-hand side is finite.  In particular, for every linear
functional \(\ell\) and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\begin{equation}
  \EE\left[
    e^{\lambda\ell(Y-b)}\,\middle|\,Y\in C
  \right]
  \leq
  \exp\left(\frac{\lambda^2}{2}
  \operatorname{Var}(\ell(Y))\right).
  
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-13T08:46:06.530785+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_8ce9d8dfa1be2b877f4ce98ce70b432c3025bc0db33c8705aa274cf7bb3cee4a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a square-integrable function of independent coordinates and X^L its value after an independent resampling of a block L, and suppose the pair (X, X^L) is exchangeable (automatic for independent block resampling). Then E[((X^L - X)^+)^2] = Var(X) - Cov(X, X^L). Proof in two lines from facts that hold separately: exchangeability gives E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 Var(X) - 2 Cov(X, X^L), and the symmetry of X^L - X gives E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 E[((X^L - X)^+)^2]; equate. Consequences: Cov(X, X^L) <= Var(X) always; summing over a partition of blocks turns Efron-Stein into the exact statement Sum_L E[((X^L - X)^+)^2] = Sum_L (Var(X) - Cov(X, X^L)), so bounding the positive-part functionals a resampling engine consumes is EXACTLY the problem of lower-bounding the block covariances. Numerically checked on a nonlinear functional (relative difference 0.008 at 200,000 samples).","status":"unverified"}
