{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:17.948244+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c762b62130a07ff83f75a496776fa59bc682951707dae65e832a374e046d5f5b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:genbackoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a \emph{send sequence}  
$\overline{p}$, a non-negative integer~$\tau$, and 
a distribution~\newsym{D-cal-0}{birth distribution}{\mathcal{D}} on non-negative integers. 
Fix a (possibly random)
tuple $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau)$ of disjoint sets 
$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau) = (\mathbf{arr}^Z_{1}(\tau),\mathbf{arr}^Z_2(\tau),\ldots)$ where
each $\mathbf{arr}_i^Z(\tau) 
\subseteq \mathcal{B}(\tau)$.
A \emph{generalised backoff process}~\newsym{Z-roman}{generalised backoff process, Definition~(def:genbackoff of the paper)}{Z} with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$,
birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}$, and 
initial population $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau)$ is defined as follows: First,
$\mathbf{b}^Z_0(\tau) = \emptyset$ and,
for all positive integers~$j$,
$\mathbf{b}^Z_j(\tau) = \mathbf{arr}^Z_j(\tau)$.
For each time step~$t>\tau$ and each bin $j\geq 0$, the process has random variables 
\newsym{Bjz-bf}{population of bin~$j$ in~$Z$ just before sends at $t$}{\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t)}, 
\newsym{sjz-bf}{balls that send from $j$ at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)},
\newsym{ejz-bf}{balls that escape from $j$ at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)}, and 
\newsym{bjz-bf}{population of bin~$j$ in~$Z$ just after step $t$}{\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t)} of respective sizes 
\newsym{Bjz}{$|\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t)|$}{B^Z_j(t)}, 
\newsym{sjz}{$|\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t))|$}{s^Z_j(t)}, 
\newsym{ejz}{$|\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)|$}{e^Z_j(t)}, and 
\newsym{bjz}{$|\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t)|$}{b^Z_j(t)}.
By analogy to backoff processes, 
$\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t)$ is the population of bin~$j$ just after step~$t$ in~$Z$, 
$\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t)$ is the population of bin~$j$ just before the sends at step~$t$,
$\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$ is the set of balls that send from bin~$j$ at step~$t$, and $\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)$ is the set of balls that escape from bin~$j$ at step~$t$.
The process evolves as   follows for $t>\tau$.
\begin{itemize}

\item   The quantity \newsym{n-z}{$|n^Z(t)|$}{n^Z(t)} is drawn from~$\mathcal{D}$.  If $n^Z(t) = 0$ then $\mathbf{n}^Z(t) = \emptyset$. Otherwise,
the set 
$\newsym{nz-bf}{set of balls born at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{n}^Z(t)} = \{\mathcal{B}(t,0,1),\ldots,\mathcal{B}(t,0,n^Z(t))\}$.

\item $\mathbf{B}_0^Z(t) = \mathbf{n}^Z(t) \cup \mathbf{b}_0^Z(t-1)$.   
For $j\geq 1$, $\mathbf{B}_j^Z(t) =  \mathbf{b}_j^Z(t-1)$.   

 
\item    
For all $j\geq 0$,  the set $\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$ is formed
by taking each element of $\mathbf{B}_j^Z(t)$ independently with probability~$p_j$. 
$\newsym{sz-bf}{set of balls that send at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{s}^Z(t)} = \cup_{j\geq 0}\ 
\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$
and $\newsym{sz}{$|\mathbf{s}^Z(t)|$}{s^Z(t)} = |\mathbf{s}^Z(t)|$.
 

\item For all $j\geq 0$, 
a random subset $\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)\subseteq \mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$ is drawn from some distribution (to fix a particular generalised backoff process this distribution will be specified).   
 

\item $\mathbf{b}^Z_0(t) = \mathbf{B}^Z_0(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}^Z_0(t)$.

\item Fix a (possibly random) tuple 
$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(t)$ of disjoint sets
$\newsym{arr-bf}{end-of-step arrivals}{\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(t)}  = ( \mathbf{arr}^Z_{1}(t),\mathbf{arr}^Z_2(t),\ldots)$
where each $\mathbf{arr}^Z_i(t) 
\subseteq \mathcal{B}(t)
\setminus  \cup_{k\geq 0} \mathbf{B}^Z_k(t)$. 

  

\item For all $j\geq 1$, 
$\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t) = \mathbf{arr}^Z_j(t) \cup (\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)) \cup 
(\mathbf{s}^Z_{j-1}(t) \setminus \mathbf{e}^Z_{j-1}(t))$.
 
 
\end{itemize}

 

For $t\geq \tau$ we use the notation ${\overline{\mathbf{b}}}^Z(t)$ for the  tuple $(\mathbf{b}_0^Z(t),\mathbf{b}_1^Z(t),\ldots)$
and we use ${\overline{b}}^Z(t)$ for the tuple 
 $(b_0^Z(t),b_1^Z(t),\ldots)$. We define $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}^Z(t) = (\mathrm{arr}_1^Z(t), \mathrm{arr}_2^Z(t),\ldots)$ where $\newsym{arr-roman}{$|\mathbf{arr}^Z_j(t)|$}{\mathrm{arr}^Z_j(t)} = |\mathbf{arr}^Z_j(t)|$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.161307+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c76ff01d24ad4f8093e496a7b8036d62b53cda129bbff51ae8e0f650a7bc1740","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$, 
and for $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
the mapping
$(\lambda,\mu)\mapsto S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$,
is continuous with respect to the Hausdorff metric $d_H$.

\begin{proof} Fix $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$.
Recall the notation \eqref{e:lam.mu.delta.ball}, and suppose
$(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda$ and

\[
    P_{Tz}=P_z-1
    \qquad
    (z\in Z);
\]

\[

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.425148+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c7c9d84c15d51e3f2b3f5f8d8c898c0968444eb9dadf9f8776f20251333d57b5","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The product functor}]
  Fix $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
  Let $(\tau^{(k)})_{k=1}^{N}$ be 
  a sequence of functors.
  The \textit{product functor} $\tau = \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}$ is defined as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$, 
      we set $\tau(S) \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}(S)$.
      We equip $\tau(S)$ with the max product metric (cf.\ (equation 2. eq: max product metric of the paper)).
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      we set $\tau_{f} \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau_{f}^{(k)}$, that is, 
      $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$ is a distance-preserving map given by 
      \begin{equation}
        \tau_{f}\bigl( (a_{k})_{k=1}^{N} \bigr) \coloneqq \bigl( \tau^{(k)}_{f}(a_{k}) \bigr)_{k=1}^{N}.
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(X, mu) and (Y, nu) are sigma-finite measure spaces","F is measurable with respect to the product sigma-algebra","F >= 0 (or the right-hand side is finite when F is complex)","1 <= p < infinity"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.552266+00:00","domain":"real analysis, Lp spaces","id":"claim_c7e6ce33332ca204b69943ebb85d6c5977e07b252cd3daa2dcc9174662d19207","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p < infinity, and F: X x Y -> [0, infinity] measurable for the product sigma-algebra. Then ( int_Y ( int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) )^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} <= int_X ( int_Y F(x,y)^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} dmu(x), both sides in [0, infinity]. Consequently, for complex measurable F with the right-hand side (computed with |F|) finite, int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) converges absolutely for nu-a.e. y and its L^p(nu)-norm is at most the right-hand side. In words: the L^p norm of an integral is at most the integral of the L^p norms. (For p = infinity the analogous statement with ess sup holds for F >= 0.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.537379+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c7ee900cea0acd73eeaf23f4b180209cddf16b77dd46c4192eca17f9254cde1b","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:LG-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.845469+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c81e16d14a6e51fc87da21e030a9ee34388bb31078a04202e7ace736392682c0","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi 15 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] A {\bf Ginibre Brownian motion} of size $N$ is an $\M_N(\C)$-valued diffusion process $Z^N(\cdot)$ of the form
    \[ Z^N(t) \equaldist \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(X^N(t) + \i Y^N(t) ) \]
    where $X^N,Y^N$ are independent Hermitian Brownian motions of size $N$.  Entrywise, this can be described simply: for $1\le i,j\le N$, 
    $\{\sqrt{2N}\,\mathrm{Re}Z_{i,j}^N, \sqrt{2N}\,\mathrm{Im}Z_{i,j}^N\}_{t\ge 0}$ are all independent standard Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}$.

    The random matrix $Z^N(1)$, whose entries are all i.i.d.\ complex normal random variables, is called a {\bf Ginibre Ensemble} first introduced in \cite{Ginibre1965}. Equivalently, the law of $Z$ has a density with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\M_N(\C)$ which is proportional to $Z\mapsto \exp(-N\mathrm{Tr}_N[Z^\ast Z])$.  Note that this density is invariant under $Z\mapsto UZV^\ast$ for any deterministic unitary matrices $U,V\in\mathrm{U}(N)$; thus, the law of the Ginibre ensemble is unitarily bi-invariant.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.492821+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c836ed719a8d442d6f73be266f4d6ec3c61685b613b2c110645479d676120e5a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 5 (Discrete Hessian and the $\De_i$ on $T_n$) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] Let $f: T_n \ra \R$ be a function.
\bit
\item Let $E_0(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_0\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +2, v_2 + 1)\}.$

\item Let $E_1(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_1\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2),  (v_1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +1, v_2 + 1)\}.$ 
\item Let $E_2(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_2\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2+1),  (v_1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +1, v_2 + 2)\}.$ 
\eit

We define the discrete Hessian $\hess(f):E(T_n) \ra \R$ to be a  real-valued function on the set $E(T_n) = E_0(T_n) \cup E_1(T_n) \cup E_2(T_n)$ and the $\De_i$ from $\R^{T_n}$ to $\R^{E_i(T_n)}$ by 
\beq\lab{eq:A}
\hess f(e_0) := \De_0 f(e_0) :=  f(v_1, v_2) - f(v_1 + 1, v_2) - f(v_1 + 1, v_2 + 1) + f(v_1 +2, v_2 + 1).\nonumber\\
\hess f(e_1) := \De_1 f(e_1) :=  - f(v_1, v_2) + f(v_1 + 1, v_2) + f(v_1, v_2 + 1) - f(v_1 + 1,  v_2 + 1).\nonumber\\
\hess f(e_2) := \De_2 f(e_2) :=  f(v_1, v_2) - f(v_1+1, v_2+1) - f(v_1, v_2 + 1) + f(v_1 + 1, v_2 + 2).\nonumber\\
\eeq","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:06:42.721285+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c839fb87ddfbc61c7a1894ba6231d804b2ee562b868699a22d681e3c374f53cf","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi stationary of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] We call $(\\mathcal X_\\omega,\\mathcal E_\\omega,\\sigma_\\omega,\\theta_\\omega)_{\\omega\\in\\Omega}$ \\emph{stationary} if for every $z\\in\\mathbb{Z}^n$ the law of the weighted graph $(\\mathcal X_\\omega,\\mathcal E_\\omega,\\sigma_\\omega,\\theta_\\omega)_{\\omega\\in\\Omega}$ is the same as the law of the translated weighted graph $(\\mathcal X_\\omega+z,\\mathcal E_\\omega+z,\\sigma_\\omega(\\cdot - z),\\theta_\\omega(\\cdot - z))_{\\omega\\in\\Omega}$. We call $(\\mathcal X_\\omega,\\mathcal E_\\omega,\\sigma_\\omega,\\theta_\\omega)_{\\omega\\in\\Omega}$ \\emph{ergodic} if all events $A\\in \\mathcal{A}$ that are invariant under translations in $\\mathbb{Z}^n$ have probability $\\mathbb{P}(A)\\in\\{0,1\\}$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:45:17.704083+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c83b41327dd3fc7f3f989d767c4ebd8ab9b61b8d2c885e02e5e04efd04ac7e1c","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:hypoexponential_derivative_properties of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] If we have positive, distinct rates $\{\lambda_i\}_{i = 1}^\infty$:

    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item At zero, the one-sided derivatives $F_k^{(m)}(0) = 0$ for $0 \leqslant m \leqslant k-1$. The nonzero derivatives take the form
        
        \[F_{k}^{{(k + r)}}(0) = (-1)^r \left(\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i\right) \left(h_r(\lambda_1,..., \lambda_k)\right),\]
        
        \noindent where $h_r$ are the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials
        
        \[ h_r(\lambda_1, ..., \lambda_k) := \sum_{1\leqslant i_1\leqslant i_2 \leqslant ...\leqslant i_r\leqslant k} \prod_{j=1}^r \lambda_{i_j}.\]
        
        \noindent In particular, for $r=0, 1$ we have
            \[F_k^{(k)}(0) = \prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i, \qquad F_k^{(k+1)}(0) = -\left(\sum_{i=1}^k \lambda_i\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^k \lambda_i\right).\]
        
        \item The derivatives are uniformly bounded. Namely, for fixed $m$
        
        \[||F_k^{(m)}||_\infty \leqslant M_m = \max_{i=1, ...,m} |F_i^{(m)}(0)|.\]

    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(a): f integrable on R","(b): the periodization converges everywhere to a continuous function AND the Fourier transform is absolutely summable over the integers","(c): f continuous with (1+|x|)^{-1-delta} decay of both f and its transform","integrability alone does NOT give the pointwise identity"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.263262+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis on Euclidean space","id":"claim_c871045185872c50e3ad107b05bbe60ce99326ffffae1aec8481b784ad7e885a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Convention $\\hat f(\\xi)=\\int_{\\mathbb R}f(x)e^{-2\\pi i x\\xi}dx$. (a) (Always, as an $L^1$ identity) If $f\\in L^1(\\mathbb R)$, the periodization $Pf(x)=\\sum_{n\\in\\mathbb Z}f(x+n)$ converges absolutely for a.e. $x$, $Pf\\in L^1(\\mathbb T)$ with $\\|Pf\\|_{L^1(\\mathbb T)}\\le\\|f\\|_1$, and $\\widehat{Pf}(k)=\\hat f(k)$ for all $k\\in\\mathbb Z$. (b) (Pointwise identity) If in addition $\\sum_nf(x+n)$ converges for every $x$ to a continuous function and $\\sum_k|\\hat f(k)|<\\infty$, then $\\sum_{n\\in\\mathbb Z}f(x+n)=\\sum_{k\\in\\mathbb Z}\\hat f(k)e^{2\\pi i kx}$ for every $x$; taking $x=0$, $\\sum_nf(n)=\\sum_k\\hat f(k)$. (c) (Convenient sufficient condition) If $f$ is continuous and there are $C,\\delta>0$ with $|f(x)|\\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\\delta}$ and $|\\hat f(\\xi)|\\le C(1+|\\xi|)^{-1-\\delta}$, then (b) applies and both series converge absolutely; this holds for every $f\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R)$. (d) Scaled and multidimensional forms: for $T>0$, $\\sum_nf(nT)=T^{-1}\\sum_k\\hat f(k/T)$; for $f\\in\\mathcal S(\\mathbb R^d)$ and the lattice $\\mathbb Z^d$, $\\sum_{n\\in\\mathbb Z^d}f(x+n)=\\sum_{k\\in\\mathbb Z^d}\\hat f(k)e^{2\\pi i k\\cdot x}$; more generally for a full-rank lattice $\\Lambda$ with dual $\\Lambda^*$ and covolume $|\\Lambda|$, $\\sum_{\\lambda\\in\\Lambda}f(\\lambda)=|\\Lambda|^{-1}\\sum_{\\mu\\in\\Lambda^*}\\hat f(\\mu)$. Classic application (Jacobi theta transformation): $\\sum_ne^{-\\pi n^2t}=t^{-1/2}\\sum_ne^{-\\pi n^2/t}$ for $t>0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.774654+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8733e81386ce57787a3ab51fb9a0075b91a4724e3e22a79b8970f41d9bcbabc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 31 (Combined clumsy-careless collector) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] For fixed $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$,
\[
        \mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \sim
        \frac{1}{(S;S)_\infty}
        \frac{n!}{n^n}Q^nS^{n(n+1)/2}.
\]
If $T_n^{\alpha,\beta}$ is the first post-thinning completion time from the empty collection, then
\[
        \mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}T_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \Rightarrow \Exp(1).
\]
Moreover, for every fixed $r\ge1$,
\[
        \Ebb\bigl(\mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}T_n^{\alpha,\beta}\bigr)^r\to r!.
\]
Consequently,
\[
        \Ebb T_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \sim
        (S;S)_\infty
        \frac{n^n}{n!}Q^{-n}S^{-n(n+1)/2},
\]
and
\[
        \Var(T_n^{\alpha,\beta})
        \sim
        (S;S)_\infty^2
        \left(\frac{n^n}{n!}\right)^2
        Q^{-2n}S^{-n(n+1)}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:13:31.904720+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c87a764610fbe61ef1c23644c0f9f4938a21a1f9ccdb4efc4a33ff94d96de279","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ be two finite sets, $\rho$ and $\gamma$ be probability measures on $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ respectively, and $f: \Omega \to 2^{\Sigma}$ be a function\footnote{Here, $2^{\Sigma}$ is the power set of $\Sigma$.}. For each $\eta \in \Sigma$, let
    $f^{-1}(\eta):=\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \eta \in f(\omega)\}.$
     Suppose that $ \sum_{\omega \in \Omega, \eta \in \Sigma} \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)] > 0$ and then define a coupling probability measure on $\Omega\times\Sigma$ by
	\[\mathscr{P}[\omega,\eta]\propto \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)],~\forall (\omega, \eta)\in\Omega\times\Sigma. \] 

	\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$, denoted by  $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]  \propto \gamma[f(\omega)]\rho[\omega]$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. 
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$, denoted by $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta] \propto  \rho[f^{-1}(\eta)] \gamma[\eta] $ for each $\eta \in \Sigma$.   

\item[(c)] For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]\neq 0$,  the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot | \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is $\gamma[\cdot \mid f(\omega)]$.
        \item[(d)]   For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot|\eta] $ on $\Omega$ is $\rho[\cdot \mid f^{-1}(\eta)]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543907+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c894786f1b55507dfb078a06491f9f69fe1f01bd76b485d4469c8716a85154c8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a real parameter delta >= 0 the SQUARED BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta started at y >= 0, written BESQ^delta, is the unique strong solution of dY_t = 2 sqrt( |Y_t| ) dW_t + delta dt with Y_0 = y; the solution is nonnegative, and pathwise uniqueness holds despite the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient by the Yamada-Watanabe criterion, which requires only Holder continuity of exponent 1/2. The BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta, BES^delta, is X_t = sqrt(Y_t); for X > 0 it solves dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt. When delta = d is a positive INTEGER, BES^d started at |x| has the law of the radial part |B_t| of a d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x - a fact that makes the family the natural interpolation of radial Brownian motion to non-integer dimension. ADDITIVITY: BESQ^delta started at y and an independent BESQ^{delta'} started at y' add to a BESQ^{delta + delta'} started at y + y'; this holds for the SQUARED process and is false for the Bessel process itself. The index nu = delta/2 - 1 is the other common parameterisation and is the one that appears in the modified Bessel functions of the transition density; delta and nu must not be confused. For delta < 2 the boundary point 0 is reached and a boundary convention (absorbing or instantaneously reflecting) must be specified; for delta >= 2 the point 0 is never reached from y > 0 and no convention is needed. [standard; e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Chapter XI]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:55:57.000374+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8b91c6ad846745543ab01427ecc658f4873f7929768971f718375e64637a53a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] For the standard cohomogeneity-one adjoint action of \(SU(3)\) on \(S^7\),
there exist infinitely many pairwise non-isometric smooth invariant Einstein
metrics.  They may be normalized by
\[
 \Ric(g_n)=6g_n,
\]
and have principal orbit \(SU(3)/T^2\) and two singular orbits
\(\mathbb{CP}^2\).

More precisely, the metrics can be chosen so that, if \(b_n\) denotes the
scale of the initial singular orbit and \(\beta_n\) its anisotropy parameter,
then
\[
 b_n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \beta_n\longrightarrow c_*<0,
\]
where \(c_*\) is the Ricci-flat threshold of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  Moreover, the sequence may be indexed so that, for some phase constant
\(\theta_*\in\mathbb R/\pi\mathbb Z\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{15}}2\log\frac1{b_n}
 =n\pi+\theta_*+o(1),
\]
and consequently
\[
 \frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}\longrightarrow e^{-2\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
\]
Let \(h_2\) denote the nonnormal Einstein metric on \(SU(3)/T^2\)
whose Ricci-flat cone is
\[
 dr^2+r^2h_2,
 \qquad
 f_1=f_2=\frac r{\sqrt5},\quad
 f_3=\sqrt{\frac25}\,r,
\]
and let \(g_{\RF,*}\) be the complete Ricci-flat threshold metric of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  If \(p_n^\pm\) are points on the two
singular orbits, then
\[
 (S^7,b_n^{-2}g_n,p_n^\pm)
 \longrightarrow (M_*,g_{\RF,*},p_*)
\]
in pointed smooth Cheeger--Gromov sense.  On the complementary scale,
\[
 g_n\longrightarrow dt^2+\sin^2t\,h_2
\]
smoothly locally on \((0,\pi)\times SU(3)/T^2\).  Finally, there are
constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
 c b_n^{-2}\le \sup_{S^7}|\Rm(g_n)|\le C b_n^{-2}.
\]
Let \(K_{02}^{(n)}\) denotes the sectional curvature of \(g_n\) in the
two-plane spanned by the radial direction and a unit vector tangent to
the third isotropy summand. At eithe singular orbit,
$$
 b_n^2K_{02}^{(n)}\longrightarrow-\frac{1+2c_*^2}{2}.
$$
Consequently,
$$
 \frac{|K_{02}^{(n+1)}|}{|K_{02}^{(n)}|}
 \longrightarrow e^{4\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:58:38.132320+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8ba2d365482112ce98c96f61ce71fc2770d361f6abc0c592dc1ff16dae7d103","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition defi:covering-packing of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Consider a metric space $(\mathcal{X},d_\mathcal{X})$ and a subset $A\subset \mathcal{X}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item {\bf (Covering number)} For any $\varepsilon>0$ we define the $\varepsilon$-covering number of $A$ as follows
    $$\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon(A,d_\mathcal{X}):=\min\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\,\exists\,x_1,\ldots,x_n\in A\mbox{ with }A\subset \cup_{i=1}^nB_\varepsilon(x_i)\}.$$
    When $A\subset \cup_{i=1}^nB_\varepsilon(x_i)$, we say that $\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ is a $\varepsilon$-net of $A$. Therefore, $\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon(A,d_\mathcal{X})$ corresponds to the minimum number of elements of a $\varepsilon$-net.
    
    \item {\bf (Packing number)} For any $\varepsilon>0$ we define the $\varepsilon$-packing number of $A$ as follows
    $$\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(A,d_\mathcal{X}):=\max\{m\in \mathbb{N}:\,\exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_m\in A\mbox{ with }d_\mathcal{X}(y_i,y_j)\geq \varepsilon\mbox{ for all }\,i\neq j\}.$$
    When $d_\mathcal{X}(y_i,y_j)\geq \varepsilon$ for all $i\neq j$ we say that $\{y_1,\ldots,y_m\}$ is a $\varepsilon$-separated set of $A$. Therefore, $\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(A,d_\mathcal{X})$ corresponds to the maximum number of elements of a $\varepsilon$-separated set.
\end{enumerate}

When the underlying metric $d_\mathcal{X}$ is clear, we may omit it in the covering and packing numbers and we will simply denote them by $\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon(A)$ and $\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(A)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.164177+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8dd5d6dbd908dc76ffcd01c3c853b2848ddab7bef6bfcc98f9f6c9096bc819d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 32 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} does not hold, then in any local
   maximizer $(\vvvv,\xxxx,\vwww)$ of the function $F_\diamond$ defined by \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, the vector $\vwww$ must be entrywise positive.
\begin{proof}
    If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} does not hold, we have $\hv_1 > 0$, $\hx > 0$, or $\mu_1 < \alpha$. We assume for contradiction that $\vwww$ is not entrywise positive, and divide the analysis into a few cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 1:} $\hv_1 > 0$ or $\hx > 0$. In this case, let  $\www_{j_1}$ be a positive entry of $\vwww$, which must exist due to the constraint $(\mu,\vwww) = 1$. Now suppose for contradiction that we have $\www_{j_2} = 0$. For small positive $\delta$, the replacement
\[(\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2})
\mapsto \bigg(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta
    \bigg)\]
increases the value of the budget
    \[\frac1\alpha
    \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\]
by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$. It follows that we may replace $\vvv_1$ with $\vvv_1 + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, or $\xxxx$ with $\xxxx + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, while remaining inside the set $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$. Recalling
\eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, we can do this in a way which increases the value of $F_\diamond$ by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, contradicting the assumption that we were at a local maximizer.

\item \emph{Case 2:} $\hv_1 < 0$, $\hx \le 0$, and $\mu_1 < \alpha$.
We divide further into two cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 2a:} $\vvvv$ is not identically zero.
    As above, let $\www_{j_1} > 0$ and $\www_{j_2} = 0$.
    Further let $\vvv_{j_3} > 0$, and note that $\hv_{j_3} \le \hv_1 < 0$.
    Therefore the replacement
    \[
        (\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2},\vvv_{j_3}) \mapsto
        \lt(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta,
        \vvv_{j_3} - \Theta(\delta^{1/2})\rt)
    \]
    improves \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$.
    This gives a contradiction.

\item     \emph{Case 2b:} $\vvvv$ is identically zero. Then the constraints defining $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$ reduce to
 \beq
        
        1 + \xxxx \le \frac1\alpha \bigg(\sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\,, \quad
        (\mu,\vwww) = 1\,.\eeq
    Since $\mu_1 < \alpha$, we have $\vwww \neq (1/\mu_1, 0, \ldots, 0)$.
   Thus there must exist at least one index $j_1\ge2$ for which $\www_{j_1}$ is positive.
    If $\www_1 = 0$, then the replacement
    \[(\www_1,\www_{j_1}) \mapsto
        \bigg(\delta,\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta\bigg)\] improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}
while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
    Therefore we must have $\www_1 > 0$.
    Finally, if $\www_{j_2} = 0$ for any $j_2 \ge 2$, the replacement
    \[
        (\www_1,\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2}) \rightarrow
        \lt(\www_1 + \delta^{2/3}, \www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta^{2/3} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta \rt)
    \]
    improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{2/3})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
This concludes the proof.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-09T16:48:21.513714+00:00","domain":"functional analysis","id":"claim_c8df104912a240938197f2669f3805c8","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let H be an inner product space with norm ||x|| = sqrt(<x,x>). If H is real, the inner product is recovered from the norm by <x,y> = (||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) / 4 for all x, y in H. If H is complex, <x,y> = (1/4) sum_{k=0}^3 i^k ||x + i^k y||^2, equivalently <x,y> = (1/4)[(||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) + i(||x+iy||^2 - ||x-iy||^2)]. \[
X=(X^x,X^z):\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R
\]
is a \emph{Hilbert calibration for $L_\varepsilon$} if
\[
\operatorname{div}_{x,z}X=0
\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathcal S)
\]
and
\[
L_\varepsilon(z,q)
\ge
X(x,z)\cdot(-q,1)
\]
for every $q\in\mathbb R^4$ and almost every $(x,z)\in\mathcal S$.

$q=Du(x)$ almost everywhere.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.374369+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8e8d5862c639944cb0487f49591d4f0ca638d936f88c94d80bb799ba8187029","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:exist of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] {\rm[Jan-Ras-20-aop]} There exists a probability space $(\widehat\Omega,\widehat{\mathfrak{S}},\widehat\mathbb{P})$,  equipped with an additive group of continuous bijections $\widehat{T}=\{\widehat{T}_x:x\in\mathbb{Z}^2\}$ and satisfying the hypotheses of Section (sec:probsp of the paper), on which there exists a stochastic process
\begin{align}    
    \bigl({\widehat B}^{h{\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}}}(x,y) : x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),\, {\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}} \in \{+,-\}\bigr)
\end{align}
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}  [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt
\item \textup{(}No $\pm$ distinction at fixed $h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$, 
\[
\widehat\mathbb{P}\bigl\{{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,y)\bigr\}=1.
\]
When ${\widehat B}^{h-}({\widehat\omega},x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}({\widehat\omega},x,y)$, call the common value ${\widehat B}^h({\widehat\omega}, x,y)$.
\item \textup{(}Generalized Busemann function\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U), {\widehat B}^h \in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}$.  

\item \textup{(}Mean $-h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),$ $\widehat\mathbb{E}[{\widehat B}^h(0,e_i)] = -h \cdot e_i.$
\item \textup{(}Monotonicity\textup{)} For $h,h'\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$ with $h \cdot e_1 \leq h' \cdot e_1$, all $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, and $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost every ${\widehat\omega}$
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1)  
\]
and
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2).
\]
\item \textup{(}Left-/right-continuity\textup{)} For $\widehat\mathbb{P}$ almost all ${\widehat\omega}$, for all $h\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$,
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:00.766306+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8f269c00a0b2323cc27ad2722d492913ab2f66a9ea2c9b39e621b44966c2522","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Suppose that we have a family $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions}$ of resistance metrics coupled with $\Gamma$ where $\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}\colon (\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma) \times (\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma) \to [0,\infty)$. Then it is associated with a weak \clekp{} resistance form if and only if the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item The metric $\rmetres{C}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}$ is continuous with respect to $\dpathY$.

  \item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected. The conditional law of the collection $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ given $\Gamma\setminus\Gamma_{U^*}$ and $(\rmetres{V'}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V' \in \metregions[\C\setminus\ol{U}]}$ is almost surely measurable with respect to~$U^*$.

  \item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected. There exists a probability kernel $\mu^{U^*}$ such that for each $z \in \C$, the conditional law of $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U+z]}$ given $(U+z)^*$ is $(T_z)_* \mu^{U^*}(\cdot -z)$ where $T_z \FR(x,y) = \FR(x-z,y-z)$ denotes translation by $z$.

  \item Let $V,V' \in \metregions$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $x,y \in \ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$ such that for every $u \in V' \setminus V$ there is a point $z \in \ol{V}$ that separates $u$ from $x,y$ in $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$. Then
  \[ \rmetres{V}{x}{y}{\Gamma} = \rmetres{V'}{x}{y}{\Gamma} . \]

  \item Suppose that $V_1,V_2 \in \metregions$ with $\ol{V_1} \cap \ol{V_2} = \{z\}$ (where the closure is taken with respect to $d_{\ol{V}}$, see Section~\ref{subsec:main_results}). If $x \in \ol{V_1} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$, $y \in \ol{V_2} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$, then
  \[ \rmetres{V_1 \cup V_2}{x}{y}{\Gamma} = \rmetres{V_1}{x}{z}{\Gamma} + \rmetres{V_2}{z}{y}{\Gamma} . \]

  \item There exists a countable set $\{z_m\}_{m \in \N} \subseteq \Upsilon_\Gamma$ that is dense with respect to $\dpathY$ and such that the following holds. Suppose that $V \in \metregions$ consists of a single connected component and let $\CL \in \Gamma$ be a loop contained in $\ol{V}$ and intersecting $\partial V$. Then there exist two distinct points $a,b \in \CL \cap \partial V$ such that the following holds for sufficiently large $m \in \N$. Let $V_{a,b}$ (resp.\ $V_{b,a}$) be the collection of components of $V \setminus \CL$ that are connected to the counterclockwise arc of $\partial V$ from $a$ to $b$ (resp.\ from $b$ to $a$) by an admissible path within $V$. Let $A = \{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}$, $A_{a,b} = A \cap \ol{V_{a,b}}$, $A_{b,a} = A \cap \ol{V_{b,a}}$, and let $w, w_{a,b}, w_{b,a}$ be the weight functions associated with $\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A}$, $\rmetres{V_{a,b}}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A_{a,b}}$, $\rmetres{V_{b,a}}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A_{b,a}}$, respectively. Then
  \[
   w(x,y) =
   \begin{cases}
    w_{a,b}(a,b)+w_{b,a}(a,b) ,& \{x,y\} = \{a,b\} ,\\
    w_{a,b}(x,y) ,& x,y \in A_{a,b} ,\, \{x,y\} \neq \{a,b\} ,\\
    w_{b,a}(x,y) ,& x,y \in A_{b,a} ,\, \{x,y\} \neq \{a,b\} ,\\

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:53:31.969854+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8f57e2680c04ac242ec7835ed2fb41fb03221ccff9cf4931faafcaa20e6a0b9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[1 6 (\cite{HX24a}) of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] If the chain $X$ is ergodic, then its mean first passage times are all finite and satisfy

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-13T08:46:06.530321+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_c8fa8f9d294eb2cc481cd757521911b88d376297acef16fe77c553f47331f843","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let g be a norm on R^2 that is even in the first coordinate (g(-h, m) = g(h, m)), as every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm is. For fixed m, the map h -> g((h, m)) is even and convex, hence minimized at h = 0, so g((h, m)) >= g((0, m)) = |m| g(e_2). Consequently, for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) with j = r + m, m > 0 (longitudinal overshoot past the far endpoint): g(v) + g((0,r) - v) - g((0,r)) >= (r + m) g(e_2) + m g(e_2) - r g(e_2) = 2 m g(e_2), and symmetrically for j = -m < 0. The dogleg excess grows at least LINEARLY in the overshoot, with the explicit constant 2 g(e_2), using convexity and symmetry alone - no curvature hypothesis of any kind. The bound is tight as h -> 0. Use: in localization arguments it kills union sites with longitudinal overshoot at a rate no curvature assumption needs to fund, letting curvature windows be quoted only where they are literally assumed. Numerical attack: 0 violations in 300,000 trials on an anisotropic convex norm, worst ratio 1.000019.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:14:46.370162+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c8fb536f65f3707a16689c9a1cd71714b1acf74252d2fd40a6d9f030c1183972","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a space $X$ with a sum operation $+$, we can define the convolution of any two discrete probability measures on it,
$$\mu=\sum_ia_i\delta_{x_i}\quad,\quad \nu=\sum_jb_j\delta_{y_j}$$
as being the discrete probability measure given by the following formula:
$$\mu*\nu=\sum_{ij}a_ib_j\delta_{x_i+y_j}$$
That is, the convolution operation $*$ is defined by $\delta_x*\delta_y=\delta_{x+y}$, and linearity.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:54:15.623482+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c916fecb8c6277def67a796f5705974ab2a15e1fa4ae6d5c5423678e2cc320ab","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 75 (Analytic critical Rees algebra) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Truncated tensor concatenation makes
\(\mathscr R^{\rm cr}_{\le N}(H)\) a graded topological algebra.  More
precisely, whenever the total tensor degree is at most \(N\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr K_m^{[a]}(H)\widehat\otimes
 \mathscr K_n^{[b]}(H)
 \longrightarrow
 \mathscr K_{m+n}^{[a+b]}(H)
 
\end{equation}
is continuous, with the conventions in
\eqref{cc:eq-cost-zero-spaces}.  Lowering either positive input cost by one
lowers the product cost by one.  Hence tensor product descends to the algebraic associated graded:
\begin{equation}
 \partial_{\rm cr}^a\mathscr K_m(H)\otimes
 \partial_{\rm cr}^b\mathscr K_n(H)
 \longrightarrow
 \partial_{\rm cr}^{a+b}\mathscr K_{m+n}(H),
 \qquad [A]\otimes[B]\longmapsto[A\otimes B].
 
\end{equation}
If \(B\) is a critical atom with \(s_N(B)\sim c/N\), then
\begin{equation}
 s_N(B^{\otimes r})
 \sim\frac{c^r}{\Gamma(r)}\phi_r(N),
 \qquad
 [B]^{\otimes r}\ne0
 \quad\text{in }\partial_{\rm cr}^r.
 
\end{equation}
Thus tensor resonance is multiplication on the analytic critical boundary,
not a separate calculation attached to each stochastic model.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.691651+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c91bb9984ea148e40ded2a45ac845506a68bfcb1c39e0f6c9edc1af271c4cc7f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 30 (Finite-frequency prefix factorisation) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space with
$\dim V\geq2$, and let
$\gamma\colon[0,T]\to V$ be a continuous bounded-variation path. Set
\[
l=\log S(\gamma),
\qquad
v=\gamma_T-\gamma_0,
\]
and assume that
\[
R(l)=\infty,
\qquad
v\neq0.
\]
Choose $\ell\in V^*$ such that $\ell(v)=1$, put $W=\ker\ell$, and write
\[
\gamma_t-\gamma_0=x_t v+X_t,
\qquad
x_t=\ell(\gamma_t-\gamma_0),
\qquad
X_t\in W.
\]

Let $\Lambda\subset2\pi\Q$ be finite and symmetric, so that
$\Lambda=-\Lambda$. Give $W$ an auxiliary Euclidean norm, let $W_{\C}$
be its complexification, and define the real Hilbert space
\[
E_\Lambda
=
\set{(z_\omega)_{\omega\in\Lambda}
\in\prod_{\omega\in\Lambda}W_{\C}:
 z_{-\omega}=\overline{z_\omega}}
\]
with the norm inherited from the Hilbert direct sum. Define the decorated
transverse path
\[
B_t^\Lambda(\gamma)
=
\left(
\int_0^t \e^{i\omega x_s}\dd X_s
\right)_{\omega\in\Lambda},
\qquad 0\leq t\leq T,
\]
and the orthogonal map
\[
T_\Lambda\colon E_\Lambda\to E_\Lambda,
\qquad
(T_\Lambda z)_\omega=\e^{i\omega}z_\omega.
\]
Denote by the same symbol the induced graded automorphism of tensor
series, and set
\[
r_t^\Lambda
=S\bigl(B^\Lambda(\gamma)|_{[0,t]}\bigr),
\qquad
h_\Lambda=r_T^\Lambda.
\]

Then there exists $t_\Lambda\in[0,T]$ such that
\begin{equation}
r_{t_\Lambda}^\Lambda
=h_\Lambda T_\Lambda\bigl(r_{t_\Lambda}^\Lambda\bigr).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, with
\[
a_\Lambda=r_{t_\Lambda}^\Lambda,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
h_\Lambda
=a_\Lambda T_\Lambda(a_\Lambda)^{-1}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:58:10.027790+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c91e1d0518ce03ebaba0defcad49fc9c5760cca566fe18864245b2e5a560f4eb","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem weighted-ua-root-finding of arXiv:2607.21428, 'Subcritical percolation and network archaeology on random recursive tree substrate network'] Let \(U_m\) be a uniform attachment tree on vertices \([m]\), rooted at
		\(1\). Let \((X_v)_{v\in[m]}\) be independent positive weights, independent
		of \(U_m\), such that for some constants \(0<c<C<\infty\),
		\begin{equation}
			
			c\leqslant \mathbb E X_v\leqslant C,
			\qquad
			\sup_v \mathbb E X_v^2\leqslant C .
		\end{equation}
		Let \(\operatorname{TopJ}_L^X(U_m)\) be the \(L\) vertices with smallest weighted Jordan
		scores. For \(\delta>0\), put
		\[
		\mathcal{A}_\delta^X(U_m)
		:=
		\{v\in U_m:
		\psi_{U_m}^X(v)\leqslant \psi_{U_m}^X(1)+\delta X(U_m)\}.
		\]
		Then for every \(\eta>0\), there exist
		\[
		L=L(\eta,c,C)<\infty,
		\qquad
		\delta=\delta(\eta,c,C)>0,
		\qquad
		m_0=m_0(\eta,c,C)<\infty,
		\]
		such that, for every \(m\geqslant m_0\),
		\begin{equation}
			
			\mathbb P\left(
			\psi_{U_m}^X(1)\leqslant (1-\delta)X(U_m),
			\quad
			|\mathcal{A}_\delta^X(U_m)|\leqslant L
			\right)
			\geqslant 1-\eta .
		\end{equation}
		The same bound holds conditionally, uniformly in the
			environment, in the following sense.  Let \(m\geqslant m_0\), let \(\mathcal{G}_m\) be a
			sigma-field, and let \(E_m\in\mathcal{G}_m\) be an event on which, conditionally on
			\(\mathcal{G}_m\): \(U_m\) has the uniform-attachment law and is independent of the
			weights, and the weights are conditionally independent, positive, and
			satisfy
		\[
		c\leqslant \mathbb E[X_v\mid\mathcal{G}_m]\leqslant C,
		\qquad
		\sup_{v\leqslant m}\mathbb E[X_v^2\mid\mathcal{G}_m]\leqslant C .
		\]
		Then, on \(E_m\),
		\begin{equation}
			
				\mathbb P\left(
				\psi_{U_m}^X(1)\leqslant (1-\delta)X(U_m),
				\ \
				|\mathcal{A}_\delta^X(U_m)|\leqslant L
				\,\middle|\,\mathcal{G}_m
				\right)
				\geqslant 1-\eta .
		\end{equation}
		The constants \(m_0,L,\delta\) depend only on
			\((\eta,c,C)\), and not on \(m\). In particular,
			if for each \(m\) such a pair \((\mathcal{G}_m,E_m)\) is given with
			\(\mathbb P(E_m)\to1\), then taking expectations in
			(equation eq:uniform-conditional-ua of the paper) gives
			\(\liminf_{m\to\infty}\mathbb P(\psi_{U_m}^X(1)\leqslant(1-\delta)X(U_m),\,
			|\mathcal{A}_\delta^X(U_m)|\leqslant L)\geqslant1-\eta\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:43:37.236802+00:00","domain":"game theory","id":"claim_c9565091907e96d8504914374b1b2370362648e70aac2f39f97cdfa7046dceb0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Solving a finite two-player zero-sum game with m x n payoff matrix A (row player maximizing, column player minimizing the same quantity) is equivalent to solving a pair of dual linear programs. The row player's LP is: maximize v subject to sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i * A_{ij} >= v for all j=1,...,n, x_i >= 0, sum_i x_i = 1. The column player's LP, minimize w subject to sum_{j=1}^{n} A_{ij} * y_j <= w for all i=1,...,m, y_j >= 0, sum_j y_j = 1, is exactly the LP dual of the row player's program. Because both programs are feasible and bounded, strong LP duality guarantees their optimal values agree (v* = w*), recovering von Neumann's minimax theorem as a consequence of linear programming duality; standard LP algorithms, such as the simplex method or interior-point methods, applied to either program simultaneously compute the game's value and both players' optimal mixed strategies.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:51:33.332050+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c95bedaa89d59dce96801447751c1a5efc29276a50e44011b95e888115a332fe","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lm:pointwise-par-colimit of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] For any object $(f\colon Y\to X)\in \Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}$, we have an equivalence
\[ T_i(f)\simeq\mathop{\textup{colim}}_{Y}(i\circ f)\]
in ${\mathcal{C}}(1)$, where $\mathop{\textup{colim}}_{Y}\colon \ul{\textup{Fun}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{Y}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}},\mathcal C)\to {\mathcal C}$ denotes the parametrized colimit-functor (left adjoint to the inclusion of constant diagrams).
\begin{proof}
    As $Y\in\Spc_{S\triangleright T}$ and $T_i$ is an $S$-cocontinuous extension of $i$, it suffices to show that $f\in\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}$ is the parametrized colimit of the composite $y\circ f\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{Y}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{X}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to\ul\Spc_{T/X}$.

As $f_!$ is $S$-cocontinuous, this reduces us to considering the case $f=\textup{id}_Y$, i.e.~we want to show that the colimit of $y\colon {\mathpalette\ulhelper{Y}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/Y}$ is the terminal object $\textup{id}_Y$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:51:30.064702+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c964ae9a508c58bef5e0a37d471ab50227a0a5075609a8cfaa0c7e15fefd9e56","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2606.00586, 'Stein's Method for Convergence Rates of Invariant Measures in the Nonlocal-to-Local Limit'] Let $h \in \sS'(\mR^d)$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item Suppose that $h(\xi)$ is a real-valued function supported in $B_1^c$ and 
    \[
    |\nabla^k h(\xi)| \leq A |\xi|^{\beta-k} \log(1+|\xi|), \quad \exists \beta \in [13/12,4/3], ~ \forall 0\leq k\leq d+3. 
    \]
    Then there exists a kernel $H$ such that the Fourier multiplier operator $T_hf(x):=\sF^{-1}(h\widehat{f})(x)$ admits the integral representation 
    \begin{equation}
        T_hf(x) = \mathrm{P.V.}\int_{\mR^d} \left(f(x-y)-f(x)\right) H(y) \d y, 
    \end{equation}
    and for any $y \in \mR^d$, it holds that 
    \begin{equation}
        |H(y)| \leq C \left[ |y|^{-d-\beta}(1+|\log|y||) \wedge |y|^{-d-2} \right], 
    \end{equation}
    where $C$ depends only on $d$ and $A$. 
    \item Suppose that $h(\xi)$ is supported in $B_2$ and 
    \[
    |\nabla^k h(\xi)| \leq B |\xi|^{s - k} \log(1+|\xi|^{-1}), \quad \exists s\in [7/4,2],~ \forall 0\leq k\leq d+4. 
    \]
    Then there exists a kernel $H$ such that the Fourier multiplier operator $T_hf(x):=\sF^{-1}(h\widehat{f})(x)$ admits the integral representation 
    \[
    T_hf(x) = \int_{\mR^d} f(x-y) H(y) \d y, 
    \]
    and for any $y \in \mR^d$, 
    \begin{equation}
        |H(y)| \leq C \left[ |y|^{-d-s} (1+|\log|y||) \wedge 1 \right], 
    \end{equation}
    where $C$  depends on $d$ and $B$. 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:53:10.161096+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c9aa5873b85cdbbd4ed8e7a37c9f057c8e92e26f99e25b0f8929f249102cf7dc","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma quotient-pb of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a map of free $G$-spaces, such that $X$ is Hausdorff. Then
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            X\arrow[r,"\textup{proj}"]\arrow[d,"f"'] & X/G\arrow[d,"f/G"]\\
            Y\arrow[r,"\textup{proj}"'] & Y/G
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is a pullback square.
    \begin{proof}
        By [schwede2018global]*{Proposition~B.13(i)}, the quotients $X/G$ and $Y/G$ are preserved by the forgetful functor to sets. Thus, to show that the comparison map $c\colon X\to X/G\times_{Y/G}Y$ is bijective, we may instead prove the analogous statement in the category of sets. This can be checked fiberwise over $X/G$; the fiber over some class $[x]$ is then given by the orbit $Gx$ (for some fixed representative), while the fiber of the projection $X/G\times_{Y/G}Y$ over the same $[x]$ is given by $\{[x]\}\times Gf(x)$. By assumption, both of these are free $G$-orbits, and any equivariant self-map of $G$ is bijective, proving the claim.
    
        It remains to show that the induced map 
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}(K,c)\colon{\textup{Hom}}_{\textbf{\textup{Top}}}(K,X)\to{\textup{Hom}}_{\textbf{\textup{Top}}}(K,X/G\times_{Y/G}Y)
        \]
        is bijective for every compact space $K$. As we already know that $c$ is bijective, it will be enough to show surjectivity, for which we consider any $(\alpha,\beta)\colon K\to X/G\times_{Y/G}Y$. The space $X/G$ is again Hausdorff by [tom-Dieck-trafo]*{Proposition~3.1(v)}, so $\alpha(K)\subset X/G$ is compact, and Proposition~3.6(ii) of \emph{op.\ cit.} shows that also the preimage $X'$ of $\alpha(K)$ under $X\to X/G$ is compact.         
        By [schwede2018global]*{Proposition B.13(iii)}, the map $X'/G\times_{Y/G}Y\to X/G\times_{Y/G}Y$ induced by the inclusion $X'\hookrightarrow X$ is an embedding, so $(\alpha,\beta)$ factors through a continuous map $K\to X'/G\times_{Y/G}Y$, and it will be enough to show that this admits a lift to $X'$. Replacing $X$ by $X'$, we may therefore assume without loss of generality that $X$ is compact. But then $X\to X/G\times_{Y/G}Y$ is a continuous bijection from a compact space to a weak Hausdorff space, hence a homeomorphism.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:32:58.300483+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c9aa8f02326e6587f22ca388c66ad612d31beb3b1f156207481bceffdc88e636","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] A family \( (P_t)_{t \geq 0} \) of operators on real-valued measurable functions on \( {\mathbb{S}^{n-1} } \) is called a \emph{Markov semigroup} if it satisfies the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item For each \( t \geq 0 \), \( P_t \) is a linear operator mapping bounded measurable functions to bounded measurable functions.
    \item \( P_t(1) = 1 \), where \( 1 \) denotes the constant function on \( {\mathbb{S}^{n-1} } \) (mass conservation).
    \item If \( f \geq 0 \), then \( P_t f \geq 0 \) (positivity preservation).
    \item \( P_0 = \mathrm{Id} \), the identity operator.
    \item For any \( s, t \geq 0 \), \( P_{s+t} = P_s \circ P_t \) (semigroup property).
    \item For each \( f \), the map \( t \mapsto P_t f \) is continuous.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["K compact","each f_n continuous","for each x the sequence f_n(x) is monotone in n, in the same direction for every x","the pointwise limit f is continuous"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.751214+00:00","domain":"real analysis","id":"claim_c9b13faaa47bc5e4c48eaac0e195f673c255de2096f3e248b1dfd899c8f459b1","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let K be a compact topological space and f_n : K -> R continuous. Suppose the sequence is monotone in n at every point (f_n(x) <= f_{n+1}(x) for all n and all x, or the reverse for all n and all x), that f_n -> f pointwise, and that the limit f is continuous. Then f_n -> f UNIFORMLY on K. All four hypotheses carry weight: (a) compactness - on the non-compact [0,1) the sequence f_n(x) = x^n decreases continuously to the continuous limit 0 but not uniformly; (b) continuity of the limit - on the compact [0,1] the same f_n(x) = x^n is monotone and continuous with a discontinuous limit and the convergence is not uniform; (c) monotonicity - the moving bump f_n which is the piecewise-linear tent of height 1 on [1/(n+1), 1/n] and 0 elsewhere on [0,1] converges pointwise to 0 with all data continuous and compact, but sup |f_n| = 1; (d) continuity of each f_n - on [0,1] the indicators of the OPEN intervals, f_n = 1_{(0, 1/n)}, decrease pointwise to the identically zero function, which is continuous, on a compact space, so every hypothesis except the continuity of the f_n holds, yet sup |f_n| = 1 for every n. Monotonicity is required POINTWISE IN THE SAME DIRECTION for all x, not merely that each f_n is a monotone function of x. [standard; e.g. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed., Theorem 7.13]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:18:27.580085+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_c9d342de5d2740b126d2418ad05e8c8a337104c8b8bb0b44fac37cd61368b81c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 14 (Simplicity, positivity, monotonicity, analyticity) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Let $M(\theta)$ have entries $M_{d,d'}(\theta)=m_*q(d')p_{d,d'}(\theta)$, with $\theta\mapsto p_{d,d'}(\theta)$ real-analytic (it is a ratio of analytic Wald integrals \eqref{eq:wald}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Krein--Rutman is unnecessary.) $\rho(M)$ is a simple, isolated eigenvalue with a strictly positive right eigenvector $\psi$ and left eigenvector $\phi$, by the Perron--Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices.
\item (Monotonicity.) $\rho(M)$ is nondecreasing in each entry of $M$, strictly so under irreducibility, since $\rho(M)=\lim_n\|M^n\|^{1/n}$ and $M^n$ is entrywise monotone.
\item (Analyticity and the gradient.) $\theta\mapsto\rho(M(\theta))$ is real-analytic on the region where $M$ is irreducible (a simple eigenvalue of an analytic matrix family is analytic, Kato \cite{Kato66}, finite-dimensional case, with no eigenvalue crossing at the top because the Perron root is simple and isolated), and
\[
\partial_{\theta_i}\rho(M)=\frac{\phi^\top(\partial_{\theta_i}M)\psi}{\phi^\top\psi}\qquad(\ne0\text{ generically, since }\partial_{\theta_i}M\ge0\text{ with a positive entry}).
\]
\item (Operator van den Driessche--Watmough lift is unnecessary.) Writing $M=FV^{-1}$ with $V=\diag(\alpha_d)$ and $F$ the $m\times m$ fertility block, the finite-dimensional next-generation theorem \cite{vdDW02} gives directly: $s(J)<0\Leftrightarrow\rho(M)<1$ and $s(J)>0\Leftrightarrow\rho(M)>1$, where $J=F-V$ is the linearised drift and $s(\cdot)$ its spectral abscissa.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:37:08.954998+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ca0d7ebacf2e9376009eb20f6df8f422c6b2ba7331c4a878f5ae0a04951f9ed2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:explicit_density of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be an ergodic diffusion with invariant measure $\mu$ whose
symmetric part $\mathcal{L}_S$ satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality~(equation eq:poincare of the paper)
with spectral gap $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}>0$ (by Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper)). 
Let $\overline{\rho}_t(V)$ denote the empirical density according to Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper)
with ergodic mean $\E^\mu[\overline{\rho}_t(V)]=\E^\mu[V]$,
and let $\nu\ll\mu$ with $\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\mu\in L^2(\mu)$.
Then for all $t > 0$ and $a > 0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\overline{\rho}_t(V) - \E^\mu[\overline{\rho}_t] \geq a\right)
  \leq
  \left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu}{\mathrm{d}\mu}\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}
  \exp\left[-t \frac{\tilde\sigma_\rho^2}{c_\rho^2} h\left(\frac{c_\rho a}{\tilde\sigma_\rho^2}\right)  \right],
  
\end{align}
where $h(u) \equiv 1 + u - \sqrt{1 + 2u}$ and we define 
\begin{align}
  \tilde\sigma_\rho^2 \equiv \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}},
  \qquad
  c_\rho \equiv \frac{\|V - \E^\mu[V]\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}.
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:56:11.133287+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ca39fbe4a5f1f69c7cdf9722c0d4e3ee478eeccdf90b8c5d35238906283dd8db","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 (\cite{Chen2013}*{Lemma 3}) of arXiv:2608.10515, 'Limiting Law of Local Fields for the Mean Field Ghatak-Sherrington Model'] Let $I\subset[0,\infty)$ and $J$ be two bounded intervals. Let $K_1,K_2,K_3>0$ be constants, and let $\mathcal F$ be a sigma-field independent of the Gaussian family $((g_j)_{j\le N},\xi)$. Assume the following conditions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item For each $N\in\N$ and $\beta\in J$, the random variables $\{X^N_{j,\beta}:1\le j\le N\}$ are $\mathcal F$-measurable and satisfy
\[
  |X^N_{j,\beta}|\le K_1\qquad\text{for all }1\le j\le N,\ \beta\in J.
\]
\item The measurable functions $f_1,f_2:\N\times I\times J\to\R$ satisfy, for all $(N,t,\beta)\in\N\times I\times J$,
\[
  |f_1(N,t,\beta)|\le \frac{K_2}{\sqrt N},
  \qquad
  |f_2(N,t,\beta)|\le K_3.
\]
\item The continuous function $U:\R\to\R$ satisfies, for some $A>0$ and
\[
  0<a<\min\left\{\frac1{8K_1^2K_2^2},\frac1{4vK_3^2}\right\},
\]
that
\[
  |U(x)|\le A e^{a x^2}\qquad\text{for all }x\in\R.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a constant $K>0$, depending only on $(A,a,K_1,K_2,K_3,v,I,J)$, such that
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{N\in\N}\sup_{\beta\in J}
  \E_0\left[\sup_{t\in I}\left|U\left(f_1(N,t,\beta)\sum_{j=1}^Ng_jX^N_{j,\beta}+f_2(N,t,\beta)\xi\right)\right|\right]\le K,
\end{equation}
where $\E_0$ denotes conditional expectation with respect to the Gaussian randomness $((g_j)_{j\le N},\xi)$, with $\mathcal F$ fixed. In particular, the bound is uniform in the realization of the additional randomness. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Integer n>=1; the threshold v has the same parity as n.","Codes may have at most 2n distinct codewords; repeated matrix rows are allowed."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.365448+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ca4ed2ec9c98afcf226b7ce43abe286b6ff980864f4e57a05f9d4b8c1b9fafc9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is the proved elementary covering-code reduction for Afonso S. Bandeira's Open Problem 11, How many deviations are needed afterall?, in Did just a couple of deviations suffice all along? (problems 10-14), Randomstrasse 101 (19 December 2024; https://randomstrasse101.math.ethz.ch/posts/HowManyDeviations/). For an n-by-n matrix A with entries in {+1,-1}, define disc(A)=min_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity, where ||y||_infinity=max_i |y_i|, and let D_n=max_{A in {+1,-1}^{n-by-n}} disc(A). For r,x in {+1,-1}^n let d_H(r,x) be the number of differing coordinates and let the complement of r be -r. For an integer v in [0,n] with the same parity as n, |r dot x|>=v exactly when d_H(r,x)<=(n-v)/2 or d_H(-r,x)<=(n-v)/2. Thus disc(A)>=v exactly when the rows of A and their complements cover the sign cube within radius (n-v)/2. (1) Unbounded domains: on $U=\\mathbb R^n$ the Dirichlet spectrum is $[0,\\infty)$, $\\lambda_1=0$, and $\\|e^{t\\Delta}\\|_{L^2\\to L^2}=1$ for every $t$, so no rate is uniform over the unit ball of $L^2$; individual solutions do decay, but only algebraically in general -- for $g=\\Phi(\\cdot,1)$ one has $\\|u(t)\\|_{L^2}=(8\\pi(t+1))^{-n/4}$. Half-spaces and cones behave the same way. (2) Neumann boundary conditions: constants solve the Neumann heat equation, $u\\equiv1$ does not decay at all. The correct statement is decay to the mean: for $U$ bounded, connected and Lipschitz (so that $H^1(U)\\hookrightarrow L^2(U)$ is compact and the Neumann spectrum is discrete), $\\|u(t)-\\bar g\\|_{L^2}\\le e^{-\\mu_2t}\\|g-\\bar g\\|_{L^2}$, where $\\bar g$ is the mean of $g$ and $\\mu_2>0$ is the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue. (3) Zeroth-order terms: for $u_t=\\Delta u+cu$ the decay rate becomes $\\lambda_1-\\sup c$, which is a growth rate as soon as $\\sup c>\\lambda_1$. Auditor's check: whenever an exponential-decay claim appears, identify the eigenvalue being used, verify it is positive on the stated function space, and verify that the domain's geometry (boundedness in at least one direction for Dirichlet, connectedness and mean-zero for Neumann) actually supplies the gap.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:48:47.287033+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_caaf82ba26dd526b12d4960d0679adfbfe0cf5e77618ccf990d13e89716944b2","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma xxphi of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Let $\zeta\in\mathcal P([0,1])$ and fix $q\in[0,1]$.
		Let $(X_t)_{t\in[q,1]}$ solve the Auffinger--Chen SDE 
		\[
		\mathrm{d} X_t=\xi''(t)\,\zeta([0,t])\,\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(t,X_t)\mathrm{d} t+\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\,\mathrm{d} B_t.
		\]
		Write $u(t,y):=\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(t,y)$. Then for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
		\begin{equation}
			\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,x)
			=1-\zeta\bigl([0,q)\bigr)\,u(q,x)^2
			-\int_{[q,1]}\mathbb{E}\!\left[u(t,X_t)^2\,\middle|\,X_q=x\right]\zeta(\mathrm{d} t).
		\end{equation}
		Consequently,
		\[
		\mathbb{E}\big[\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,X_q)\big]
		=1-\zeta\bigl([0,q)\bigr)\,\mathbb{E}\big[u(q,X_q)^2\big]
		-\int_{[q,1]}\mathbb{E}\big[u(t,X_t)^2\big]\,\zeta(\mathrm{d} t).
		\]
		Moreover, if $\mathbb{E}[u(t,X_t)^2]=t$ for $\zeta$-a.e.\ $t\in[q,1]$
		and also $\mathbb{E}[u(q,X_q)^2]=q$,
		then
		\[
		\mathbb{E}\big[\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,X_q)\big]
		=1-\zeta\bigl([0,q)\bigr)\,q-\int_{[q,1]}t\,\zeta(\mathrm{d} t)
		=\int_q^1 \zeta([0,t])\mathrm{d} t.
		\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:32:23.741389+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cacc7b69b610a23a1e0040aa6e604bfb5a9801c5189b2cdd44d542ddd54935d2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:main_result of arXiv:2603.24803, 'Critical Spectral Invariants in Random Walks with Geometric Resetting'] Consider a random walk on $\{0,1,\ldots,a\}$ with absorbing boundaries at $0$ and $a$,
transition probabilities $p,q \in (0,1)$ ($p+q=1$), and geometric resetting with
parameter $\gamma \in (0,1]$. Let $q_z(\gamma)$ denote the probability of absorption
at $0$ starting from position $z \in \{1, 2, \ldots, a-1\}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Existence and uniqueness of sign-change point:}
For fixed $\gamma \in (0,1]$, define
$h_z(\gamma) := \partial q_z(\gamma)/\partial\gamma$ for
$z \in \{1, 2, \ldots, a-1\}$.
There exists a unique pair of consecutive integers $(z_0, z_0+1)$ such that
$h_{z_{0}}(\gamma) \cdot h_{z_{0}+1}(\gamma) < 0$. This defines a \emph{sign-change point}
$z^{\dagger}$ satisfying:
\[
h_z(\gamma) > 0 \ \text{for } z < z^{\dagger}, \quad
h_z(\gamma) < 0 \ \text{for } z > z^{\dagger}.
\]

\item \textbf{Midpoint invariance (even $a$):}
If $a$ is even, then $z^{\dagger} = a/2$ for all $p \in (0,1)$, $\gamma \in (0,1]$.
Moreover, the absorption probability at the midpoint is:
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_{a/2}(\gamma)& = \frac{(q/p)^{a/2}}{1 + (q/p)^{a/2}} \quad\\
& \text{for all } \gamma \in (0,1], \; p \in (0,1),
\end{aligned}
\]
and consequently $\partial q_{a/2}(\gamma)/\partial\gamma \equiv 0$.

\item \textbf{Location for odd $a$:}
If $a$ is odd, $z^{\dagger}$ lies between $(a-1)/2$ and $(a+1)/2$, with the
precise location depending on $p$ according to the asymptotic expansion,
valid for $|p-q| \ll 1$:
\[
z^{\dagger}(\gamma,p) = \frac{a}{2} - \frac{C(\gamma,a)}{2}(p-q) + O(|p-q|^2),
\]
where $C(\gamma,a) > 0$ for all $\gamma \in (0,1]$ and satisfies $C(\gamma,a) = \Theta(a)$.

\item \textbf{Approximate invariance for odd $a$:}
When $a$ is odd, no exact invariance exists at integer sites. However, for the
two central positions $z \in \{(a-1)/2, (a+1)/2\}$,
\[
\left|\frac{\partial q_z(\gamma)}{\partial\gamma}\right|
\le \frac{K(\gamma)}{a},
\]
where $K(\gamma) > 0$ is independent of $p$ and may grow moderately with $\gamma$.
Consequently, the sensitivity to resetting at these sites is significantly
reduced compared to bulk positions.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:51:12.740044+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cad48e1173243dc7f8b71f18d8aca5cf18221840afadb34f88c430fb297f373f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{Bilateral words, relative height, shifts})
$(\textbf{a})$ A \emph{bilateral word} is a sequence 
$u\! =\!  (a_k)_{k_1 <k\leq k_2}$ where $k_1\ino \bbZZ$, $k_2 \ino \bbZ$ and $a_k \ino \bbN^*$, $k_1 \leko k \leqo k_2$.   
If $k_1\! \geq \! k_2$, then $u\! = \! \varnothing$. We denote by $\overline{\bbU}$ the set of bilateral words. 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{b})$ Let $u\eqo (a_{k})_{k_1 < k\leq k_2 } \ino \obbU$, as above. Then 
\begin{equation}  

\bbn u\bbn_-\! =\!  k_1 , \quad \textrm{and} \quad \bbn u \bbn\! = \! k_2 .
\end{equation}
Here $\bbn u \bbn$ is called the \textit{relative height} 
of $u$ and $\bbn u \bbn_-$  its \emph{depth}. 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{c})$  Let $u\eqo (a_{k})_{k_1 < k\leq k_2 } \ino \obbU$ as above. 
Let $l \ino \bbZ$. We denote by $\varphi_l (u)$ the \emph{$l$-shifted word $u$}. Namely, 
\begin{equation}  

\varphi_{l} (u) = (a_{k+l})_{k_1 -l < k\leq k_2 -l }, 
\end{equation}
Therefore, $\bbn \varphi_{l} (u) \bbn_- \! = \! \bbn  u\bbn _- \! -\! l$,  $\bbn  \varphi_{l} (u) \bbn \! = \! \bbn  u \bbn \! -\! l$.  We adopt the convention $\varphi_l (\varnothing)\! = \! \varnothing$. Observe that the $\varphi_l\! : \! \obbU \! \to \! \obbU$ are bijections such that $\varphi_l \! \circ \! \varphi_{l^\prime} \! = \! \varphi_{l+ l^\prime}$, $l,l'\ino \bbZ$. For all $k \ino \bbZ$, we then set 
$$ \overline{\bbU}_k = \varphi_{-k} (\bbU) \; .$$
Note that $\overline{\bbU}_k \backslash \{ \varnothing \}$ is the set of bilateral words $u$ such that 
$\bbn u \bbn_- \eqo k$.  We shall also denote by $\overline{\bbU}_{-\infty}$ the set of bilateral words with an infinite depth.  \cq","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.350975+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb10364dace7dba743898e874e7664b4dd7421f41ae9cdd370defd519baac0d2","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 184 (quenched second moment bounds for 
$\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ and 
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In addition to Lemma~\ref{l:barD.Ising.second} we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[\max\bigg\{
	\bE\Big[\Delta\bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2\Big]
	: 0\le d\le\dmax-1
	\bigg\}
	\le \frac{\SMAX_N(\Ising)^2\BUCKETS\delta}{N}\]
where $\SMAX_N(\Ising)$ is a random variable satisfying the bound
	\[\P\Big(\SMAX^N(\Ising) \ge \log N\Big)
	\le \exp
	\bigg(
	-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}
	\bigg)
	\,.\]
The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ in place of
$\bar{D}^{\Ising}$.

\begin{proof}
Recall that we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.Ising} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)}{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}
	=\frac{1}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\sum_{i\in B}
	\frac{\be_i}{|B|^{1/2}},
	\by\bigg)
	\equiv \frac{(\be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))}{|B|^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we abbreviate $B\equiv B^\Ising$.
If we define the random variable
	\[
	\SMAX_N(\Ising)
	\equiv\max
	\bigg\{
	\Big|( \be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))\Big|
	: 
	0\le d\le \dmax-1, B\in \mathcal{B}^\Ising(q_d)
	\bigg\}\,,
	\]
then we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[
	\bE[\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2]
	= \frac{\delta_d}{N}
	\sum_{B\in \mathcal{B}^\Ising(q_d)}
	(\be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))^2
	\le  \frac{\SMAX_N(\Ising)^2\BUCKETS\delta}{N}\,.
	\]
The bound on $\SMAX_N(\Ising)$ follows by a similar argument as the bound for $\SMAX_N(\RomII)$ from Lemma~\ref{l:barD.II.second.quenched}, with the simplification that $\|\be_B\|=1$ is trivially bounded. 
This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

\[
  H(\bs{q}):=-\sum_{i=1}^d q_i\log q_i
\]
denote the usual Shannon entropy, and define the complementary entropy functional
\[
  H_{\mr c}(\bs{q}):=-\sum_{i=1}^d(1-q_i)\log(1-q_i).
\]

\[
  S(\bs{q}):=H(\bs{q})-H_{\mr c}(\bs{q})
\]
the local Bethe entropy functional.

probability distribution on a finite set, we write $H(\mu)$ for the

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:30:08.165877+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb4600cd0cb5ffb71bc92c3e8d590fdfc8af3a78565b9797a841e6785fef4dac","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] \Authornote{Jeff}{alt version}{blue}
	For any deviation vector $\eta_\tau$ associated with a non-trivial shape $\tau$ such that
$\eta_\tau \neq \eta_0$, we have
\[
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\eta_\tau^\top M^{-1}\eta_\tau\right]
    =   
    \frac{1}{1-\gamma}\,
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\eta_\tau\|_2^2\right] + O(1) \,.

\]
\Authornote{Jeff}{notice an error bound of $O(d)$ is interesting here as $\eta_0$ would have deviation $m/d$ by itself, so we are making polynomial improvement}{blue}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:42:57.183102+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb46b0f84139a0238bf1fbc72025695b844fab752763a68a43e5a1be3354746b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem {\cite[Theorems~1.1.4 and 1.1.5 of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] {LevelLineGFFI}}]
	Let $h$ be a GFF on $\BH$ with piecewise constant boundary conditions that change only finitely many times. For all $u \in \BR$ and $x \in \partial \BH$, we denote by $\gamma_u^x$ the level line of $h$ with height $u$ starting from $x$ and ending at $\infty$. Fix $x_2 \leq x_1$ and $u_1, u_2 \in \BR$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $u_2 < u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ a.s.\ stays to the left of $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$.
		\item If $u_2 = u_1$, then $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ may intersect $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and, upon intersecting, the two curves merge and never separate.
		\item If $u_1 - u_2 \geq 2 \lambda$, then $\gamma_{u_1}^{x_1}$ and $\gamma_{u_2}^{x_2}$ do not intersect each other a.s.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["both measure spaces sigma-finite (needed for Tonelli and for L^p-L^q duality)","f product-measurable and nonnegative, or with a finite right-hand side","1 <= p <= infinity"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752220+00:00","domain":"real analysis","id":"claim_cb6ac42afbf5cb613a530cbb8393109c2b97fb3282b5e1c27ca1629a6a611759","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p <= infinity, and f : X x Y -> [0, infinity] product-measurable. Then the L^p(mu) norm of the y-average dominates in the direction: || integral_Y f(., y) dnu(y) ||_{L^p(dmu)} <= integral_Y || f(., y) ||_{L^p(dmu)} dnu(y). For signed or complex f the same holds provided the right-hand side is finite, and then the inner integral converges absolutely for mu-a.e. x. The inequality is the continuous form of the triangle inequality for the L^p norm and reduces to it when nu is counting measure on two points. The reverse inequality is false for p > 1 and TRUE for 0 < p <= 1 with the roles of the two sides exchanged. Special case worth naming: taking nu counting measure on the integers gives || sum_n f_n ||_p <= sum_n || f_n ||_p. [standard; e.g. Stein, Singular Integrals and Differentiability Properties of Functions, Appendix A.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:10:07.473363+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb79141dcb1fc490b9d4b16fe109e95273ae65cd23a5e2b93b438fb424cfff0d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma eq:mixture-remainder-X of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[lemma]{lem:product-mixture-path}
Let \(\mu_i\) and \(\gamma_i\), \(1\le i\le M\), be probability laws whose
moments agree through order \(m\), and put
\[
 \mu_{i,t}=(1-t)\mu_i+t\gamma_i,
 \qquad \lambda_t=\bigotimes_{i=1}^M\mu_{i,t},
 \qquad A(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^M}F(z)\,\lambda_t(\,\mathrm d z),
\]
where \(F:\mathbb R^M\to(0,\infty)\) is \(C^{m+1}\).  Let
\(Z\sim\lambda_t\), \(X_i\sim\mu_i\), and \(Y_i\sim\gamma_i\) be
independent.  Assume \(0<A(t)<\infty\) on \([0,1]\), that the
expressions below are absolutely integrable, and that differentiation
under the finite product measure is justified.  Set
\(\Delta_i^X=X_i-Z_i\) and \(\Delta_i^Y=Y_i-Z_i\).  If, uniformly in
\(t\in[0,1]\),
\begin{align}
 &\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbb E\left[
  \left\lvert\Delta_i^X\right\rvert^{m+1}
  \int_0^1(1-s)^m
  \abs{\partial_i^{m+1}F(Z+s\Delta_i^Xe_i)}\,\mathrm d s\right]
 \le R A(t),\\
 &\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbb E\left[
  \left\lvert\Delta_i^Y\right\rvert^{m+1}
  \int_0^1(1-s)^m
  \abs{\partial_i^{m+1}F(Z+s\Delta_i^Ye_i)}\,\mathrm d s\right]
 \le R A(t),
\end{align}
then
\begin{equation}
 \left\lvert\log A(1)-\log A(0)\right\rvert\le \frac{2R}{m!}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:51:26.589301+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb7cc8fd1114c41bfc16383467dd69f2f04c77f37babab12ced15ff799e959af","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:SaS-measure of arXiv:2606.02003, 'Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion:\\ Definition and Fundamental Properties'] Let $(E,\mathcal{E})$ be a measurable space with $\sigma$-finite measure $m$.
Set $\mathcal{E}_0 := \{A \in \mathcal{E} : m(A) < \infty\}$.
A mapping $M_\alpha : \mathcal{E}_0 \to L^0(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$
is a \emph{S$\alpha$S random measure with control measure $m$} if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every $A \in \mathcal{E}_0$:
  $M_\alpha(A) \sim \mathrm{S}\alpha\mathrm{S}(m(A)^{1/\alpha})$, i.e.,
  \begin{equation}
  
  \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{i\theta M_\alpha(A)}\bigr]
  = e^{-|\theta|^\alpha m(A)},
  \quad \theta \in \mathbb{R}.
  \end{equation}
\item For pairwise disjoint $A_1, A_2, \ldots \in \mathcal{E}_0$,
  the variables $M_\alpha(A_1), M_\alpha(A_2), \ldots$ are independent.
\item For pairwise disjoint $\{A_j\} \subset \mathcal{E}_0$ with
  $\bigcup_j A_j \in \mathcal{E}_0$:
  $M_\alpha\!\left(\bigcup_j A_j\right) = \sum_j M_\alpha(A_j)$
  almost surely.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:55.644464+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb857d1dad3494a3cf99dabc2cda5ddc7e0cc4e2b95cf9ad1e32505945ce3e4d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 19 (Wasserstein-1 distance) of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] Let $(\Omega, d)$ be a Polish metric space and let $\mu,\nu$ be two probability measures on $\Omega$ with finite first moment.
The \emph{Wasserstein-1 distance} between $\mu$ and $\nu$ is
\[
    W_1(\mu,\nu)
    \;:=\;
    \inf_{\pi \in \Pi(\mu,\nu)}
    \int_{\Omega\times \Omega} d(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}\pi(x,y),
\]
where $\Pi(\mu,\nu)$ is the set of all couplings of $\mu$ and $\nu$,
i.e., all probability measures $\pi$ on $\Omega\times\Omega$
with marginals $\mu$ and $\nu$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:17:17.062061+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb874539e13deba5947fe6e95375e80c8e031e1c5d52cdef72f24b040655a49e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Consider the birth-death process with immigration introduced above and let
    $A_T=\int_0^T \de s \, X_s$.
For $0<\theta<a/(c-b)$, define $r_\theta=\sqrt{\frac{c\theta}{a+b\theta}}$ and $\beta_\theta
      =br_\theta+\frac{c}{r_\theta}-b-c$.
Moreover, let
\[
    v_\theta
      =\frac{2ac r_\theta^3}{(c-br_\theta^2)^3},
    \qquad
    I_{\mathrm{BDI}}(\theta)
      =\left(
          \sqrt{a+b\theta}-\sqrt{c\theta}
       \right)^2.
\]
Then, for every fixed $n\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
    \bbP_n(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim
    \frac{
      \psi_{\beta_\theta}(n)
      \langle\psi_{\beta_\theta},\mathbf 1\rangle_{\ell^2(\pi)}
    }{
      \beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}
    }
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_{\mathrm{BDI}}(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\]
On every fixed time interval, the conditioned process converges in total
variation to the birth-death process with rates
\[
    q^{(\theta)}(n,n+1)=r_\theta(a+bn),
    \qquad
    q^{(\theta)}(n,n-1)=\frac{c}{r_\theta}n.
\]
Its invariant law is negative binomial with shape parameter $a/b$ and
mean $\theta$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.667269+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_cb97ee9edeea22349ada59114228c7916782a63e40120b33671714dfc9e37161","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.04644, 'Khinchin's and Chung's Laws of the Iterated Logarithm at Time Zero for the Linear Stochast'] \cite[Theorem 2.4]{T1994}
